### SC-20 · P1 · ui — Worn painted avatars are clipped by their circle and sized inconsistently (fox ears, crane wings, lamp head, dragon tail cut; cat and lantern float small)

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** All 12 painted avatars drawn by the real KOS.governor.avatarNode(120) (the component used in the sidebar pill, Home ring, Seat and Avatar stage): Fox's ears and tassels are cut by the circle; Crane's wing tips cut left and right; Desk lamp's shade cut at top-left and the book at bottom-left; Dragon's tail and Owl's books cut at the sides; meanwhile Cat sits low with an empty top third, Lantern leaves dark bands left and right, and Koi / Moon rabbit are painted discs of their own that don't match the CSS disc (a dark crescent rim shows round Koi). The set looks like twelve different sizes. The art files are transparent cut-outs of varying aspect (lantern 417x640, cat 640x510, fox 546x640, bloom 532x640, others ~640x640, bbox touching every edge) and the CSS fits each one's full box to the square with object-fit: contain inside a border-radius:50% overflow:hidden disc, so anything in the art's corners falls outside the inscribed circle and narrow art leaves bands.
- **Evidence:** audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/shop-cosmetics/b3/avatar-montage.png, audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/shop-cosmetics/b3/avatar-row1-2x.png; image sizes via PIL (assets/app/img/app.avatar.*.webp); css/layout.css:250-251 (.k-avatar overflow hidden, .k-avatar-art object-fit: contain); js/core/governor.js:697-699
- **Root cause:** Art generated as rectangular cut-outs with content in the corners, displayed contain-fit in a circular clip.
- **Proposed fix:** Recompose the art for a circle: each avatar keyed to fit inside an inscribed circle of ~88% of a square canvas, on a consistent ground (either all full painted discs or all cut-outs on --s2), then keep object-fit: contain. Short of new art, pad the img (inline-size/block-size ~78%) so cut-out corners clear the circle, and a per-item focal/scale in the catalogue for outliers (cat, lantern).
- **Flags:** effort M, needs art (Gemini sheet)

### SC-21 · P1 · ui — Worn painted frames leave a dark empty band between the avatar and the ring (the ring's hole is ~75% of the art, the avatar is drawn at 66%)

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** On the real component (not just the shop preview reported earlier) every painted frame — Ice, Ember, Lacquer most visibly, Sakura, Wisteria and Koi too — shows a ring of bare background between the avatar and the painted band: at avatar 90px the art is drawn at 137px (152% + 2*--fo), but the art's transparent inner hole measures ~0.73-0.78 of the image (ice 239/320, ember 245/320, lacquer 239/320, gilt 248/319, amethyst 246/320) = ~103px, leaving ~6-7px of gap each side at 90px and ~13px at the Seat's 180px. Where an HP ring is present --fo adds the ring's frame-out, so the frame grows further and the gap widens. Wisteria and Koi holes are non-circular (wisteria L173/R193/T219/B237), so the avatar is visibly off-centre in them. This is exactly the user's 'avatar circle small inside a big ring'.
- **Evidence:** audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/shop-cosmetics/b3/frames-2x.png, audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/shop-cosmetics/b3/avatar-montage.png (bottom rows); hole radii measured with PIL on assets/app/img/app.frame.*.webp; css/layout.css:254 (152% fixed), :260-262 (--fo)
- **Root cause:** A single fixed 152% scale assumed a 66% hole; the imported art's holes are 73-78% and some are off-centre.
- **Proposed fix:** Store each frame's measured hole ratio and centre offset in the catalogue (e.g. hole:0.75, cx/cy) and size the art as avatarOuter / hole (≈133%, not 152%) positioned by its hole centre; let the art cover the HP ring instead of sitting outside it, or re-key the art so every hole is a centred circle of one fixed ratio.
- **Flags:** effort S

### SC-19 · P2 · ux — Two sources of truth for the Focus scene / Shrine hall / banner: the shop's 'Use' says 'In use' while the picture drawer's rule silently wins

- **Detail / repro:** The shop and Wardrobe wear a scene with g.scene (KOS.governor.wear), while the picture drawer (KOS.artSlot) stores state.artSlots.focus = {mode, pick, ...}. Once the drawer has ever been used, KOS.art.pick('focus') returns the drawer's rule and ignores g.scene. Reproduced: drawer 'One picture' -> The library, then shop/Wardrobe 'Use' The night train: g.scene = scene-train and the shop card reads '✓ In use', but KOS.art.pick('focus') = app.focus.library and explain = 'Now: The library, always.' Nothing in the shop or Wardrobe says a rule is overriding the choice. Also, with no drawer rule yet, the drawer opens on 'One picture' with no thumbnail selected and says 'Now: First snow, by the season' although nothing rotates (explain() falls through to the season wording).
- **Evidence:** eval after clicking the library thumb in KOS.artSlot.open('focus') then KOS.governor.wear('scene','scene-train'): {cfg:{mode:'one',pick:'app.focus.library'}, worn:'scene-train', pick:'app.focus.library'}; /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/shop-cosmetics/seed-drawer-focus.png; js/core/art.js:118-126 (rotated: cfg wins), 168 (fallback to G.scene only without cfg), 143-152 (explain); js/modules/governor-ui.js wareActive/wareUse
- **Root cause:** Rotation rule added beside the existing worn-item field instead of replacing it
- **Proposed fix:** Make one record: 'Use' in the shop/Wardrobe should write the drawer rule ({mode:'one', pick: art}) or clear it, and the drawer's One picture should mark/write g.scene; the drawer's initial state should select the worn item and explain should say 'always' for the implicit one-picture state.
- **Flags:** effort S

### SC-22 · P2 · ui — Ten of the 23 paid shop themes are near-copies of free Graphite (same near-black ground, accent within dE 2-6 of Graphite's crimson)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Measured every theme's resolved --crimson and --bg (OKLab distance x100 vs Graphite; ~2 is a just-noticeable difference, <6 is 'the same colour' at a glance). Accent: moss-garden 1.9, rosarium 2.3, spectral-rose 3.3, azure-corset-noir 3.8, ember-wraith 4.1, scarlet-garden-night 4.2, porcelain-sky-night 5.0, crimson-moth 5.4, lycoris-radiata 5.5, first-snow 6.0. Ground: every dark theme sits within dE 1.5-4.6 of Graphite's #0D0E12 and every theme keeps s1-vs-bg contrast ~1.06, so cards, rail and header read identically. In the 29-theme contact sheet the only visible difference between these ten and the free default is a slightly different hero tint. The user pays 140-1,500 gold for what looks like Graphite. Recommendation: KEEP the distinct ones (Atelier Dawn, Washi Morning, Verdigris Duel, Clinic Noir, Midnight Lilies, Celestial Duality, Azure Butterfly, Solar Manuscript, Violet Requiem, Rain Cafe, Sakura Skyline, Lantern Hall, Gothic Camellia, Shattered Bloom); REMOVE or re-tint (give a real ground hue/lightness and an accent away from crimson) moss-garden, rosarium, spectral-rose, azure-corset-noir, ember-wraith, scarlet-garden-night, porcelain-sky-night, crimson-moth, lycoris-radiata, first-snow (an owned copy keeps working, as the retired CSS banners do).

- **Root cause:** themes.css overrides only the role colours but every dark theme copies Graphite's ground lightness/chroma and most red/pink themes pick an accent hue within ~10 degrees of Graphite's.
- **Proposed fix:** Retire the ten (catalogue flag like retired banners, governor.js:529) or redesign each with a distinct ground (lightness 0.18-0.24 and real chroma, not 0.15/0.04) and an accent hue at least ~15 dE from Graphite.

### SC-25 · P2 · bug — Switching between two painted avatars loses your own photo: taking the second off falls back to the default seal, not your picture

### SC-26 · P2 · ux — One click on a card's Buy spends up to 12,000 gold with no confirmation and no undo, and silently re-dresses the app

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The shop card's 'Buy' button (shop.buy) calls buyWare directly: KOS.governor.buy then wareUse(it,true). There is no confirm step, no Undo on the toast, and no refund path, for prices up to 10,000 (Gala) and 12,000 (Every area). Buying also immediately applies the item: a theme re-themes the whole app, a frame replaces the worn frame, an avatar replaces your photo (see the prevKind finding), a scene/hall replaces the current one — none of which the user asked for at purchase time. The preview sheet shows '12,476 → …' but the card button skips the sheet. Months of earned gold can be lost to a mis-tap on iPad/iPhone where cards are dense.
- **Evidence:** js/modules/governor-ui.js:1045-1046 (card Buy -> buyWare), :893-903 (buy + wareUse + toast, no undo); js/core/governor.js:542-556 (buy has no inverse)
- **Root cause:** buyWare couples purchase and equip, no reversible step.
- **Proposed fix:** Route the card's Buy through the preview sheet (or KOS.ui.confirm) showing price and balance after, and offer 'Undo' on the toast for ~10 s (refund + remove from owned, restore what was worn). Ask 'Use it now?' instead of auto-applying, or apply only kinds with nothing currently worn.
- **Flags:** effort S

### SC-31 · P2 · bug — Picture drawer 'Rotate by season / time of day' ignores what the pictures are: First snow never shows in winter, the rooftop and First snow never show at all, the night train shows at 2 pm

- **Detail / repro:** KOS.art.rotated indexes the owned pool by position: season -> SEASONS.indexOf(season) % n, time of day -> 0..3 % n. With all six Focus scenes owned: Jan->library, Apr->train, Jul->shrine, Oct->cafe; 08h library, 14h night train, 19h shrine, 23h cafe. Scenes 5 and 6 (rooftop, First snow, 3,600 gold) are unreachable by either period, and the mapping is arbitrary (a 'night' scene by day, snow never in winter). Same for Shrine halls (Jan lantern, Jul gold). Also in 'By condition' mode the drawer hides the period control and says 'Otherwise the season decides', but the fallback uses whatever period was set before (eval: explain -> 'Now: The night train, by the day').
- **Evidence:** eval: setCfg('focus',{mode:'rotate',period:'season'}) rotated for 15 Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct -> library/train/shrine/cafe; period 'tod' 8/14/19/23h -> library/train/shrine/cafe; condition mode with period 'day' -> 'by the day'; js/core/art.js:131-137 (index by position), js/modules/artslot.js:65 (period hidden in condition mode) and :73 ('Otherwise the season decides')
- **Root cause:** Rotation treats the pool as an anonymous list; only Home's four seasonal heroes happen to line up with SEASONS order.
- **Proposed fix:** Give each scene/hall catalogue item its own season and time-of-day tags (snow: winter + evening, rooftop/train: night, library: afternoon...) and rotate among the owned pictures that match, falling back to all; set period 'season' when switching to condition mode (or show the period there).
- **Flags:** effort M

### SC-32 · P2 · bug — Edit your seat > Background offers '+ Upload an image' with 0 gold and no unlock, bypassing the 3,000-gold 'Profile banner' unlock (invariant 2)

- **Detail / repro:** On an empty account (gold 0, owns('upload-banner') false, KOS.art.canUpload('banner') false) #/governor/edit > Background shows the upload tile. It calls KOS.governor.setCustomBanner(file), which prepares the file and opens bannerCropper with the picture already loaded; allowUpload:false there only hides the cropper's own upload button, so saving sets g.bannerImg (the profile banner the shop sells as 'Upload your own profile banner'). The Avatar & profile page and the picture drawer DO gate the same thing, so the shop item is pointless and the rules disagree. There are also two separate 'own banner' stores: g.bannerImg (synced state) from this path and art.own.banner (media kv, device-only) from the drawer's 'Your own' mode.

- **Root cause:** The unlock was added to the drawer and the banner cropper's own button, not to the older Edit-seat upload path that feeds the same banner.
- **Proposed fix:** Gate the tile on KOS.art.canUpload('banner') (show the lock with 'Open in the shop' otherwise, as the drawer does) and make the drawer's 'Your own' banner and g.bannerImg one store.
- **Flags:** effort S

### SC-34 · P2 · ux — Exam and Sketch pen sets barely differ from the default, label their swatches wrongly, and silently recolour every stroke already written

- **Detail / repro:** Resolved ink palette (Graphite) per pen set: default accent rgb(234,105,114), teal (65,193,186). Exam set ('Black pen, red pen and pencil'): accent (232,95,97) - visually the same red - and teal -> grey (131,134,142); ink stays the theme's near-white. Sketch set ('Graphite, wash and highlight'): ink (180,183,190), accent -> bloom (230,169,197) which is identical to the bloom highlighter, teal -> (235,197,115) a near-twin of the amber swatch (230,181,93). The swatches keep their role names, so the gold swatch is announced and titled 'Teal' and the pink one 'Accent'. Because strokes store a ROLE and the palette is read live (invariant 133), wearing a pen set repaints every existing page in every notebook (all teal working turns grey under Exam set) - and 'Take off' changes it back - which a shop description never warns about.
- **Evidence:** eval KOS.inkUI.palette(host) after KOS.governor.wear('penset', id): default/study identical; exam {accent:'rgb(232,95,97)',teal:'rgb(131,134,142)'}; sketch {ink:'rgb(180,183,190)',accent:'rgb(230,169,197)',teal:'rgb(235,197,115)',amber:'rgb(230,181,93)',bloom:'rgb(230,169,197)'}; css/views/ink.css:37-42; js/core/inkui.js:1265-1266 (aria-label/title from PEN_ROLES names); js/core/ink.js:56 (PEN_ROLES)
- **Root cause:** Pen sets were implemented as CSS remaps of the shared roles on :root rather than as new roles.
- **Proposed fix:** Give each set distinct colours and its own swatch names (Pen/Red pen/Pencil; Graphite/Wash/Highlight) and apply the set to NEW strokes only (store the resolved set on the stroke, or have the set add roles rather than remap existing ones).
- **Flags:** effort M

## ST — Study desks (CS/Maths/IT), topic page, Review, Assignments (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** Study-core on kos-redraw-1: all 24 earlier findings still reproduce. The inventory-driven behaviour checks found 19 new problems, two serious: deleting an assignment permanently deletes every file linked to it, including a topic's own files (removeAttachments treats every listed file as owned; P0), and the IT desk wipes a saved unit mark when an out-of-range number is typed and Enter is pressed (invalid input is treated as 'emptied'; P1). The other systemic root causes: study evidence is logged only on full completion and without context (unfinished flashcard batches log nothing; Due today runs are logged with no subject/topic and no duration, so subject streaks, topic sessions and 'Time' miss the user's main daily study); read helpers that write (quiz qstats creates a record on render); per-view state not remembered (notes page, assignment selection has no URL, tab strip scroll); and stats computed from raw counts or stale renders (Quiz best %, inspector not refreshing under the held redraw). ### ST-25 · P0 · data — Deleting an assignment permanently deletes every file linked to it, including files that belong to a topic or another record

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.assignments.remove -> removeAttachments() lists the files for ref "assignment:<id>" in every subject and calls KOS.attach.remove() on each. KOS.attach.list() returns not only files whose home is the assignment but every file whose links index holds the assignment (anything attached there with "Attach to…", or a topic file linked to the assignment). remove() deletes the whole record and its blob and records a cloud tombstone, so the file also disappears from its topic (and from other devices). Invariant 150: "Remove" from one place removes the link; the file is deleted only when nothing else links it, after a confirm. The Delete confirm only says "its calendar entry, countdown and Home card" go with it; files are not mentioned.
- **Evidence:** eval fixture (seeded account): KOS.attach.add("compsci","4.2.3.1", file, …, {links:[{kind:"assignment",id:"29"}]}); topic list before: ["topic-notes.txt|[]", "topic-notes.txt|[{kind:assignment,id:29}]"]; KOS.assignments.remove(29); topic list after: ["topic-notes.txt"] (the linked file is gone from the topic). js/core/assignments.js:203-208, :220-231; js/modules/attachments.js:275-292 (list includes the links index), :392-411 (remove deletes and tombstones); js/modules/assignments.js:454-457 (confirm text).
- **Root cause:** Assignment deletion predates the many-links file index (R1) and still treats every listed file as owned.
- **Proposed fix:** In removeAttachments, for each file use the Files detach rule: removeLink(fileId, {kind:"assignment", id}) when the file has another link (topic home or other links), and delete only files whose sole link is the assignment; list those in the confirm body.
- **Flags:** effort S

### ST-03 · P1 · bug — 'Quiz best' shows a raw count as a percentage: 6 of 11 right reads 'Quiz best 6%'

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The quiz engine stores a topic's best as the number of correct answers (st.best = correct), but the topic inspector and the subject desk's 'Quiz best' tile print it through pctText as a percent. Reproduced on a fresh topic (#/ref/compsci/4.2.2.1): 6/11 (lastPct 55) is stored best 6 and the inspector shows 'Quiz best 6%'. The subject tile then takes the max of counts across topics of different lengths. The seeded account has percentages in best (57), so the quiz header reads 'best 57/10'. Either way one surface is wrong for every learner.
- **Evidence:** eval: state.study.quiz['compsci:4.2.2.1'] = {attempts:1, best:6, lastPct:55}; inspector text 'Quiz best\n6%'; quiz head 'score 0 · best 6/11'. js/engines/quiz.js:159 (best = correct count), :77 (prints best + '/' + items.length); js/modules/hub.js:3224 and :2200 pctText(best); hub.js:126 max over topics. | Recheck 6 Nov (kos-redraw-1, slot 5): Fixture on the empty account: 5 of 11 right -> state.study.quiz {attempts:1,best:5,lastPct:45}; CS desk analytics 'Quiz best | 5% | 1 attempt across 1 topic'. The subject desk tile has the same bug (js/modules/hub.js:119-129 max of raw counts, :2200 pctText + bar pct = count), not only the inspector (hub.js:3224) and js/engines/quiz.js:159.
- **Root cause:** two readers disagree on the unit of study.quiz[k].best
- **Proposed fix:** Store best as a percent (bestPct) in the quiz engine, migrate existing records once at the store gate (best/len where the deck length is known, else keep), and print '/n' only from a stored count; or keep the count and make hub.js divide by the topic's quiz length. Add a smoke check that the inspector and the quiz header agree.
- **Flags:** effort S

### ST-04 · P1 · bug — Cards reviewed in an unfinished flashcard batch are never logged: no streak, no pay, 'Today so far · Reviewed 0'

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The flashcard engine logs its session (and so the Governor's XP/gold/HP, the study streak and every ledger reader) only when the WHOLE batch is finished. Due today opens 'Start review · all 308'; rating 7 cards and leaving (or rating 100 of 308) writes FSRS schedules and review-log rows but adds nothing to the ledger: Review's 'Today so far' still says Reviewed 0, Card stats' Reviews per day and Rating mix stay at zero, the day does not count for the streak (invariant 4) and nothing is paid. With a real backlog the user is punished for doing most of the work.
- **Evidence:** eval: on #/due rated 5 cards Good, navigated to #/review: 0 new sessions, 'Today so far Reviewed 0 Accuracy —', dueCount 308 -> 303. js/engines/flashcards.js:325-353 (sessions.log only in finish()); js/modules/due.js:222-230 and js/modules/cardstats.js:218-228 read only those session entries. shots/study-core/q-cardstats-mac.png (Total reviews 5,810 beside an empty Reviews per day and an all-zero Rating mix). | Recheck 6 Nov (kos-redraw-1, slot 5): Empty account fixture: 3 cards rated Good on #/ref/compsci/4.2.2.1 then left: state.srs 3 keys, sessions 0 before and after leaving; only a full 16-card batch logged one flashcards entry (31 XP). Same in a Due today run left after an Again (leech fixture). js/engines/flashcards.js:325-355 logs only in finish().
- **Root cause:** session logged only in finish(); review surfaces read session metrics rather than the review log
- **Proposed fix:** Log the batch when the view is left or hidden (the page-hide / KOS.show teardown the engine already notes at :373), paying for the cards rated so far, once (a session id held by the engine and updated, never logged twice); or cap a due batch at a size people finish (e.g. 20-50 with 'Next 50'). Read 'Reviewed today' and Reviews per day from KOS.reviewLog (one row per rating) instead of session metrics.
- **Flags:** effort M

### ST-26 · P1 · data — IT desk: an out-of-range mark typed over a saved one (e.g. 459 for 45) and Enter silently erases the unit's result

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Editing a Done unit's mark, an invalid number (above the max, negative) only turns the input red and sets editing.value to "". save() treats an empty value on a Done unit as "emptied the mark" and calls KOS.itUnits.clearResult(): pressing Enter or ✓ Save after a typo wipes the stored raw/UMS and flips the unit to "Sitting · date not set". No message, no confirm, no undo; the aggregate and the predicted qualification grade change with it (and it syncs).
- **Evidence:** eval #/subject/it: F200 {status:done, raw:45} row "F200 … | Done | ≈45 / 60 | Merit"; edit, type 459 (input data-state bad), Enter -> KOS.itUnits.get("F200") {status:"sitting", raw:null, ums:null}; row "Sitting · date not set | + Enter mark | —"; no toast. js/modules/itdesk.js:221-225 (invalid -> value ""), :277-282 (empty on a done unit -> clearResult).
- **Proposed fix:** Distinguish an emptied field (inp.value === "") from an invalid one: on invalid, keep editing, focus the field and say "Enter 0–60"; clearing a result should ask (or offer Undo).
- **Flags:** effort S

Duplicated per-space rules: css/views/code.css:162-163, css/views/japanese.css:82,172, css/views/mind.css:103-104, css/views/creatives.css:26-27 (identical grid-template-rows/path padding/border written four times); css/views/study.css:54-55 makes the side column follow the hero. | Recheck 6 Nov (kos-redraw-1, slot 5): Re-measured (hero5.js): mac CS/Maths/IT 189, Code 292, Mind 296, Japanese 339, Creatives 341; iPad CS 347, Maths/IT 297, Code 459, Mind 482, Ja 507, Cr 509; iPhone CS 255, Maths/IT 205, Cr 309, Code 379, Mind 402, Ja 438 — identical to the first audit.

### ST-27 · P2 · bug — Opening a topic's Quiz tab writes a quiz record, and the subject desk then reports "Quiz best 0% · 0 attempts across 1 topic"

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** qstats() in the quiz engine creates state.study.quiz[sid:ref] = {attempts:0,best:0,lastPct:0} as a side effect of READING it, and the quiz renders call it on mount. Merely opening the Quiz tab (no answer given) therefore writes synced state (a render that writes), and subjectQuizStats() counts that record: the CS desk Subject analytics tile changes from "Quiz best — · no quiz attempts yet" to "Quiz best 0% · 0 attempts across 1 topic". Same for the inspector (Quiz best 0%). The bar is also driven by the raw count (pct: quiz.best), see the Quiz best % finding.
- **Evidence:** eval (empty account): state.study.quiz before {} ; after clicking [data-tab=quiz] on #/ref/compsci/4.2.2.1 {"compsci:4.2.2.1":{attempts:0,best:0,lastPct:0}}; #/subject/compsci analytics tile text "Quiz best | 0% | 0 attempts across 1 topic". js/engines/quiz.js:16-21 (q[k] = q[k] || {...}), :58; js/modules/hub.js:119-129, :2200-2203.
- **Root cause:** Read helper doubles as initialiser.
- **Proposed fix:** Make qstats a pure read (return a default without assigning) and create the record only in finish(); subjectQuizStats should skip records with attempts 0.
- **Flags:** effort S

### ST-20 · P3 · bug — Streak milestone note repeats '36-day streak' once per milestone, and missing milestone records pay every past milestone at once

The note text uses the current streak (stk) instead of the milestone (ms). The retro-payment happens whenever g.milestones lacks the run's dates (seen on the seeded account; also possible after the ledger's 2,000-entry cap shortens the computed streak, which moves the run's start date and re-pays every milestone).

## SY — Background redraws / cloud sync disrupting work (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** On kos-redraw-1 the stopgap does what it promised for the reported cases: a background redraw (cloud pull, habit auto-tick, Daily Review close, boot loads) is held on task pages, while typing, under a dialog or menu and within 45 s of a touch, so the flashcard position, notes page, quiz, Japanese session, ink panes, menus and dialogs survive (8 of the 17 earlier findings no longer reproduce under background redraws; 7 changed, 2 hold). But holding the repaint without reconciling the data introduced a P0: the study editor on a held topic page keeps its pre-pull rows and its next autosave writes them back wholesale, so material another device added is deleted locally and the three-way merge then deletes it everywhere. Outside the task list the remount still loses state: vault scroll (lazy batches make the restore clamp to 0, iPad and iPhone), the unsaved Edit-your-seat draft, horizontal strips and in-page tabs, and unsent text in a blurred field; plain KOS.rerender() calls from timers and async callbacks (Exams planner, Connections, Mind) bypass the hold and redraw whatever page is current; the achievement unlock overlay is modal over a flashcard set; and task pages now go stale with no indicator. Root cause throughout: one global remount-everything redraw with no notion of what changed, which page asked, or where a view keeps its transient state; the fix is a redraw policy that diffs, scopes and reconciles (see the systemic design in the findings).

**Coverage.** Build kos-redraw-1 (sw), harness slot 6, seeded account (and an empty-files state for Files). Inventory: findings/sync-disruption.inventory.md — 27 redraw triggers (A1-A27) and 21 state surfaces (B). Matrix: A1-A4 cloud pulls -> behaviour checked on 40 non-task routes (r5, ipad) + task pages (r1, r3, r9; ipad) + iPhone Home/anime -> new vault-scroll, strips, tabs, seat-draft, unsent-input findings; held pages -> stale-data finding; editor -> P0 (r11). A5 habit auto-tick -> code-read, carried #12 changed. A6 Review close -> rerun, carried changed. A7 auto-open -> code-read only (no slot due in the harness) -> carried holds. A8/A9 boot -> code-read, carried changed. A10 -> OK code-read. A11 unlock overlay -> reproduced r10 + screenshot -> new P2. A12-A14 unscoped plain rerenders -> code-read + effect reproduced (r1 np3) -> new P2. A15/A16 -> OK code-read. A17 Files repaint -> r13 -> new P3. A18/A19/A20 -> OK (A20 rerun r8a). A21-A23 no-redraw pulls -> code-read -> carried #17 widened. A24 HUD -> OK. A25 OAuth return navigation -> code-read, not filed (expected after a sign-in return). A26 toasts -> sd10 rerun iphone -> holds. A27 -> intended. Surfaces B: all exercised as listed in the inventory. Devices: iPad portrait for most, iPad landscape for Side by side, iPhone for scroll and toast; Mac not re-run separately (same code path, no layout dependence). NOT checked: real two-device Supabase traffic (simulated with store.replaceState + KOS.rerender({background})); Daily Review auto-open live; Shop Try on under a redraw; Exam Room / paper viewer under a redraw (task view, mechanism verified); Dawn/shop themes (not relevant to redraw behaviour).

### SY-18 · P0 · data — With the redraw held, an open study editor writes its stale copy over material another device added — the pulled card is deleted locally and the three-way merge then deletes it everywhere

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Review note (8 Nov):** The hold for an open editor while typing predates kos-redraw-1; the stopgap made it indefinite on ref views, widening (not creating) the defect.
- **Devices:** iPad + Mac (two devices editing the same topic's material)
- **Detail / repro:** The study editor (KOS.editor.mount) keeps the fork's rows in memory (flashcards, quiz, exam, notes, spec) and every autosave writes the WHOLE array through KOS.edits.set. Before kos-redraw-1 a cloud pull remounted the editor from the fresh fork; now the topic page ('ref') is a TASK_VIEW, so the redraw is held until navigation and the editor keeps its pre-pull copy indefinitely (state.ui.editing also keeps the editor open per device across visits). Reproduced: editor open on 4.5.4.3 flashcards (15 rows), a pull brings device B's new card (state 16 rows, hasB true), the held editor still shows 15; one more keystroke and the autosave writes 15 rows back (final 15, hasB false). The next push sends a document whose fork lacks a row that the base has, which the merge reads as a local deletion — and a deletion on either side wins (invariant 33/88) — so the other device's card is removed on every device. The same applies to notes blocks and spec blocks, quiz and exam items.
- **Evidence:** eval r11.js (ipad): {forkN:15, afterPull:16, hasB:true, editorRows:15, final:15, hasBFinal:false}. js/modules/editor.js:408-414 (cards = KOS.edits.material(...) captured; save() sets the whole array), :470, :567, :650, :656; js/core/edits.js:199-206 (set replaces the kind wholesale); js/core/ui.js:358-359 (ref held); js/core/cloudsync.js:768-775 (pull replaces state, rerender held).
- **Root cause:** The stopgap holds the repaint without telling long-lived in-page editors that their source changed; the editor's whole-array save model turns a stale copy into deletions.
- **Proposed fix:** Short term: let a held background redraw notify mounted editors (an event with the changed paths); the study editor re-reads its fork when idle and merges by row id instead of writing the stale array (or saves per-row patches: KOS.edits.patchRow / addRow / removeRow). Never hold a redraw over an editor whose source record changed without that reconciliation. Add a smoke test: editor open, remote fork change, local keystroke, remote row survives.
- **Flags:** effort M

### SY-01 · P1 · bug — KOS.rerender() never keeps the scroll position: it saves #main.scrollTop but #stage is the scroller, so every cloud pull jumps the page to the top

- **RESOLVED:** resolved by the stopgap kos-redraw-1 (Gemini B partially-confirmed it; Claude's review 8 Nov, gemini/CLAUDE_REVIEW.md §3): scrollers() keeps #stage's scroll everywhere measured except the lazily batched Collection vaults, which are SY-19.
- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** changed: KOS.rerender now saves and restores #stage, #main and the document scroller (ui.js:376-378, 399-404); re-measured 40 routes on ipad (r5-ipad.json) and Home on iphone (900 -> 900): kept everywhere EXCEPT lazily batched vaults (anime 3414->0, books 29226->0, vn, game, mangaka; iphone anime 2500->0) — see the new vault finding
- **Independent check:** partially-confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all (mac, ipad, iphone)
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.rerender (the cloud-pull/background redraw path) reads and restores document.getElementById('main').scrollTop, but the element that actually scrolls is #stage (#main has overflow visible; on the iPad #main.scrollHeight 2406 vs #stage 2406/1120 scrolling). KOS.show then empties #main, the height collapses and the browser clamps #stage.scrollTop to 0. Repro (seeded account): open compsci 4.5.2.1, set #stage.scrollTop=900, KOS.rerender() -> 0. Same on Home (700 -> 0) and the Anime vault (1500 -> 0) at mac, ipad and iphone sizes. So any pull, merge, auto-ticked habit, Daily Review close etc. throws the reader back to the top of the page.
- **Evidence:** harness eval sd3.js: ipad {st1:900,st2:0,h1:700,h2:0,a1:1500,a2:0}; mac {st1:530,st2:0,...}; iphone same. Code: js/core/ui.js:353-356 (var main=getElementById('main'); var top=main.scrollTop; ... main.scrollTop=top); KOS.show resets main.scrollTop=0 at js/core/ui.js:1526
- **Root cause:** rerender measured the wrong element after the shell moved scrolling to #stage
- **Proposed fix:** Save/restore the real scroller (#stage, or a KOS.shell.scroller() helper that returns the element whose overflow scrolls, including the phone shell) and restore AFTER the view has rendered (and once more after async content lands, e.g. on next rAF / after vault lazy batch). Better: part of the redraw policy below — background redraws should not happen while the user is reading.
- **Flags:** effort S

### SY-02 · P1 · bug — CS/Maths/IT notes reset to page 1 on every background redraw (the reported 'notes page 4 jumps back to page 1')

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** no longer reproduces for background redraws: eval r1.js (ipad) {np0:'Page 4 of 7', held:true, np1:'Page 4 of 7' (hard), np2:'Page 4 of 7' (soft)}; a plain KOS.rerender() still resets it (np3:'Page 1 of 7'), so any unscoped plain caller (examviews.js:264, connections.js:70) still can
- **Independent check:** partially-confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Review note (8 Nov):** Since the stopgap only plain KOS.rerender() stragglers (e.g. connections.js:70, examviews.js:265 timers firing after leaving) can reset the notes page; propose P2 in the plan.
- **Devices:** all; most visible on iPad
- **Detail / repro:** In a subject topic the current note page lives in a closure variable (`var notePage = 0` inside the topic view). KOS.rerender re-runs the view, so the variable is recreated at 0. hub.js keeps only the open TAB across a redraw (openTabMemo), not the page. Repro on iPad: open compsci 4.5.2.1, Next page x3 -> 'Page 4 of 7', KOS.rerender() -> 'Page 1 of 7'. Code, Japanese, Mind and Creatives lessons do NOT have this bug because they store the page in state.ui.<space>.page[ref].
- **Evidence:** harness eval: {before:'Page 4 of 7', after:'Page 1 of 7'} at --size ipad. js/modules/hub.js:2901 (var notePage = 0), :2983 (cur = o.keep ? notePage : 0), :2590 (only the tab survives KOS.ui.redrawing). Contrast js/modules/codetopic.js:342/377, jatopic.js:206/229, crtopic.js:154/171, mindtopic.js:261/282 (ui.page[ref])
- **Root cause:** transient reader state held in a view-render closure
- **Proposed fix:** Keep the note page in a module-level memo keyed by sid:ref (like openTabMemo) or per device in state.ui.notePage[sid:ref], and read it when KOS.ui.redrawing (and arguably on return to the topic). Same pattern the study spaces already use.
- **Flags:** effort S

### SY-03 · P1 · bug — A background redraw mid-flashcards restarts the set at card 1 and silently drops the cards already rated from the session ledger (no XP, no streak credit)

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** no longer reproduces for background redraws: eval r9.js (ipad) — after three ratings the set text is identical before and after KOS.rerender({background:'hard'}) ('QUESTION · 12'); ref is a TASK_VIEW (ui.js:358-359). Still reachable through a plain unscoped rerender
- **Independent check:** partially-confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Review note (8 Nov):** Since the stopgap background redraws are held on the review views; what remains is plain rerenders and finish()-only logging (root cause 18); propose P2 in the plan.
- **Devices:** all; reported on iPad
- **Detail / repro:** The flashcard engine keeps queue, graduated and counts in its mount closure, and only logs the review session in finish(). A KOS.rerender mid-set remounts it: on a topic's Flashcards tab the queue is rebuilt from ALL the topic's cards, so the learner is put back on card 1 and re-meets cards they just rated (re-rating them applies FSRS's short-term rule again, skewing their schedule); on Due today the counts reset ('This session: 0 again · 0 hard · 3 good' -> ''), and because a session is only logged at finish(), the ratings made before the redraw never produce a session entry — their XP/gold and the study-streak credit are lost (the SRS schedule itself was saved). Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.2.1 Flashcards, rate 3 Good ('15 left of 18'), KOS.rerender() -> '18 left of 18', first card again. Due today: rate 3 ('304 left of 307', life line 3 good) -> after rerender '304 left of 304', life line empty.
- **Evidence:** harness eval (ipad): topic log ['18 left of 18 What is a number base?', ..., '15 left of 18'] -> afterFront '18 left of 18 What is a number base?'; due {d3life:'This session: 0 again · 0 hard · 3 good · 0 easy', dAfterLife:''}. js/engines/flashcards.js:295-322 (rate keeps counts in closure, store.save only), :325-355 (finish is the only KOS.sessions.log), :356 restart
- **Root cause:** session progress and the pay-at-finish rule live in DOM-bound closures
- **Proposed fix:** (1) Never redraw under an active study session (redraw policy below). (2) Keep an in-progress review session in a per-device session store (state.ui.fcSession[deckKey] = {queue keys, graduated, counts, startedAt}) and resume it on remount. (3) Log/bank the partial batch on unmount/pagehide (like Focus banks its clock, invariant 4c) so pay never depends on the DOM surviving.
- **Flags:** effort M

### SY-04 · P1 · bug — Quiz progress and a typed exam answer are wiped by any background redraw

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** no longer reproduces for background redraws: eval r3.js {quiz0:'Question 3 of 11', quiz1:'Question 3 of 11'}; a plain rerender still resets (quizUser:'Question 1 of 11')
- **Independent check:** partially-confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Review note (8 Nov):** Since the stopgap ref/exams are held as TASK_VIEWS and typing() holds too; only plain rerenders reset the quiz/exam; propose P2 in the plan.
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Topic Quiz (MCQ) and Exam tabs keep the question index, chosen answers and typed text in engine closures. Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.2.1 Quiz, answer two -> 'Question 3 of 11'; KOS.rerender() -> 'Question 1 of 11' (tab kept, progress lost). Exam tab: go to 'Question 3 of 14', type into the answer textarea, KOS.rerender() -> 'Question 1 of 14' and the textarea is empty: the typed answer is lost with no recovery.
- **Evidence:** harness eval sd1.js (ipad): {quizBefore:'Question 3 of 11', quizAfter:'Question 1 of 11', examBefore:'Question 3 of 14', examTA:true, examAfter:'Question 1 of 14', examTAAfter:''}. js/engines/quiz.js:62-121 (MCQ state in closure), :225-232 (exam 'at' index in closure); js/modules/hub.js:3044-3084 remounts them
- **Root cause:** engine state in closures + unconditional rerender
- **Proposed fix:** Persist the quiz/exam position and drafts per device (state.ui.quizRun[sid:ref] = {at, picks, drafts}) like Code drafts, and restore on remount; plus the redraw policy (no background redraw while a study engine is mounted and touched).
- **Flags:** effort M

### SY-05 · P1 · arch — Every cloud pull/merge redraws the active view unconditionally — even when nothing the view shows changed, and even while the user is mid-task

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** changed: rerenderCurrent now calls KOS.rerender({background:'hard'}) (cloudsync.js:731), held on TASK_VIEWS, while typing, under a dialog/menu and within 45 s of a touch (ui.js:349-392). Still no diff of what changed: every other page is remounted after 45 s idle (r5-ipad.json: redrawn:true on all 40 non-task routes), and task pages now go stale instead (new finding)
- **Independent check:** partially-confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** iPad primarily (app switching + Pencil study), all
- **Detail / repro:** cloudsync.rerenderCurrent() calls KOS.rerender() after every applied remote state: the clean path (applyRemoteState, cloudsync.js:775), the merge path (mergeRemoteIn, :495, also used by a push that lost its compare-and-set race, :533-560) and first link (:1279). There is no check of whether the merged document differs in anything the current view reads, no check that the user is interacting, a dialog/menu is open, an input has focus, or a study engine is running. The only guard in KOS.rerender is the ink pen (ui.js:347). Triggers that reach it: another device's push -> Realtime 'changed' (1.5 s debounce, :1483); returning to the app (visibilitychange/focus, :1548-1552, at most once a minute) — on the iPad every app switch; the 15-min interval; and the iPad's OWN ratings: each store.save -> noteChange -> push after 4 s -> if the Mac/iPhone pushed meanwhile the CAS fails -> conflict() -> mergeRemoteIn -> rerender. An idle open Mac pushes on its own (achievement sweep every 30 min, goals/notify ticks, routine auto-ticks, Daily Review words), so the iPad is redrawn under the user regularly. This is the root of the reported iPad resets.
- **Evidence:** js/core/cloudsync.js:487-497 (mergeRemoteIn -> rerenderCurrent), :723-733 (rerenderCurrent -> KOS.rerender), :773-777, :533-560 (conflict path), :1447-1459 (noteChange push), :1480-1495 (Realtime), :1541-1553 (interval/visible/focus); js/core/ui.js:344-357 (rerender: only inkUI.busy guard). Harness: KOS.rerender() reproduces every reset in the other findings.
- **Root cause:** full remount used as the generic refresh for background state changes, with no busy/changed gating
- **Proposed fix:** Systemic redraw policy: (1) cloudsync passes what changed (top-level keys that differ between pre- and post-merge state, cheap JSON compare per key) to KOS.rerender({changed:[...], background:true}); views declare the state keys they read (KOS.views.x.reads = ['srs','edits',...]) and are skipped when untouched. (2) A background redraw is DEFERRED while the page is 'busy': a dialog or menu open, focus in an input/textarea/contenteditable, a study engine mounted and touched in the last N minutes (flashcards/quiz/exam/japanese session/code task), pointer down, or within 30 s of the last interaction — instead show a quiet 'Updated on another device · Refresh' chip, and redraw on the next navigation. (3) For views that must refresh live, give them a refresh(changed) hook that patches in place instead of a full remount.
- **Flags:** effort L

### SY-08 · P1 · ux — A background redraw steals focus from whatever is being typed in — the iPad/iPhone keyboard closes mid-sentence

### SY-19 · P1 · bug — A background redraw of a Collection vault throws the reader back to the top: the lazy batches are rebuilt at 60 entries, so the saved scroll position cannot be restored

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** iPad, Mac, iPhone (any vault page)
- **Detail / repro:** Vault pages are not in TASK_VIEWS, so a cloud pull 45 s after the last touch (or any soft redraw: a habit ticking itself, the Daily Review closing, an own picture loading) remounts #/anime, #/books, #/vn, #/game or #/mangaka. KOS.rerender saves #stage.scrollTop and restores it twice (sync and next frame), but the remounted vault holds only its first lazy batch (60 cards), so the page is too short and the restore clamps to 0. Reproduced on the seeded account (ipad): anime 3414 -> 0, books 29226 -> 0, vn 504 -> 0, game 3414 -> 0, mangaka 6056 -> 0. Scrolling through 1,900 titles and losing the place on a pull is exactly the disruption the stopgap set out to stop.
- **Evidence:** audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/r5.js + r5-ipad.json (diff.top for #/anime, #/books, #/vn, #/game, #/mangaka). js/core/ui.js:399-404 (restore of tops[] only, sync + one rAF); js/core/ui.js:358-359 (TASK_VIEWS has no vault views); invariant 8 (60-entry lazy batches).
- **Root cause:** Scroll restoration assumes the remounted page is as tall as before; lazily batched lists are not, and the vault views are not held like task views.
- **Proposed fix:** Either add the vault views (anime, books, vn, game, mangaka, seasonal, wishlist, shrine) to the held set, or make the vault render keep its loaded batch count in a per-visit memo (like scrollMemo) so a redraw renders up to the batch that contained the scroll position before restoring; longer term the redraw policy should diff and skip a redraw when the vault's query result did not change.
- **Flags:** effort M

### SY-25 · P2 · bug — Delayed plain KOS.rerender() calls redraw whatever page is on screen by then — bypassing the background hold (Exams planner's 8 s flash, Connections' Sync now, Mind's journal-ready)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Several callbacks that fire seconds after the user acted call KOS.rerender() WITHOUT {background}, and without checking that their page is still on screen, so they remount whatever the user has moved on to — including task pages the stopgap protects: a flashcard set restarts at card 1, notes go back to page 1, a quiz to question 1 (KOS.rerender() with no opts is never held; r1.js shows a plain rerender on a topic resets 'Page 4 of 7' to 'Page 1 of 7'). Sites: the Exams planner's 'Sent · Undo' flash clears with setTimeout(KOS.rerender, 8100) (examviews.js:264); Connections' 'Sync now' re-renders when the provider sync resolves, which can take many seconds (connections.js:66-70); Mind's desk and pages re-render when the Journal store becomes ready, guarded only by main.isConnected — #main is always connected (mind.js:52 checks ui.view === 'subject', true on any desk; mind.js:217).
- **Evidence:** js/modules/examviews.js:264; js/modules/connections.js:66-70; js/modules/mind.js:52, :217; eval r1.js {np0:'Page 4 of 7', np3:'Page 1 of 7'} for the effect of a plain rerender on a topic.
- **Root cause:** KOS.rerender has no notion of 'the page that asked'; async callers re-render the global current view.
- **Proposed fix:** Give KOS.rerender a scope: KOS.rerender({ onlyIf: navKey }) (or a helper KOS.redrawIfStill(viewId, arg)), use it for every async/timer caller, and mark them background.
- **Flags:** effort S

### SY-26 · P2 · ux — Held task pages never catch up while the user stays on them: another device's progress stays invisible, with no sign that the page is out of date

- **Devices:** iPad + Mac
- **Detail / repro:** On a TASK_VIEW the stopgap holds a background redraw until navigation and sets no retry (ui.js:383-391: the timer is only armed when why !== 'task'). Leaving the iPad on a topic or a Code/Japanese/Mind lesson for an hour while studying on the Mac, the iPad keeps showing the old inspector (RAG band, status, checks, due counts), the old flashcard queue (cards already rated on the Mac are asked again and rated twice) and the old Code evidence, with nothing on screen saying newer data arrived. Tab switches inside the topic are not navigation, so they do not refresh it either. Combined with in-page editors this is also what makes the editor overwrite in the P0 finding possible.
- **Evidence:** js/core/ui.js:358-359 (TASK_VIEWS), :380-392 (task holds with no timer, bgPendingFor only cleared by the next redraw); eval r1.js: held:true, page and scroll kept, no later flush.
- **Root cause:** Stopgap trades staleness for stability with no reconciliation and no indicator.
- **Proposed fix:** Part of the redraw policy: hold the REMOUNT, not the data — show a small 'Updated on another device · Refresh' chip on held pages, flush at a safe boundary (end of a flashcard/quiz session, page turn, tab change, idle 2 min with no draft), and let session engines re-read the queue between cards.
- **Flags:** effort M, needs a design prompt

### SY-15 · P3 · a11y — After a background redraw the open dialog's opener is detached, so closing it drops focus to <body>

- **RESOLVED:** no longer reproduces on kos-redraw-1 (7 Nov, SY re-check): background redraws are held while a dialog is open (sd7 rerun).
- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** no longer reproduces: background redraws are held while a dialog is open — sd7 rerun with background:'hard' {dlgAfter:true, inpAfter:'Typed title', openerConnected:true, focusAfterClose:'BUTTON'}
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Dialogs survive a redraw (they live on body), but KOS.ui.openDialog restores focus to the opener, which the redraw replaced. Repro: Assignments, '＋ New assignment', type a title, KOS.rerender() (dialog and text survive), Cancel -> document.activeElement is BODY; the keyboard/VoiceOver user is thrown to the top of the document. cloudsync does not check for an open dialog (routines.onSession does).
- **Evidence:** eval sd7.js: {dlgAfter:true, inpAfter:'Typed title', openerConnected:false, focusAfterClose:'BODY'}. js/core/routines.js:699 has the dialog guard; js/core/cloudsync.js:723-733 has none
- **Root cause:** redraw under an open dialog
- **Proposed fix:** Defer background redraws while KOS.ui.topDialog() (policy), and in openDialog's restore fall back to an element with the same data-ui/text in the new DOM (as mobile-shell's calendarFocusSignature already does, mobile-shell.js:620-640).
- **Flags:** effort S

### SY-16 · P3 · ux — Boot-time redraws of whatever page the PWA reopened on (Google read-only copy, own art pictures, sample seed)

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** changed: ext.js:364 and main.js:303/307 now pass {background:'soft'}, so task pages are held; other pages still remount once at boot when the Google copy or own pictures load
- **Devices:** iPad (PWA restore), all
- **Detail / repro:** Three boot paths call KOS.rerender() on the current page after async work: KOS.ext boot when Google Calendar is connected (ext.js:364, after loadRo from IndexedDB), KOS.art.loadOwn (main.js:307) and the sample seed (main.js:299-304). The iPad Home Screen app restores the last route (e.g. a topic), so the page the user has just started reading or tapping is remounted a moment after launch, for data (Google's read-only chips, decorative art) that only Calendar or a painted slot needs.
- **Evidence:** js/core/ext.js:364; js/main.js:299-307
- **Root cause:** KOS.rerender used as a broadcast
- **Proposed fix:** Have these refresh only the views that read them (Calendar for loadRo; the art slots via KOS.art.apply/paint, which artslot.js already does in place) instead of a full remount.
- **Flags:** effort S

### SY-17 · P3 · arch — Inconsistent refresh policy: Google/Todoist pulls change Calendar and Reminders without redrawing them, while a state pull redraws every page

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds and is wider: besides Google/Todoist (ext.js:325-337), the Money (money.js:1227), Mind journal (mindjournal.js:268), review log, reports and media autosync pulls change data without any redraw, while a state pull redraws every non-task page
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.ext.syncAll (every cycle and the 1.5 s 'soon' sync) writes pulled events and reminders through the owners, then only notifies KOS.ext.onChange listeners — only the Connections page listens. An open Calendar or Reminders page keeps showing the old data (a task completed in Todoist stays unticked on screen) until the user navigates, whereas a cloud state pull remounts any page however unrelated. There is no single 'state changed → which views care' mechanism.
- **Evidence:** js/core/ext.js:325-337 (syncAll -> changed()), :294; js/modules/connections.js:173-177 (the only listener); js/core/extgcal.js and exttasks.js contain no redraw
- **Root cause:** no domain-scoped change notification
- **Proposed fix:** Introduce one change bus (KOS.changed(domains)) fired by cloudsync (with the keys that differed), ext, routines, inksync, files; views subscribe by domain and refresh in place (or defer while busy).
- **Flags:** effort M

### SY-27 · P3 · ux — The Files page repaints its whole list on every text-index step and cloud file event, outside the redraw hold

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** files.js listens for kos-files-index and calls paintSubj(), paint() and paintSide(), which empty and rebuild the list. That event fires after every file the background text indexer finishes (one file at a time, files.js:404) and after every cloud files change (cloudsync notifyFiles -> kos-files -> refresh -> emit). 'files' is in TASK_VIEWS, but this path never goes through KOS.rerender, so the hold does not apply: an open per-file menu is left pointing at a detached opener (closing it drops focus), and focus on a card button is lost while a large import is still indexing.
- **Evidence:** eval r13.js (ipad): {menuOpen:true, menuAfter:true, openerConnected:false}. js/modules/files.js:319-320 (onIndex), :241-249 (paint empties listEl), :280-281; js/core/files.js:45 (emit), :100, :404; js/core/cloudsync.js:1414.
- **Root cause:** A page-local repaint on a global event with no diff and no hold.
- **Proposed fix:** Repaint only the changed card (key by fileId) or only the 'Indexing…' counts; skip the list repaint while a menu or dialog is open, as KOS.rerender does.
- **Flags:** effort S

**QoL ideas from this auditor:**
- Show a quiet 'Updated from another device' chip with Refresh instead of redrawing a busy page
- Remember the CS/Maths/IT note page per topic (like the study spaces) so returning to a topic lands where you left off
- Keep a partly rated flashcard batch resumable from the Due today chip after leaving the page

**Backlog ideas from this auditor:**
- Domain-scoped change bus (KOS.changed(domains)) replacing KOS.rerender as a broadcast; views refresh in place
- Per-view session store for transient study state, so engines resume after any remount, reload or iPad app kill
- Smoke test: for each study view set transient state, call KOS.rerender(), assert page, card, question, scroll and focus survive
- A real redraw policy to replace the stopgap: each view declares its transient state (or keeps it in a per-visit session store keyed by route), background changes carry the changed paths, a view redraws only when a path it reads changed and never mid-task, async callers pass the route they belong to, and long-lived editors reconcile by row id instead of writing whole arrays.

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds

- **Detail / repro:** The Spec tab is drawn from js/data/maths.js content/info lines, which are raw, broken PDF extraction. Examples: M7.3 guidance reads "v = u + at r = ut +1at2 / e.g. , with vectors / 2 given in i - j or column vector form". 5.6 reads "Understand and use double a n g le f / rm u l a e ; u s e / f s in ( A ± B ), fo r m u l a e fo r / ± ± cos (A B)". 2.1 reads "× = , ÷ = - , = m n n am / The equivalence ofa and should be known." 2.10 starts mid-sentence: "into partial fractions". 25 leaves still contain the extraction artefact "need to learn:" or "students need to learn:". A heuristic found fragment lines in 36 of the 89 leaves: 1.1 2.1 2.2 2.3 2.4 2.5 2.7 2.9 3.3 4.1 4.2 4.3 5.1 5.2 5.3 5.5 5.6 5.7 6.2 6.3 6.4 7.1 7.2 7.4 8.2 8.3 8.5 8.6 9.4 10.4 S2.3 S4.1 S5.3 M7.4 M8.3 M8.6, and reading the dump shows more. Exponents, fractions, sums and integrals are lost throughout. This is very likely part of why M7.3 looks bare.
- **Evidence:** shots/content-maths/m73-spec-mac.png; shots/content-maths/p5-6-spec-mac.png; cm/spine.txt (every leaf's spec text); tools/gen_data.py:240-255 (maths_group copies clean(x) of the extracted lines) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): Re-shot on kos-redraw-1: shots/content-maths/top-m73-spec-mac.png (Guidance: 'r = ut +1at2', 'e.g. , with vectors', '2 given in i - j'); js/data/maths.js still has 25 'need to learn:'; no commit to tools/gen_data.py or js/data/maths.js since 56b1a8c.
- **Root cause:** The spec spine is generated from a PDF text extraction (/home/claude/extract) that splits equations and kerned headings, and no override or cleanup pass exists for Maths.
- **Proposed fix:** Hand-author the 89 Maths spec entries from the Edexcel 9MA0 PDF as typeset blocks (LaTeX in $…$). Either fix the extractor or add a checked-in override table that gen_data.py applies (as SHORT does), and regenerate. Drop the "need to learn:" headers. Add a smoke test that refuses fragment lines (≤4 characters, runs of single letters, "need to learn").
- **Flags:** effort L

### CM-02 · P1 · content — Quiz answers are almost always A or B, and options are never shuffled

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Of 1,058 Maths quiz items, the correct option is A in 531 and B in 481. Only 44 are C and 2 are D. Base files: 380 A, 100 B, 17 C, 1 D. Bank files: 151 A, 381 B, 27 C, 1 D. KOS.quiz.mountMCQ renders opts in authored order, and its Shuffle button only reorders the questions. A learner soon learns to pick A on a base item or B on a bank item, so the quiz score stops measuring understanding. Separately, the correct option is uniquely the longest in 317 items (30%).
- **Evidence:** cm/metrics.json ansDist per leaf; js/engines/quiz.js:66 (Shuffle shuffles order only), :88-96 (item.opts rendered in order, answer compared to item.ans at :113); e.g. js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js:305-306 (every item ans: 0); shots/content-maths/m73-quiz-ipad.png (Q1 answer A) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): Re-measured: base answers A 380/498, bank answers B 381/560 (D appears 1+1 times); js/engines/quiz.js:66 Shuffle reorders questions only, :88-96 options in authored order. New repro: answering A to every question of M7.3 scores 9/13 = 69% (cm/qz-retry.js), which the RAG then reads as Green.
- **Root cause:** Authors put the right answer first (bank authors second), and the engine trusts the authored order.
- **Proposed fix:** In mountMCQ, shuffle a per-question option permutation at mount and on Retry, seeded per attempt, and map clicks back to the original index so the stats and the why text stay valid. Optionally also rebalance the authored ans positions so a fixed order is fair too.
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-14 · P1 · bug — Exam questions self-mark ignores the M1/A1 codes on Maths worked-derived items, and the Answer line counts as a mark

- **Independent check:** confirmed by Claude's independent re-check (B2, runtime + code)
- **Review note (8 Nov):** Also breaks invariant 135 (an A mark ticked without its M is accepted). Shares its root cause with CC-14/CC-17 (the Answer line is a tickable mark); 28 derived parts' [M/A/B] weights do not sum to their marks (cf. CM-21).
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** 592 of the 1,244 Maths exam parts (48%) are derived from exam-style worked examples by KOS.content.examFromWorked. Each mark-scheme point is one STEP, ending in its codes, for example '[M1 A1]', and the worked answer is added as an extra point, '**Answer:** …'. The self-mark tally in js/engines/quiz.js knows nothing about those codes. When the number of points equals the marks (106 parts), each tick counts as 1 mark. When there are more points (112 parts), it caps at the total. When there are fewer (374 parts), it scales the marks in proportion. Repro on maths 1.1 Q1 (3 marks; points '[M1 A1]', '[A1]', 'Answer'): ticking only the Answer line awards 1/3, and ticking only the [M1 A1] step also awards 1/3, when it is worth 2. Each row prints '1' beside it. The needsM rule (an A needs its M) never applies, because the lines start with the working, not with 'A1'. So the logged exam session (KOS.sessions.log type exam, marks/max) records partial marks that do not match the mark scheme it shows. The 652 bank parts are written one point per mark and are correct.
- **Evidence:** shots/content-maths/selfmark-answerline-mac.png (Answer ticked → Awarded 1/3; step 1 shows [M1 A1] but '1'); eval on #/ref/maths/1.1 Exam questions: onlyAnswerTicked '1', onlyStep1Ticked '1'; counts via eval over KOS_CONTENT: derived parts 592 (perMark 106, more 112, fewer 374), bank 652 all perMark; js/core/content.js:547-555 (ms = one line per step + '[mk]', Answer pushed as a point); js/engines/quiz.js:264-268 (needsM tests /^\s*A\d/), :286-296 (perMark / proportional fromTicks)
- **Root cause:** examFromWorked emits one scheme point per step (several marks) plus the answer, but the tally assumes one point = one mark or scales proportionally
- **Proposed fix:** In examFromWorked, expand each step into one point per mark code (e.g. '[M1] …', '[A1] …' with the step text on the first), so the scheme is one point per mark like the banks; do not push the Answer as a point (show it as a separate 'Answer' line under the scheme). Alternatively give points a weight parsed from their [codes] and make fromTicks sum weights and needsM read the code tokens. Add a smoke check: Σ point weights = marks for every exam part.
- **Flags:** effort M

### CM-04 · P2 · arch — A curriculum fork silently hides later curriculum upgrades (plausible cause of "M7.3 is basically bare")

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.content.get and srs read state.edits first (invariant 86). A fork copies the shipped material at the moment of the first edit and is never compared with the curriculum again. M7.3 was an outline entry until commit 4d791ca ("load M6–M7 at depth, drop their outline entries"), and a9f64b5 rewrote M7.2 and M7.3. A Notes fork made before then (or one carried over from S7.3 by the ref rename, router.js:117 renamedRef) keeps showing the old, thin outline notes. Nothing tells the user that a newer, much deeper version exists. The only sign is the Edit button's data-state forked (hub.js:2828). The shipped M7.3 renders in full (8 pages), so a bare M7.3 on the user's device most likely comes from such a fork.
- **Evidence:** js/core/edits.js:1-60 (no base hash or staleness check: grep for stale/baseHash finds nothing); git log -- js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js (a9f64b5, 4d791ca); shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (shipped content present) | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): js/core/edits.js:199-207 set() stores only the kind and updatedAt — no shipped hash or version; fixture: KOS.edits.set('maths','M7.3','notes', first 3 blocks) then reopen: no notice on the Notes tab or inspector (eval, then reset); shots/content-maths/top-m73-forked-mac.png taken after the reset shows the shipped 8 pages.
- **Root cause:** The fork model has no notion of the base version it was taken from.
- **Proposed fix:** Record a hash of the shipped kind on each fork (fork.base). When the shipped hash differs, show a banner on the tab: "The curriculum for this topic was updated after you edited it: View new · Keep mine · Merge (append your rows)". Check the user's real state for state.edits.topics['maths:M7.3'] (or 'maths:S7.3').
- **Flags:** effort M, needs a design prompt

### CM-08 · P2 · content — Wrong flashcard answer: 9.3 Newton–Raphson from x0 = 0 gives x1 = −2.5, not 2.5

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds

In fact f(0) = −5 and f′(0) = −2, so x1 = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5, which the card's own formula (2x³+5)/(3x²−2) also gives. The question also states something false: it says the method fails and the answer says it does not.
- **Evidence:** js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-c.js:646 | RECHECK 8 Nov (kos-redraw-1): js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-c.js:646 unchanged: answer says '$x_1 = 2.5$'; x1 = 0 − f(0)/f'(0) = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5.
- **Root cause:** An arithmetic sign slip in the bank author's answer, with no automated check on numeric answers.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite the card, e.g. "Where would NR fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" → "Where $f'(x_0)=0$: $x_0=\pm\sqrt{2/3}$". Or keep the x0 = 0 example with "$x_1=-2.5$ (far from the root 2.09)". Keep its schedule key (invariant 87).
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-16 · P2 · bug — Newton–Raphson generator prints a 'Root estimate' that is not a root in about a third of its random examples

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The worked-example generator 'newraph', wired to 9.3, always does exactly three iterations from a random x0 and then prints 'Root estimate: x ≈ …', whatever f is at that point. In 138 of 400 random examples, |f(x3)| > 0.01. Two cases: x^3 − 2x − 5 from x0 = 1 gives 'x ≈ 3.34870 (f ≈ 25.85)' (the true root is 2.0946), and x^3 + x − 1 from x0 = 3 gives 'x ≈ 0.88069 (f ≈ 0.564)' (the true root is 0.6823). A learner using the generator to check their own working is taught that a non-converged value is the answer.
- **Evidence:** eval on slot 7: 400 runs of KOS.worked.byIds(['newraph'])[0] → bad 138; examples quoted above; js/labs/worked.js:704 (Root estimate step printed unconditionally after three iterations)
- **Proposed fix:** Iterate until |x_{n+1} − x_n| < 1e-6 (cap about 20) and show the first three steps plus 'converges to …'. Or pick x0 near a root (from a sign change). If it does not converge, say so ('not converged yet: f(x3) = …').
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-17 · P2 · bug — 'Retry the N missed' overwrites the topic's quiz score with the retry's: 9/13 then 4/4 records lastPct 100 and the head reads 'best 9/4'

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** After a quiz, 'Retry the N missed' (js/engines/quiz.js:178-181) mounts the SAME engine on the missed subset with the topic's own stats record. finish() (quiz.js:156-160) then sets lastPct = correct / subset size, logs a second 'quiz' session with total = the subset, and the head line compares the stored best (a count out of the full quiz) with the subset length. Repro on #/ref/maths/M7.3 (empty account): answer every question with A → 9/13, record {attempts 1, best 9, lastPct 69}; press 'Retry the 4 missed', answer them right → record {attempts 2, best 9, lastPct 100}, sessions [{9/13 69%}, {4/4 100%}], head 'score 4 · best 9/4'. RAG reads lastPct (js/modules/rag.js:63-71), so a learner who got 69% now shows no quiz weakness at all, and the ledger/Reports count a 100% quiz that never happened.
- **Evidence:** audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/qz-retry.js (eval on slot 7, output quoted); shots/content-maths/top-quizbest-inspector-mac.png ('best 9/13', inspector 'Quiz attempts 2', 'Data says Green'); js/engines/quiz.js:156-165, :178-181; js/modules/rag.js:63-71
- **Root cause:** The missed-retry reuses mountMCQ's normal finish path, which assumes items is the topic's whole quiz.
- **Proposed fix:** Pass a 'practice' flag for the missed retry: do not touch st.lastPct/best (or record it under a separate missedRetry field), log it as a practice session (or not at all), and print the head as 'retrying 4 missed' instead of best/total.
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-18 · P2 · ux — One mediocre quiz makes a Maths topic 'Data says Green': the RAG starts at 100 and a 69% quiz only takes 8 points off

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** rag.auto (js/modules/rag.js:30-110) starts every topic at score 100 and SUBTRACTS for weak signals; band() (rag.js:17) is Green from 70. With only a quiz as evidence, the most a quiz can remove is 25 (lastPct 0 %), so ANY single quiz attempt — even 0 % — leaves the topic Amber or Green, and a 69 % quiz removes 8 → Green. Thin evidence (one quiz, no cards rated, no exam questions, 0/4 checks, status Not started) is judged as mastery. Repro: empty account, M7.3, quiz answered all-A (9/13 = 69 %): inspector shows 'Data says Green' beside 'Not started' and '0/4 checks'. The answer-position bias (all-A scores 69 %) makes this reachable without reading a single question.
- **Evidence:** shots/content-maths/top-quizbest-inspector-mac.png; js/modules/rag.js:17 (band), :63-71 (quiz penalty capped at 25), :103 (no minimum evidence); eval qz-retry.js before the retry: lastPct 69 → band g
- **Root cause:** Subtractive scoring from 100 with capped penalties and no evidence threshold.
- **Proposed fix:** Make the auto band evidence-weighted: start from 'no claim' and require a minimum amount of evidence (e.g. ≥ N cards rated or a quiz ≥ 80 % plus another signal) before Green; map a lone quiz to a score proportional to its percentage rather than a capped deduction.
- **Flags:** effort M

- **Proposed fix:** Print P(min(x, 2μ−x) < X < max(x, 2μ−x)).
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-23 · P3 · content — Hypothesis-test generators draw contradictory set-ups (testing p < p0 with x far above the mean)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The 'hyptest' generator (S5.2) draws the tail and x independently. In 187 of 400 random examples, x lies on the wrong side of the mean for the alternative being tested. Example: H1: p < 0.4 with n = 17 and x = 15 gives P(X ≤ 15) = 1.00000. The example is formally right but teaches nothing, and no exam question is set up that way. The projectile generator also prints '−0 = 20T − 4.9T²' and '4.9T² − 20T − 0 = 0' whenever h = 0 (174 of 400 runs). The partial-fractions and normal-parameters generators print unbracketed double signs: '(5·-1 + -1) / (-1 − 1)' and 'μ = 25 − -0.9945 × 8.0963'.
- **Evidence:** eval on slot 7 (400-run sweeps of every one of the 36 Maths generators: no exceptions or NaN; hyptestSilly 187/400; projectile '−0' 174/400); js/labs/worked.js:752 (hyptest random); js/labs/worked-extra.js:356-373 (projectile)
- **Proposed fix:** hyptest: draw x from the alternative's side (below n·p0 for 'lower'), and draw h in the projectile generator only when h > 0 or drop the term. Use a shared signed formatter that brackets negatives inside a product or after a minus sign.
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-24 · P3 · content — Seven Maths callouts use an undefined kind 'key' and render as an unlabelled teal Tip

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The callout schema (js/core/content.js:31, CALLOUT_META :49-58) knows info, def, tip, warn, miscon, mnemonic, memorise and formula. Seven Maths callouts in 1.1, 9.2, 9.3 and 10.x use t:'key'. The renderer falls back to the Tip icon (◆), and the stylesheet has no [data-kind=key] rule, so they get the base teal, the same as info and formula. The author meant a 'key idea' box, but on the page it cannot be told apart from an ordinary formula or info box.
- **Evidence:** audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/cm/beh1.js output 'bad callout types: key 7'; grep -rn 't: "key"' js/data/content → maths-pure-p1.js:152, maths-pure-p10.js:27, :437 and maths-pure-p9.js; js/core/content.js:346 (CALLOUT_META[t] || tip); css/views/study.css:321-334 (no key rule)
- **Proposed fix:** Either add a 'key' kind to CALLOUT_META and the stylesheet (e.g. 'Key idea', crimson), or change the seven to an existing kind. Then make validate_content.js reject unknown callout kinds.
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-25 · P3 · content — Two bank items depend on the item before them and break when the quiz is shuffled (M8.4 'Tension then:')

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The M8.4 bank item Q6 reads only 'Tension then:' (options 0 / 39.2 N / 78.4 N / 19.6 N). It relies on Q5 ('Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley'). The quiz has a Shuffle control that reorders the questions (js/engines/quiz.js:66), so after a shuffle, or when Q6 appears alone in a review of missed items, the question has no data. A sweep of all 1,058 Maths quiz stems found no other stem that leans on the previous item: the 'then' in 4.1, M7.1 and M9.1 completes the sentence.
- **Evidence:** js/data/content/bank-maths-mech.js (M8.4 quiz, items 5–6); node print of maths:M8.4 quiz: 'Q5b Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley. Acceleration: … Q6b Tension then:'; stem-dependency regex sweep over KOS_CONTENT maths quiz
- **Proposed fix:** Make Q6 self-contained: 'Two 4 kg masses hang over a smooth pulley. The tension is:'.
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-26 · P3 · content — 6.4 flashcard question mixes base 2 and base 10 in one garbled stem

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The 6.4 bank card reads 'Solve log_2(x+3) + log_2(x+10) = 2 + 2log_2 x… with base 10 and 2 = log 100.' The answer works in base 10 ((x+3)(x+10) = 100x², x = 0.620), so the stem is a half-edited sentence. Read as written (base 2), the answer would be (x+3)(x+10) = 4x², giving x = 6, which is a different answer.
- **Evidence:** js/data/content/bank-maths-pure-b.js:739
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite the stem as 'Solve log(x+3) + log(x+10) = 2 + 2 log x (base 10).'
- **Flags:** effort S

### CM-27 · P3 · content — A third of Maths quiz explanations are a bare label: 352 of 1,058 'why' lines are three words or fewer with no working ('Definition.' ×9, 'Chain rule.' ×9, 'Add.', 'Tables.')

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** After a wrong answer the quiz shows the item's 'why' as the explanation. In 352 of 1,058 Maths quiz items (99 base, 253 bank) it is three words or fewer with no maths: 'Definition.' ×9, 'Chain rule.' ×9, 'Power law.' ×5, 'Product rule.', 'Multiply.', 'Add.', 'Tables.', 'Vertex.', 'Union.', 'Conjugate.'. A learner who picked the wrong option is told the name of a rule, not why their option was wrong or what the right working is. The bank files are the main source (253 of 560 bank items vs 99 of 498 base).
- **Evidence:** node one-liner over cm/load.js (KOS_CONTENT maths quiz): 352/1058 label-only, by source {base 99, bank 253}; examples: maths:2.2 Q11 'Conjugate.', maths:2.3 Q14 'Vertex.', maths:2.5 Q10 'Union.'; js/data/content/bank-maths-*.js
- **Root cause:** Bank items were authored with terse whys and no length/quality check in validate_content.
- **Proposed fix:** Rewrite the label-only whys as one line of working that names the misconception behind the most tempting wrong option (e.g. 'Multiply by the conjugate $3-\sqrt7$, so the denominator becomes $9-7=2$').
- **Flags:** effort M

### CM-28 · P3 · content — Four Pure leaf titles show raw caret notation ('e^x', 'Gradient of e^kx', 'Solving a^x = b', 'Differentiating x^n, e^kx…') in the spine, heading and search

## CC — A-Level CS and OCR IT content quality (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** CS content is deep and renders cleanly at every device size, but its practice layers have systematic faults: multiple-choice answers sit at A/B 94% of the time, bank files duplicate past-paper questions already authored as worked cards, and ~30 decks ask one fact twice. The inventory pass found that the self-mark tally, not just the content, misjudges marks: examFromWorked turns the one-line Answer summary into a tickable mark and ignores each step's own weight, so 60 CS items cannot reach full marks from their real points, and IT schemes give one checkbox per two marks. IT is the weak side: the generated spec dumps garbled assessment-criteria text into the last leaf of each unit and duplicates F206.6.1, F201 has no worked answers and almost no examiner intel, the IT desk's 'Start here' points at the finished F200, and its boundary card collapses on iPad portrait. Shared presentation gaps: the worked card's 'Write it out' pill covers titles on iPhone, the reading place is lost on any detour (a notes diagram, then Back, reopens page 1), and syntax colours are nearly invisible in the light shop theme Washi Morning. Root causes: authoring without automated checks (no near-duplicate, answer-position, mark-sum or validate_content gate), mark weights kept as display text, the IT parser's missing section boundaries, and view-local or dark-tuned state that was never generalised.

### CC-01 · P1 · content — IT spec text for F206.6.1, F204.6.5, F202.5.1, F201.5.2, F200.5.3 (and F200.2.x/F202.2.x) holds garbled PDF dumps of the assessment criteria

- **Review note (8 Nov):** Partly wrong for F201: the hand-made KOS_SPEC_FIX covers 5.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.6 and Factor analysis on the Spec tab. The faulty parser is tools/parse_it.py, not tools/gen_data.py.
- **Detail / repro:** The generated IT spec (js/data/it.js) contains multi-thousand-character strings of shuffled PDF text in the Spec tab content/info lists for the last leaf of each unit: e.g. F206.6.1 'Ways to reflect' ends with a 2,271-char 'Lessons learnt Assessment criteria The table below gives...' string and a 2,884-char info item; F204.6.5 has 2,164/1,007/2,510-char strings; F202.5.1 2,330/538/2,502; F201.5.2 (the unit the user is sitting) has 'Urban and community planning Assessment guidance This unit is assessed by an exam...' and an 831-char run; F200.5.3 876 chars. Shorter merged rows also start with a dangling 'include:' (F200.2.2, F200.2.3, F200.2.6, F201.2.4, F202.2.2, F202.2.4, F202.2.5, F202.3.3). Column-interleaved words ('The tasks. means that the unit grade awarded') are unreadable on the Spec tab and pollute search and the Assistant's spec reads. F206 is the NEA the user is doing now. Beyond the long dumps, 189 short spec rows in 39 IT leaves are fragments ('□ Does', '□ Techniques To', '• Diagnostic Prescriptive □', a bare '□'), e.g. F201.2.3 Data mining techniques reads ['□ Data mining','□ Data mining techniques','• Descriptive','• Diagnostic Prescriptive □','□','□ Does','□'] and F201.2.6 omits 'Factor analysis' which the notes teach.
- **Evidence:** js/data/it.js:2246-2283 (F206.6.1 content/info); node scan of dump.json: strings >260 chars listed per leaf (F206.6.1 2271/894/2884, F204.6.5 2164/1007/2510, F202.5.1 2330/538/2502, F201.5.2 324/328/308/831, F200.5.3 331/308/876)
- **Root cause:** PDF parser in tools/gen_data.py appends trailing unit-level sections (criteria tables, guidance, synoptic tables) to the last topic leaf and mis-splits two-column 'To include' boxes.
- **Proposed fix:** Fix tools/gen_data.py's IT parser to stop each leaf at the 'Assessment criteria'/'Assessment guidance'/'Synoptic assessment' headings and at page-column breaks, and to join 'To include:' continuation lines into bullet rows; regenerate it.js (invariant 24) and add a smoke check that no IT spec string exceeds ~300 chars or starts with 'include:'.
