## PR — Focus, Reminders, Routines, Daily Review, Calendar, Pacing (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** Top-up on sw kos-redraw-1 (e6c08b1): all 22 earlier findings re-checked (20 hold, 2 changed, none gone) and 21 new ones from a behaviour inventory with fixtures across Focus, Reminders, Routines, the Daily Review, Calendar and Pacing. The four P1s still hold: the Afternoon review's 'Place in a free block' menu opens under the dialog (z-menu 110 < z-modal 120, the one root cause behind several 'dead' menus inside dialogs), page headers draw the previous page's art (pageHeader reads state.ui.view before KOS.show sets it), About to Study overrides 'General study — no link' with an assignment, and a long assignment title runs off the running Focus stage. The inventory found the engines mostly sound (Focus pay rules per mode, idle watch, switching, snapshots, rest days, streaks, late ticks, carry-over and lesson ticks all behave as their invariants say), but the edges leak: a routine of only optional steps can never be kept, ticking the minimum first locks out the full award, a one-step 'New routine' silently becomes a habit, monthly reminders drift after a short month, a repeating reminder's completion cannot be undone (the review's Undo does nothing for it), auto-tracked Focus habits count aborted sessions on the calendar rather than routine day, and Pacing accepts a mid-week week beginning that takes over 'this week'. Most root causes are a missing rule in a single gate (verdict, updateWeek, the dayReview settings normaliser, nextOccurrence) rather than structural problems; the structural ones are the menu layering and the header-art ordering.

**Coverage.** Seeded and empty accounts on slot 13; Mac 1470x832, iPad 820x1180 (and the Calendar at 1180x820 earlier), iPhone 402x874; Graphite, Atelier Dawn (body and root data-theme set — the harness's --theme alone leaves body on Dusk) and the sakura-skyline shop theme. DOM sweeps (prod2/s-*.json seeded mac/ipad/iphone, prod2/e-*.json empty mac/iphone) over #/focus, #/reminders, #/routines (today, routines, templates, history, settings, edit/habits), #/calendar, #/pacing and #/pacing/braid; screenshots looked at are in shots/productivity/inv/. Behaviour fixtures (prod2/*.js): every Focus mode's pay and end paths, the idle watch end to end, a mid-session switch; routine verdicts (all-optional, minimum, snapshot, re-tick, on-demand), schedules (every N days, weekend override), rest days, streak/best/summary, late evening ticks, several-times-a-day habits, auto-tracking with thin and contradictory evidence, the one-step New routine save, the player to the end; reminders' recurrence, completion, undo, lists, tags, reward cap and alert forecast; Daily Review due()/folding with out-of-order times, the morning Three picks, the afternoon Place menu and time strip, triage code; Calendar recurrence, validation, the modal; Pacing carry-over, lesson ticks, week edit/delete. Matrix: productivity.inventory.md. NOT checked: break nudge chime, distraction penalties and wake lock (need real time/visibility/audio), Kurenai's review words (no AI route in the harness), iPad Home Screen standalone and real Safari, Google/Todoist sync, the phone Focus dock and mini-player drag (presentation from the 1–2 Nov run only), the Pacing Class days dialog image, and the Evening review end to end on this build.

### PR-01 · P1 · bug — Afternoon review: 'Place in a free block' menu opens BEHIND the review dialog, so it does nothing

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds: eval prod2/place.js 6 Nov 18:52 — menu panel z-index 110 under the review dialog's 120, elementFromPoint at the panel = .k-dr-place (not the menu); a programmatic click on its item does add the event (added 1); js/core/ui.js:857-870, css/tokens.css:1031-1032
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Daily Review > Afternoon > step 3 Time left. Pressing 'Place in a free block' sets aria-expanded=true and appends the menu panel to <body>, but the panel is z-index var(--z-menu)=110 while the review overlay is var(--z-modal)=120, so the menu is painted under the dialog's scrim and panel: nothing visible appears, and a tap where the item would be lands on the dialog (elementFromPoint at the first item's centre returns another row's 'Place in a free block' button). The item's onSelect itself works: invoking it programmatically creates the study block (15:30, 90 min, type study, assignmentId 1) with an Undo toast. Same root cause affects EVERY KOS.ui.menu used inside a KOS.ui.openDialog (the primitive never raises a menu above an open modal). Also reproduced on About to Study's 'Change ▾' task menu (preflight dialog): panel z=110, elementFromPoint at its first item returns the dialog's k-field, not the menu.
- **Evidence:** shots/productivity/dr-place-open-mac.png (menu open per aria-expanded, nothing shown); eval: panel z=110, overlay z=120, panel parent BODY, topEl at item centre = 'k-btn k-btn--sm ui.menu-button'; css/tokens.css:1031-1032 (--z-menu:110, --z-modal:120); css/components.css:334 (.k-menu-panel z-index var(--z-menu)); js/core/ui.js:813 (place() appends panel to document.body); js/modules/dayreview.js:609
- **Root cause:** Menu layer token (110) below the modal layer token (120); menus are portalled to body regardless of an open modal.
- **Proposed fix:** In KOS.ui.menu place(): when the button is inside an open dialog (btn.closest('[data-ui~="ui.dialog"], .k-dialog-overlay')), append the panel inside that overlay (or set a state the CSS maps to z-index above --z-modal, e.g. a --z-menu-modal token 130). Add a smoke test that opens a menu inside openDialog and checks elementFromPoint hits the item.
- **Flags:** effort S

### PR-02 · P1 · bug — Every page header shows the PREVIOUS page's painted band after in-app navigation

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds: eval navigating #/pacing,#/routines,#/focus,#/reminders,#/calendar,#/routines → page-header art page.reminders, page.pacing, page.reminders, none, (no header), page.calendar; js/core/ui.js:642-643 (reads state.ui.view) and 1592-1594 (view rendered, then ui.view assigned)
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.ui.pageHeader picks its art from KOS.store.state.ui.view, but KOS.show sets state.ui.view only AFTER the view function has rendered. So navigating Pacing -> Routines draws Pacing's band on Routines, Routines -> Focus draws Reminders' band (Routines maps to 'reminders') on the Focus Timer, Focus -> Reminders draws none (Focus has no PAGE_ART entry), etc. Only a reload (where ui.view was persisted) shows the right picture. Repro via eval navigating #/pacing,#/routines,#/focus,#/reminders,#/calendar,#/routines: header images were reminders, pacing, reminders, none, none, calendar respectively. Affects every page that uses pageHeader, not only Productivity; the art audit just released depends on it.
- **Evidence:** eval output: '#/pacing [app.hero.page.reminders.webp]', '#/routines [app.hero.page.pacing.webp]', '#/focus [app.hero.page.reminders.webp]', '#/routines [app.hero.page.calendar.webp]'; shots/productivity/focus-mac-seed.png and routines-mac-seed-2.png (sticky-note pinboard band on Focus/Routines); js/core/ui.js:589-592 (art = PAGE_ART[state.ui.view]); js/core/ui.js:1541-1543 (view rendered, then ui.view assigned)
- **Root cause:** Ordering: state.ui.view is assigned after render in KOS.show (js/core/ui.js:1543), while pageHeader reads it during render.
- **Proposed fix:** Set a module variable (e.g. KOS.ui.currentView = viewId) BEFORE calling KOS.views[viewId] and read that in pageHeader; or have each view pass opts.art explicitly. Add a smoke check: navigate A->B and assert B's band id.
- **Flags:** effort S

### PR-03 · P1 · data — Focus: 'General study — no link' is overridden by About to Study, which silently links the session to the first assignment (even with 'Just start')

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds: eval 6 Nov (empty account + one assignment) — preflight({subject:null, assignmentId:null}) shows 'QA essay · Assignment · due Sun 8 Nov'; 'Just start' → active {subject:'compsci', assignmentId:1}; js/modules/routineplayer.js:279-287
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** On #/focus with subject 'General study — no link' and 'No assignment', pressing Start focus opens About to Study pre-filled with the overdue NEA assignment. Pressing 'Just start' (or Start Focus) starts a session with subject 'compsci' and assignmentId 1. The completed session then banks its minutes on that assignment (invariant 4a) and counts as CS study, i.e. time is misattributed. The only escape in the dialog, 'Change ▾', is a KOS.ui.menu that opens behind the dialog (same z-index bug), so there is no way to keep 'no link' short of turning off About to Study.
- **Evidence:** eval: Focus page left on General study/no assignment -> Start focus -> preflight.just-start -> session {subject:'compsci', assignmentId:1}; shots/productivity/focus-running-mac.png (About to Study shows NEA); js/modules/routineplayer.js:279-287 (taskOf falls back to taskChoices()[0] when ctx has no subject/assignment), 257 (go(skip) merges task even when skip); js/modules/focus.js:2253
- **Root cause:** taskOf() treats an empty subject as 'nothing chosen' and fills it from Today's three/assignments; go(true) still merges the filled task.
- **Proposed fix:** taskOf(ctx) must respect an explicit 'no link' from the Focus page: pass ctx.explicit = true from focus.js and return {title:'General study'} without falling back; offer the ladder's suggestion as a 'Use: <task>' choice instead of a default. 'Just start' should start exactly the Focus page's config (ctx without task). Fix the menu z-index too.
- **Flags:** effort S

### PR-05 · P2 · ui — Afternoon review time strip: end label '22:00 夜' overprints the last hour tick; 30-minute block text wraps to two lines

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** changed: time-dependent — at 18:52 the strip is clean (ticks 19:00 248-281, 20:00 588-621, 21:00 927-960; end label 1210-1261) and a 99-minute block shows its two lines by design; the overprint still follows from the code whenever the strip starts after ~21:00 (js/modules/dayreview.js:593-605); the related mislabel is filed separately ('Time-left strip's end label…')
- **Devices:** all, worst on iPad portrait/iPhone
- **Detail / repro:** In the Time left strip the hour ticks are left-anchored at their position and run up to the last hour before the evening review, while the end label is pinned at inline-end. With from=04:46 and until=22:00 the 21:00 tick starts at ~94% of the width, exactly under '22:00 夜' (the screenshot shows '2̶2̶:̶0̶0̶' overprinted). Short free blocks (30 min = ~31px) wrap '30 min' onto two lines and overflow their outline. Same overlap happens at any width; worse on iPad portrait and phone where the strip is narrower.
- **Evidence:** shots/productivity/dr-afternoon-timeleft-mac.png (top-right of strip, and the 08:00 block); js/modules/dayreview.js:593-604 (tick loop t<to; tend appended unconditionally); css/views/routines.css:340-341; shots/productivity/dr-afternoon-ipad-empty.png (iPad portrait: ticks 20:00/22:00 and '22:00 夜' overprinted, '30 mi' clipped)
- **Root cause:** No collision handling between left-anchored ticks and an inline-end end label; fixed hourly tick density regardless of width.
- **Proposed fix:** Skip any tick whose position is within ~1 label width (e.g. >88%) of the end label, or render the end label as the final tick; thin ticks by available width (every 2h/3h below ~700px). For blocks narrower than the label, show the length only in the aria/tooltip or as a single-line '30m' with white-space:nowrap and no padding.
- **Flags:** effort S

### PR-06 · P2 · ux — Calendar has no Agenda (or Day) view on Mac or iPad; Agenda exists only under 700px

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds: js/modules/calendar.js:1545 (desktop/iPad: month|week only), 1606-1618 (Agenda only in the phone composition); iPad portrait month chips are 81 px wide and unreadable (shots/productivity/inv/cal-ipad.png)
- **Devices:** mac, ipad, ipadl
- **Detail / repro:** At >700px the Calendar offers only Month and Week (js/modules/calendar.js:1545 mode is 'week'|'month'; buttons at 1589-1591). The Agenda list (renderPhone, the stored 'week' mode) is drawn only when matchMedia('(max-width:700px)') matches (calendar.js:1562-1563, 1613). So the user cannot get the agenda on the MacBook (1470) or iPad (820/1180). There is no Day view at any size. Also the same stored value calMode='week' means 'Week grid' on desktop and 'Agenda' on phone, so an iPad in Split View flipping across 700px silently changes view type.
- **Evidence:** shots/productivity/cal-week-mac.png, cal-week-ipad.png, cal-month-ipadl.png (segmented control: Month | Week only); shots/productivity/calendar-iphone-seed.png (Agenda | Month); js/modules/calendar.js:1545,1562-1563,1589-1591,1613-1620
- **Root cause:** Agenda was designed as the phone composition (frame 15g) and is hard-wired to the phone branch of render().
- **Proposed fix:** Make the mode a 3-value per-device setting {month, week, agenda} (+ optional day). Factor the phone agenda list (renderPhone's day lists + agendaRows) into a renderAgenda(board) usable at any width: on desktop/iPad draw it as the board beside the existing Today/Countdowns side column (a 2-week scrolling list grouped by day with time column, hue bar, derived chips). Keep phone default Agenda; migrate stored 'week' on phone to 'agenda'.
- **Flags:** effort M, needs a design prompt

### PR-23 · P2 · bug — A routine whose steps are all optional can never be kept: ticking every step leaves it 'partial' for ever (no pay, no streak)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** verdict() counts only required steps and requires req.length > 0 for done, so a routine saved with every step marked Optional (the editor's per-step Optional switch allows it, and 'Ask the next morning' forces a step optional) is judged of=0: ticking both steps returns state 'partial', no award, and the day shows as partial in History and breaks the streak. The editor's save() only refuses zero steps.
- **Evidence:** eval prod2/rt1.js: R.add({steps:[{optional},{optional}]}) → tick both → {state:'partial', award:null}, verdict {done:false,n:0,of:0}; js/core/routines.js:316-323 (verdict: done = req.length > 0 && n === req.length); js/modules/routines.js:965-969 (Optional switch, checkMorning forces optional), 1039-1044 (save validates only step count)
- **Root cause:** verdict() has no rule for a routine with no required steps and the editor does not prevent one.
- **Proposed fix:** Either refuse to save (toast 'At least one step must be required') or judge an all-optional routine kept when every step (or any step) is ticked; the same rule in verdict() and the editor's total.
- **Flags:** effort S

### PR-24 · P2 · bug — Ticking a routine's minimum step first pays the small minimum award and locks out the full award when you then finish every step

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** pay() runs on the first tick that makes the day 'min' or 'done' and sets e.paid; routineAward gives a minimum day 5 XP/1 gold/2 HP. If the minimum step is ticked before the others (natural when it is the first or easiest step), the day is paid as a minimum; completing all three required steps afterwards turns the day 'done' but pays nothing more (award null), so the user receives less than if they had ticked the minimum last. The streak/verdict is right; the reward depends on tick order.
- **Evidence:** eval prod2/rt1.js: routine [full1, small(minimum), full2]: tick small → award {xp:5,gold:1,hp:2}, then tick full1 and full2 → state 'done', award null, sessions added still 1; js/core/routines.js:370-377 (pay when v.done||v.min and !e.paid), js/core/governor.js:124-131 (min → 5/1/2; 3 required → 11/1/3)
- **Root cause:** Pay-once is keyed to the first kept state rather than the best state reached that day.
- **Proposed fix:** Pay the difference when a 'min' day becomes 'done' (store e.paidAs = 'min' and top up once to the full award through one extra todo entry or by amending the award before the day closes), or pay a minimum only when the routine day ends without the full set.
- **Flags:** effort M

### PR-25 · P2 · ux — '+ New routine' with a single step silently becomes a habit and disappears into Daily habits

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The routine editor's save() turns a NEW custom routine with one step into kind 'habit' (and normalise() names it after the step, ignoring nothing). After Save the app lands on the Routines tab, where the new routine is not listed: it is a row inside the Daily habits card on Today, with the routine's window/days applied as a habit. A user who started a one-step routine (e.g. 'Stretch, 5' with a 07:00–08:00 window) cannot find it where they made it, and its mark is dropped from view.
- **Evidence:** eval prod2/rtnew.js: #/routines {edit:'new'} → add step 'Stretch, 5' → Save → record {kind:'habit', name:'Stretch'}, location #/routines/routines and the tab text does not contain it; Today's habit card shows 'Daily habits 0 of 1 today … Stretch'; js/modules/routines.js:1045 (if steps.length === 1 && kind === 'custom' && isNew → kind 'habit'), 1047 (KOS.show('routines','routines') either way)
- **Root cause:** Implicit kind conversion on save with no feedback and a fixed landing tab.
- **Proposed fix:** Keep what the user made: save a one-step routine as a routine (kind custom) unless it was started from 'Add a habit'; if converting, say so in the toast ('Saved as a habit in Daily habits') and land on Today with the habit highlighted. The redundant ternary at 1047 shows the intended branch was never written.
- **Flags:** effort S

### PR-26 · P2 · data — Monthly reminders drift: due 31 Jan repeats 28 Feb, then 28 Mar (the day-of-month is lost after a short month)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.reminders.nextOccurrence advances from the PREVIOUS occurrence (clamped), so after one short month the repeat stays on the clamped day for ever: 31 Jan → 28 Feb → 28 Mar → 28 Apr. The Calendar's monthly recurrence anchors on the original day (occursOn: min(start day, last day)), so a reminder and a calendar event set up the same way disagree from March onwards. Yearly on 29 Feb has the same drift (to 28 Feb permanently).
- **Evidence:** eval prod2/rem.js: add({due:'2026-01-31',recur:'monthly'}) → nextOccurrence = '2026-02-28', next of that = '2026-03-28'; js/core/reminders.js:166-187 (addMonths clamps from `cur`), compare js/modules/calendar.js:422-428 (anchored to s.getDate())
- **Root cause:** Recurrence is stepped from the last clamped date instead of the series' anchor.
- **Proposed fix:** Store the anchor day (item.recurDay = original day of month, set when recur is chosen) and compute each next occurrence as min(anchor, last day of month), like the Calendar does.
- **Flags:** effort S

### PR-27 · P2 · ux — Completing a repeating reminder cannot be undone and leaves no record: no Undo, un-tick does not restore the date, nothing in Completed

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Ticking a repeating reminder rolls its due date forward (skipping every missed occurrence) and clears done/completedAt. The row's tick has no Undo toast (unlike plan rows), the item never appears in Completed, and KOS.reminders.complete(id,false) only clears flags, so the old date is gone. The Daily Review's 'Done' for a repeating reminder shows an Undo that calls complete(id,false) and therefore does not undo anything. A mis-tap on 'Pay rent · monthly' silently moves it a month.
- **Evidence:** eval prod2/rem.js: weekly due 22 Oct → complete → due '2026-11-12', done false, completedAt null, not in query({section:'completed'}); complete(false) → due still '2026-11-12'; js/core/reminders.js:213-250 (roll forward, no history), js/modules/reminders.js:370-375 and 546/569 (tick → complete → draw, no toast/undo); js/core/dayreview.js:300 (undo = complete(id,false))
- **Root cause:** Recurrence mutates the record in place with no undo token or completion log.
- **Proposed fix:** Have complete() return the previous {due, alerted, subs} and offer an Undo toast that restores it; keep a small completion history on the item (completions: [ts…], last 20) so Completed and Reports can show 'done 3 times'.
- **Flags:** effort S

Moving w/c 9 Nov's 'Week beginning' to Wednesday 4 Nov is accepted: the week now overlaps w/c 2 Nov (2–8 Nov), keeps its label 'w/c 9 Nov', moves its 16 rows, and on Friday 6 Nov currentWeek()/weekFor() return the moved week instead of w/c 2 Nov, so the hero, carry-over, Home's plan card and lesson dating all read the wrong week. ### PR-31 · P3 · bug — Review times can be set out of order and a later slot then folds a review that has not happened yet

- **Evidence:** eval: setConfig({slots:{morning:{weekday:'19:00'}}}) → due(17:00 Mon) = {slot:'afternoon', folded:['morning']}; js/core/dayreview.js:90-100 (no ordering), 166-176 (due iterates slots in fixed order)
- **Root cause:** The settings gate validates each time alone.

### PR-32 · P3 · data — Auto-tracked Focus habits count aborted sessions and split a late-night session at midnight instead of at the routine day start

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** autoMeasure() sums every focus entry's stretches for the day, including incomplete sessions that pay nothing (a 9-minute early stop added 9 min: 19 → 28), so three aborted 9-minute starts tick a '25 min of Focus' habit. It also filters by the ledger's calendar day (e.date === day) while `day` is the ROUTINE day (04:00 start, invariant 148): a session from 23:30 to 00:30 is split between two calendar days, and between 00:00 and 04:00 the minutes count towards the next routine day, not the night they belong to.
- **Evidence:** eval prod2/auto.js: baseline focus/maths today 19 min → after pushing an incomplete 540 s maths focus entry 28 min; reading (media) sessions correctly ignored; js/core/routines.js:628-645 (e.date !== day; no complete check), 676-678 (day = routineDay(now))
- **Root cause:** The habit reads the Goals engine's calendar-day convention inside the routine-day model.
- **Proposed fix:** Decide and document: count only sessions with metrics.complete (or full 10-minute blocks, matching the pay rule), and measure by the routine day (filter on routineDay(e.ts) rather than e.date).
- **Flags:** effort S

The same text is the toast, the bell item and the closed-app push (the outlook reuses notice()). An all-day reminder's 'At the time' alert fires at 09:00 as 'due now'.

- **Root cause:** String substitution on the option labels.
- **Proposed fix:** Word it as 'Due in 10 minutes · 09:00' / 'Due tomorrow' / 'Due today' from the actual offset and time.
- **Flags:** effort S

**QoL ideas from this auditor:**
- Daily Review Time left: after placing a block, mark the row 'Placed 15:30' (and remove that free block) so the same item isn't placed twice.
- Week view: open on the first event or 07:00 when 'now' is outside working hours, instead of centring on 05:00.
- Focus mini player (Mac): show the subject or objective beside the clock; the tiny progress ring next to the time is barely readable.
- Routine player (Mac): it has both an ✕ and a 'Close' in the side panel; keep one.
- Reminders: a 'Place in a free block' / 'Focus on this' action on a reminder, to tie Reminders to Focus and the Calendar.
- Calendar: stored events with unknown types (e.g. 'other' from imports or the seeder) render with no hue at all; run the stored events through KOS.calendar.normalise once at boot.
- Reminders: offer 'Remind me again tomorrow' (snooze) on an overdue row and in the reviews, instead of only Tomorrow/Done.
- Routines: show 'kept late' in History when a day was kept after its window.
- Calendar: 'Skip this showing' for a repeating event (the model already has a skip list for Google).

**Backlog ideas from this auditor:**
- Routines inside routines: a step can reference another routine. Model: add step.sub = <routineId> in normaliseStep (js/core/routines.js:142). Display text and minutes are DERIVED from the sub-routine (mins = the sum of its required steps' mins), never copied. Integrity, enforced in normalise(rec, base) and in the editor: (a) no cycles: walk sub links depth-first from the routine being saved, refusing any step whose sub reaches the parent (also cap depth at 2, so a sub-routine cannot itself contain subs); (b) the sub-routine's total cannot exceed the parent step's budget. Either make the step's mins read-only (= sub total), or, if the user sets a budget, refuse a save of the sub that would push it over and say which parent step it breaks; (c) a sub-routine must be on demand or share the parent's days (kind/anchor), otherwise it would also show on its own schedule. Keep 'days: null' (on demand) as the rule for anything used as a sub; (d) deleting a routine used as a sub is refused, or offers to unlink (steps become plain text with the last derived minutes). Logging: ticking a sub step in the player expands the sub's steps inline, and the parent step counts done when the sub's own completion rule is met that routine day. The sub's log entry is written under its own key with a parent tag, so it pays nothing on its own (pay once per invariant 143: only the parent pays). snapOf must store the sub's id and its frozen step list in the parent's snapshot (x[6] = sub snapshot), so editing the sub never rewrites a past day. The cloud merge needs no change (steps merge whole with the routine). Player: a nested progress bar, 'Shower · from Morning hygiene (3 steps)'.
- Calendar Agenda view for Mac and iPad: a 2-week scrolling day list beside the Today/Countdowns column, sharing the phone's agendaRows.
- Focus page while running: a live in-page session card (clock, cycles, objective, notes, Switch) in place of the empty banner.
- Unify KOS.ui.menu layering: a single top-layer root (or native popover API) that every menu, picker and toast uses above modals.

## MG — Money (Santander import); Goals pages only (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** Money's weakest part is still bank import, and every problem the user reported is reproduced on kos-redraw-1. All seven reconstructed Santander exports (midata comma, Windows-1252, semicolon/blank-first-line, Online Banking CSV with its preamble, .txt, QIF, OFX) are refused at step 1, because the importer reads line 1 as an exact-match header and knows only CSV. The duplicates come from a de-dupe key of date|amount|payee TEXT: re-importing with a different mapping, confirming a recurring rule, or typing the same payment all create twins; the same key also throws away genuine identical same-day payments inside one statement, and the app's own export re-imports every expense as income. After import nothing helps the student: raw bank strings, everything in Other, Type and Balance discarded, no batch history or undo after the dialog, and on iPhone and iPad portrait an entry cannot even be opened for editing (its Edit/Delete render below the whole list). The inventory also found thin-evidence leniency in Money goals ('5 no-spend days ✓ Met' on an account with no entries), a 14-day window that silently drops unconfirmed recurring payments, editor state bugs (Out→In saves income under Food; editing a transfer into a pot-to-pot move duplicates it), and a dead Payday picker. Root causes: no import pipeline (format detection → normalise → identity → categorise → reconcile), identity by display text instead of by source (FITID/balance/row hash), and master-detail layouts stacked on touch without changing the interaction.

**Coverage.** INVENTORY MATRIX (full table in audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/findings/money-goals.inventory.md). Sizes: mac 1470x832, ipad 820x1180, ipadl 1180x820 (touch threshold applied at every width this time), iphone 402x874; themes Graphite, Atelier Dawn (now renders: --theme works) and shop theme azure-butterfly. Accounts: seeded (+117 Money entries, 4 rules, 2 pots, 3 budgets) and empty (reset).
Views: Overview P mac/ipad/ipadl/iphone/Dawn, B low-data + chips → C12,C16, no-spend chip folded into the goals-leniency finding | Transactions P all sizes + azure, B filters/search/range/select/bulk/edit → C18,C19, new phone-selection, search, bulk Set category, Out→In editor, transfer edit | Budgets P mac/ipad/iphone, B inline edit, Edit budgets, rollover (verified OK: −20 rollover, effective 80), archive/restore, payday → new payday-picker, income-categories | Recurring P all, B due cards, confirm/skip/unmark, rule editor every unit/ends → C14, new 14-day window, row a11y, setPrice | Pots P mac/ipad/iphone, B move form (balance check OK), hero choice, close → C13, new closed-pot | Month P mac, B same-length compare, row links, export → C10,C11, new month links/export | Year P mac, B figures → new set-aside/income-line | Phone section switch → C8,C20 | Import dialog P mac/ipad/iphone, B 9 sample files through the real dialog (File on the input), Done-step undo (OK 3→0) → C0–C7,C9,C17, new identical-rows, own-export, odd amounts, lower-case i, 80-row cap | Export → new own-export round trip, CSV formula cells.
Engine fixtures verified OK: monthly dom 31 → last day, 29 Feb yearly, count/end dates, price history math, skip of a confirmed occurrence removes its entry, payday periods, rollover, splits must add up, refunds, Wishlist mirror (appears, cannot be deleted, Collection budget = Wishlist limit), notices (trial tomorrow, bill in 2 days, income late; figures dropped when hidden), set-aside per month (£111.43), subscriptions totals.

### MG-01 · P0 · data — Duplicate transactions after re-importing: de-dupe key includes payee, so a second import mapped differently is all 'new'

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Re-run on kos-redraw-1: importing the same two rows with Description→Payee then Description→Note gives preview {dups:0, rows:2} and both import again (stored: one row with payee=bank text, one with payee '' and the text in note — exactly the 'Other' twin in the user's screenshot). Same mapping re-imported: dups 2 (correctly caught). Key unchanged. — Exactly the user's screenshot: the same Heron Foods row twice, once titled with the payee and once titled 'Other' with the bank text as the subtitle. Reproduced: import a statement with Description->Payee, then the same file with Description->Note (or payee unmapped); preview reports 0 duplicates and every row imports again. The key is date|minor|payee.lower(), and an empty payee never equals the first import's payee. The second row reads 'Other' because txRow falls back to the category name when payee is empty and shows the note as the sub-line.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:1025-1031 (key date|minor|payee), js/modules/money.js:587,591; eval scratchpad t2.js: reimportNoteMapped {dups:0, rows:2}, reimportSame {dups:2}; shots/money-goals/tx-dups-all-mac.png
- **Root cause:** Dedupe depends on user-chosen mapping; raw source text not kept.
- **Proposed fix:** Key duplicates on date+amount+kind+normalised bank text (payee OR note OR raw description, stored as tx.raw), with the bank's own id (OFX FITID / balance-chain) when present; keep the raw description on every imported row; offer 'Replace the previous import of this period' in the preview when a batch overlaps.
- **Flags:** effort M

### MG-02 · P1 · integration — Santander midata CSV is refused: 'Merchant/Description' and 'Debit/Credit' headers are not recognised

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Through the REAL dialog (File set on the input): midata-comma.csv and midata-cp1252.csv both fail at step 1 with 'It has no header row with a date and an amount. Nothing was imported.' — the mapper that could fix it is never shown. — The midata export's header 'Date,Type,Merchant/Description,Debit/Credit,Balance' maps only Date; GUESS has no pattern for 'Merchant/Description' (payee) or 'Debit/Credit' (signed amount), so read() fails with 'It has no header row with a date and an amount.' before the user ever reaches the column mapper, even though the mapper could have fixed it by hand. Reproduced through KOS.money.csv.parse/guess on money-samples/midata-comma.csv: mapping {date:0}, dialogAccepts false.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:970-977 (GUESS), js/modules/money.js:937-940; dialog run over money-samples/midata-comma.csv, midata-cp1252.csv
- **Root cause:** Exact-match header regexes plus a hard gate before the manual mapper.
- **Proposed fix:** Add patterns (merchant/description, debit/credit, 'amount (£)', 'money in/out (£)'); and never hard-fail on unguessed headers: open the Columns step with the unmatched columns and let the user map them.
- **Flags:** effort S

### MG-03 · P1 · integration — Import only reads the first line as the header: midata with a leading blank line or a semicolon delimiter, and Online Banking CSV with an account preamble, all fail

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Dialog run: midata-semicolon.csv (blank first line, ';') and santander-online-excel.csv (Account:/From: preamble) refused with the same generic message. — parseCSV picks the delimiter from line 1 only (a leading blank line forces ','), and takes rows[0] as the header. Santander midata variants (';' delimited, trailing ';', blank first line) parse into one column; the Online Banking CSV/Excel export starts with 'Account:'/'From:' preamble lines so the header is 'Account:,Santander…'. All refused with the same generic message.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:947-969 (delimiter and header from line 1); dialog run over money-samples/midata-semicolon.csv, santander-online-excel.csv
- **Root cause:** Header = rows[0], delimiter sniffed from text.split(/\r?\n/)[0].
- **Proposed fix:** Detect the delimiter over the first ~10 non-empty lines; scan the first 20 rows for the first row that matches date+amount header patterns and treat everything above as preamble (show it as 'Skipped: 3 header lines'); drop trailing empty columns.
- **Flags:** effort S

### MG-04 · P1 · integration — Santander's other exports (.txt, QIF, OFX) are not supported at all; the picker accepts .txt but cannot read it

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Dialog run: santander-online.txt, santander.qif and santander.ofx all refused at step 1; the picker still accepts text/plain. — Online Banking 'Download transactions' offers text (Date:/Description:/Amount:/Balance: blocks with non-breaking spaces), Excel CSV, Quicken QIF and Microsoft Money OFX. The importer is CSV-only, yet the file input accepts text/plain, so the user's .txt is taken and fails with 'It has no header row with a date and an amount.' OFX would also give a stable FITID for exact de-duplication.
- **Evidence:** js/modules/money.js:889 (accept), js/core/money.js:947; dialog run over the three samples
- **Root cause:** Single CSV parser path.
- **Proposed fix:** Add format sniffing: OFX/QFX (parse STMTTRN, use FITID as the dedupe key, LEDGERBAL to reconcile), QIF (D/T/P/M/^ records), the Santander .txt block format; name the format detected in the Columns step. Keep CSV for everything else.
- **Flags:** effort M

### MG-05 · P1 · ux — No way to see, undo or replace an import after the result dialog closes

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Undo works only on the Done step (verified: 3 imported → Undo → 0). No other caller of undoBatch, no batch/source filter in list(), no select-all in the bulk bar. — Each import has a batch id, but 'Undo this import' exists only on the Done step of the dialog (money.js:915). Once closed there is no import history, no filter by source/batch in Transactions (list() filters kind/cat/tag/search only), and bulk select has no 'select all' over a range, so removing a bad 200-row import means ticking rows one by one.
- **Evidence:** js/modules/money.js:915-917 (only undo), js/core/money.js:1050-1056 (only definition), 690-712 (list keep(): kind/cat/tag/search); grep undoBatch: 2 hits
- **Root cause:** Batch metadata is not stored anywhere but on rows; UI only exposes it in a transient dialog.
- **Proposed fix:** An 'Imports' list (Transactions › Imports or Settings): file name, date range, rows, when imported, with Undo/Delete and 'Replace with a new file'. Store {batch, fileName, from, to, n, at} in state.money.imports. Add a Source filter and Select all in view.

### MG-06 · P1 · data — Unquoted thousands separators shift columns: '£1,234.56' imports silently as £1.00

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** parse of 'Date,Description,Amount,Balance' + '27/10/2026,STUDENT FINANCE,£1,234.56,£1,500.00' gives 6 cells for a 4-column header and previews as ['in', 100] (£1.00). — A comma-delimited bank file that writes amounts like £1,234.56 without quotes (common in hand-rolled UK exports, and what users get after re-saving midata in a text editor) splits the amount into two cells. The parser never checks a row's cell count against the header, so the Student Finance row imported as +£1.00 and the balance column swallowed '234.56'. No warning in the preview.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:947-969, 1005-1013; eval t2.js thousands: row ['27/10/2026','STUDENT FINANCE','£1','234.56','£1','500.00'] → pv [['in',100]]
- **Root cause:** Parser trusts column positions without validating row width.
- **Proposed fix:** Flag rows whose cell count differs from the header ('Row 3 has 6 cells, the header has 5'), and for the known Santander layout re-join a split £n,nnn.nn amount; show the running Balance column so a mismatch is visible.
- **Flags:** effort S

### MG-07 · P1 · data — A recurring rule's 'Confirm' and an imported bank row for the same payment double-count

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Fixture: rule 'Google One' £1.59 confirmed for 20 Jan, then a bank row '20/01/2027, GOOGLE *Google One, ON 19-01-2027, -1.59' previews duplicate:false and would import as a second £1.59. Seeded data shows the same for Student Finance (typed £450 on 27 Oct and the rule's 27 Oct occurrence still 'Due · 12 days ago' with a 'Received £450.00' button). — Confirming an occurrence (Google One £1.59, Phone £10) writes its own transaction r:<rule>:<date> with payee = rule name; importing the bank statement then adds 'GOOGLE *Google One, ON 27-10-2026' £1.59 as a separate row. Neither side looks at the other: preview's dedupe compares payee text ('google one' vs the bank string) and confirm() never searches existing transactions. Spend, budgets, Safe to spend and Reports count the payment twice. This is a second path to the duplicates the user saw.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:414-433, 1025-1031; eval t3.js confirmVsImport {dup:false}; #/money/recurring due card 'Student Finance · £450.00 | Due · 12 days ago'
- **Root cause:** Rules and imports are two independent writers of the same real-world payment.
- **Proposed fix:** On import, match rows to due occurrences (same amount ±0, date within ±3 days, payee alias set on the rule) and MARK the occurrence done pointing at the imported tx instead of creating a new one; on Confirm, offer 'Use the bank entry from 27 Oct' when one matches.
- **Flags:** effort M

### MG-23 · P1 · data — Two genuine identical payments on the same day in one statement: the second is marked 'Already have' and skipped by default

- **Independent check:** confirmed by Claude's independent re-check (B2, runtime + code)
- **Review note (8 Nov):** Mitigation: each flagged row has an 'Import anyway' toggle, but Skip is pre-selected and the row claims to match an entry that is not in the store.
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** previewCSV adds every row's key (date|amount|payee) to the seen set as it goes ('a repeat inside the same file is a duplicate too'), so two real card payments of the same amount at the same shop on the same day (two meal deals, two bus fares) are treated as one: the preview shows the second as '≈ Already have · matches an entry on 29 Oct' with Skip pre-selected, and Import imports one. Reproduced through the real dialog with midata-workaround.csv (two HERON FOODS -£3.45 rows on 29/10/2026 whose Balance column proves they are different: 120.10 vs 123.55): 'Preview 4 rows · 3 new · 1 look like ones you have', 'Import 3 entries'. Silent loss of real spending, and the totals under-report.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:1027-1031 (keys[k] = true inside the file loop); eval of the import dialog with money-samples/midata-workaround.csv: pv row 2 '≈ Already have … matches an entry on 29 Oct Skip'
- **Root cause:** Within-file repeats are deliberately folded into the duplicate set.
- **Proposed fix:** Compare file rows only against what is STORED, not against earlier rows of the same file; for stored matches count multiplicity (n identical rows in the file vs m stored) and only flag the surplus. With a balance column (or OFX FITID) use it as part of the identity.
- **Flags:** effort S

### MG-24 · P1 · data — Re-importing the app's own CSV export turns every outgoing into income and files the category as a note

- **Independent check:** confirmed by Claude's independent re-check (B2, runtime + code)
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Export CSV writes 'Date,Type,Amount,Category,Payee,Note,Tags,Pot' with unsigned amounts and the kind in Type. guessMapping maps Amount as a signed column (no minus = money IN), ignores Type, and maps 'Category' to Note (the note pattern includes 'category' and Category comes first). Round trip of October's export: all 40 rows previewed as kind 'in' (e.g. Steam £14.38 'in', note 'Other'); only the duplicate check (same device, same data) stops them importing. On another device, after a reset or after 'Delete all', importing your own export (the only Money backup a user sees) books every expense as income; transfers lose their pot and splits come back as separate entries.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:973-977 (note: /category/), 1005-1013 (sign from the minus), 1058-1076 (export unsigned + Type); eval: roundtrip kinds {in: 40}, pv[0] ['2026-10-01','in',1438,'Steam','Other']
- **Root cause:** Export and import were written independently; the importer has no notion of a direction column.
- **Proposed fix:** Recognise the app's own header exactly and import it losslessly (Type → kind, Category → cat by name, Pot → pot, Tags). Generally, offer a 'Type/Direction' column mapping (DEB/DD/SO/FPO = out, FPI/BGC/CR = in).
- **Flags:** effort M

### MG-17 · P2 · bug — Painted page header shows the PREVIOUS page's picture (Goals shows Money's jar, Money shows Goals' mountain)

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Sequence goals → money → … → goals → money/budgets: #/goals shows app.hero.page.money.webp, #/money shows app.hero.page.goals.webp, #/money/budgets after #/goals shows goals' picture; the same pages loaded from themselves show their own. — KOS.ui.pageHeader picks its art from KOS.store.state.ui.view, but KOS.show only sets ui.view AFTER the view function has rendered. So the first render of any page that relies on PAGE_ART draws the art of the page you came from; a redraw on the same page then corrects it. Reproduced: money -> goals gives app.hero.page.money.webp on Goals; goals -> money/budgets gives app.hero.page.goals.webp on Money. Affects every page in PAGE_ART (Review, Assignments, Exams, Pacing, Calendar, Reminders, Routines, Goals, Money, Wishlist, Governor, Reports, Archive...).
- **Evidence:** eval hdr.js imgs per route (mac and ipad); js/core/ui.js:589-592, 1540-1543; shots/money-goals/r2-goals-week-empty-mac.png (Money's jar on Goals)
- **Root cause:** Ordering in KOS.show: state.ui.view assigned after render.
- **Proposed fix:** Set KOS.store.state.ui.view (or a transient KOS.ui.rendering = viewId) before calling KOS.views[viewId], or have pageHeader take the view id from the router's current call.
- **Flags:** effort S

### MG-26 · P2 · data — Amounts written as (3.45) or 3.45 DR import as money in

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** toMinor strips everything but digits, '.', ',' and '-', so accountant notation '(3.45)' and suffixed '3.45 DR' become +3.45 and the row is previewed as '+£3.45' income; '3.45-' (trailing minus) is rejected as 'no amount'. Statements and spreadsheet re-saves use these notations. Dates written with a month name ('06 Oct 2026', as Nationwide and many PDFs-to-CSV tools write them) are rejected as 'No date I can read'.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:63-70; dialog preview of money-samples/odd-amounts.csv: 'PAREN NEG +£3.45', 'DR SUFFIX +£3.45', row 5 'no amount'
- **Root cause:** toMinor only knows a leading minus.
- **Proposed fix:** In toMinor treat (x), trailing '-', 'DR'/'CR' and 'D'/'C' suffixes as signs; flag any row whose sign was inferred.
- **Flags:** effort S

### MG-27 · P2 · bug — Editing a transfer into a move between two pots keeps the original and adds two new entries

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** In the entry editor, save() handles 'pot → pot' by calling addTx twice and returns before the existing/updateTx branch, so editing an existing transfer (e.g. the £120 Main → New laptop top-up) to 'New laptop → Emergency' leaves the original untouched and adds an out and an in. Reproduced through Transactions → select → Edit → From/To → Save: transfers went from 1 to 3 entries.
- **Evidence:** js/modules/money.js:814-821 (early return before line 832 updateTx); eval: before [[2026-10-28,laptop,in,12000]] after adds [laptop,out,12000],[emergency,in,12000]
- **Root cause:** The between-pots path was written for new entries only.
- **Proposed fix:** When editing, turn the existing entry into one half (updateTx) and add only the other; or delete the original in the same step with an undo.
- **Flags:** effort S

### MG-29 · P2 · data — Recurring: an occurrence left unconfirmed for more than 14 days disappears; older months are never offered

### MG-30 · P2 · data — Money goals are met with no evidence: 'No-spend days' counts days with no entries at all, and 'Spend under' is met by an empty month

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** money-no-spend counts every day of the period up to today on which no 'out' entry exists, so on an account with zero Money entries a weekly '5 no-spend days' goal created today reads '✓ Met · 7 of 5 days · Met. Nothing more to do here.' (it also counts days before the goal existed). money-spend-under reads 0 spent for a month with no entries and will be judged met at the end of the period. A user who simply did not log spending is told they kept their goal, and the outcome is stored in the goal's history. The Overview makes the same claim: its chip read '7 no-spend days' on a month with entries on one day, while Safe to spend in the same hero says it needs 7 days WITH entries — the two disagree about what an empty day means.
- **Evidence:** js/core/goals.js:680-711; empty account (reset), goals added via KOS.goals.add: #/goals text '✓ Met | 5 no-spend days | 7 | of 5 days | Met. Nothing more to do here.' and 'Your run … 2 met this week'; shots/money-goals/r2-goals-thin-mac.png; shots/money-goals/r2-overview-dawn-mac.png (chip '7 no-spend days', '1 day so far')
- **Root cause:** Absence of data is read as absence of spending.
- **Proposed fix:** Require evidence that Money is in use for the period (entries on at least N days, or an import covering the range) before judging; otherwise read 'Not enough entries to judge'. Start counting from the goal's creation day.
- **Flags:** effort S

- **Evidence:** js/modules/money.js:1067 (out only), 1119-1131 (actions per out row), 1188-1190 (budget field regardless of kind); js/core/money.js:113 (in → budget null)
- **Proposed fix:** Add an 'Income categories' card on Budgets' side (rename, colour, archive), and hide the budget field when Income is picked.
- **Flags:** effort S

### MG-40 · P3 · ux — Month and year: a past month's category row opens Transactions on 'Everything', and Export CSV ignores the month on screen

- **Devices:** all

The page's Export CSV opens the shared dialog whose 'This view' is Transactions' range (txRange), not the month or year being looked at, and 'This month' is today's month.

### MG-41 · P3 · content — Year view: 'Set aside · 2 pots' counts every open pot, and the dashed income line carries no amount

- **Devices:** all

The chart's subtitle promises 'income where it was recorded, as the dashed line', but .k-mn-yin is only a marker at the baseline under months with any income: its amount is not drawn, so income cannot be compared with spending (Aug in ≈ £700 vs out £264).

### MG-42 · P3 · bug — A subscription's price rise can never be recorded: setPrice has no caller, and editing the amount re-prices past occurrences

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.money keeps a price history (prices, setPrice, priceChange) and the Overview and Recurring draw '▲ Up from … more a year' from it, but nothing in the app or the Assistant calls setPrice. Changing the amount in the rule editor overwrites minor, so every unconfirmed past occurrence now shows the new price and the price-rise notice never appears.

### MG-43 · P3 · ux — Import preview shows only the first 80 rows without saying so

- **Devices:** all

A year's statement can only be checked for its first 80 rows; duplicates and unreadable rows further down cannot be seen or toggled (their 'Import anyway' choice is unreachable). Cannot-read rows are appended after the 80, so they are listed but the duplicates past 80 are not.

### MG-44 · P3 · bug — CSV export does not neutralise cells that start with = + - @ (bank descriptions can carry formulas into Excel)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** csvCell only quotes cells containing quote, comma, newline or ';'. Payees come straight from imported bank text (merchant-controlled), so a description such as '=HYPERLINK(…)' is written as a live formula when the export is opened in Excel/Numbers.
- **Evidence:** js/core/money.js:1057 (csvCell), js/modules/money.js:1039-1046 (selection export, same rule)
- **Proposed fix:** Prefix a single quote (or a tab) to cells beginning with = + - @, as OWASP recommends for CSV export.
- **Flags:** effort S

- A 'Not yet confirmed' queue for Recurring covering every past occurrence, with Confirm all / Skip all and automatic matching to imported rows.

## GO — Goals: every goal type's measurement, editor, notices, joins (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** The Goals engine is well structured (one registry, one compute, pure notices) and the range-reading types (Study hours, Focus, cards, Code, Creatives, repeating Money) measure exactly the period with pre-start sessions excluded, and exam-linked goals follow, unlink and archive as invariant 128 says. The big problems are in what the editor promises versus what types can read: UR-20 is verified (every Collection type except spend-below reads the whole vault, so goals are Met at once, write receipts and farm the Goal getter badge), state types (streaks, no-overdue, subscriptions) get start dates and are judged at the moment of looking, and UR-22's lenient RAG completes 'Move topics to Green' from failing quizzes. Several types are unusable from the UI: routine goals have no routine picker, the habit picker reads the frozen pre-Routines list, and editing a title goal silently relinks it. Repeating goals count the days before their start and keep stale period history when their grid changes; completion is sticky through edits. Presentation is solid on mac and iPad; the phone list hides deadlines/pace/actions, the template rows balloon to 180px, and the chart labels shrink to ~6px.

**Coverage.** Slot 15, build sw kos-redraw-1, today Thu 5 Nov 2026. Empty account and seeded account (and an empty account with a hand-made fixture). Sizes: mac 1470x832 (list all/week/done, goal pages weekly/collection-met/exam, editor), ipad 820x1180 (list), iphone 402x874 (list, goal page, editor, Home card). DOM measurement (overflow, clipping, small targets, ovals) run on the list at all three sizes.
MATRIX (type -> presentation / behaviour -> result):
study-hours: card+page mac/ipad/iphone / fixture (pre-start, untagged, media, incomplete Focus) -> OK except GO-03 (repeat first period);
cards-reviewed, recall-rate: card / fixture (subject filter, 50-review floor) -> GO-11;
topics-green: card ipad / fixture (one 0% quiz per leaf; subject edit) -> GO-23 (UR-22), GO-24;
study-paper-score, study-finish-unit: card mac / code read only -> OK by reading, NOT exercised with tracker data;
focus-hours, focus-blocks: card / fixture -> OK;
todos-done: fixture (todo, external, routine) -> OK (external batch counts once: noted, no finding);
plan-ticked, carryovers-cleared: code read only -> carryovers in GO-08; plan-ticked NOT exercised;
habit-streak: editor mac / fixture -> GO-07; routine-days, routine-streak: editor / fixture -> GO-06;
no-overdue: fixture (flip, deadline) -> GO-08; money-subs-under: default deadline checked -> GO-08;
money-spend-under: card ipad, editor mac/iphone / seeded months -> GO-18, GO-22; money-income: code only, OK by reading; money-no-spend: code -> GO-18; money-save: editor code read (no pots in seed) -> NOT exercised;
code-tasks, code-retrievals: fixture (seen/topup/again excluded) -> OK; code-capstone: code read -> OK by reading;

Engine: repeat week/month + weekFrom + closePeriods + run -> GO-03, GO-04; sticky completion/edit -> GO-05; receipts + Achievements goal-getter -> GO-02; notices via real tick() (done, due tomorrow) -> GO-10 (code), GO-05 evidence; Reports f.goals -> GO-09 (code only); Home switch -> GO-20; pins/Morning Review -> GO-26; search -> GO-21; list/hero -> GO-01, GO-12, GO-13, GO-14, GO-19; goal page -> GO-16, GO-17.

### GO-02 · P1 · bug — UR-20 verified: Collection goal types read the whole vault, so a goal starting today is Met at once and pays the Goal getter badge

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Fixture on the seeded account (today Thu 5 Nov): goals with startDate 2026-11-05 and deadline 2026-12-15 measured titles-completed 222/10 (completed), library-size 1880/100, episodes-watched 13326/100, chapters-read 21735/100, game-hours 3115/100 (all 'completed' on the day they were made); favourites 82, purchases 7 and routes-cleared 16 are all-time counts too. Six seeded goals were completed on first compute, wrote six completionLedger receipts and earned achievement goal-getter tier 1 at once (state.achievements.earned['goal-getter']). Because remove() leaves the ledger entry and the badge counts ledger rows, creating and deleting such goals farms Goal getter's 10 and 50 tiers, which invariant 162 never takes back. The editor still offers Starts and Deadline and draws a pace line for these types, promising a range. Of the 13 Collection types only spend-below reads the range (specific-title/finish-series read one title by design).
- **Evidence:** eval fx1/seed compute: rows 'titles-completed | 222 | 10 | completed', 'library-size | 1880 | 100 | completed', 'episodes-watched | 13326 | 100 | completed'; completionLedger ids 1,2,4,5,6,9; achievements.earned goal-getter tier 1; js/core/goals-collection.js:49-53,54-57,87-94 (mods() reads mediadb.stats aggregate); js/core/goals.js:438-441 (receipt + achievements.touch); js/modules/goals.js:892 (Starts/Deadline offered for every non-repeat type); js/core/achcatalogue.js:461-462; after deleting and recreating fixture goals the ledger held 13 receipts for 2 live goals and Goal getter II (10 goals) unlocked (screenshot shots/goals/routine-days-saved-mac.png)
- **Root cause:** goals-collection.js types were moved unchanged from Collection Goals v2, which measured vault state, while the v3 editor gives every type a start date and a pace line
- **Proposed fix:** Measure the period from the media activity journal (mediadb journal [ts,kind,from,to], invariant 99): completions/status->completed, progress/volume/hour deltas and favourites added with ts in [start, deadline]; purchases by purchasedAt (as spend-below already does); library-size by createdAt. Then mark these types repeat-capable. Until then, record a baseline at creation (onCreate, as topics-green does) and measure the delta. Decide with the user whether goal-getter earned this way is revoked (needs an explicit exception to invariant 162).
- **Flags:** effort M

### GO-06 · P1 · bug — 'Keep a routine on N days' and 'A routine's streak' can never be linked to a routine: the editor has no routine field

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Both routine goal types are offered under Productivity in New goal, but goalDialog draws no routine picker (nothing in js/modules/goals.js reads or writes params.routine), so Save stores params {} and the goal measures 'No routine linked' forever (current null, status active). Reproduced: with two routines (Stretch habit, Evening wind-down) the routine-days editor shows Title, Target, Repeats, Starts, Deadline and Milestones only; the saved goal computes [null, 'No routine linked', 'active']. No other surface (Routines pages) creates these goals either (grep routine-days/routine-streak: only js/core/routines.js:752-764).
- **Evidence:** eval: editor text 'Keep a routine on N days ... Title Target Repeats ... Starts Deadline · optional Milestones' and saved params '{}'; compute -> ['Keep a routine on N days', null, 'No routine linked', 'active']; js/core/routines.js:750-764; js/modules/goals.js:828-902 (no routine field)
- **Root cause:** types registered by routines.js after the editor was built; the editor only knows fields it hard-codes
- **Proposed fix:** Add a fields.routine flag to both types and a Routine select (KOS.routines.all(), including Daily habits) in goalDialog that writes params.routine; refuse Save without one. Offer 'Make this a goal' from a routine's page.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-07 · P1 · bug — 'A habit's streak' lists habits from the frozen pre-Routines store, so habits made in Routines can't be picked

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all

With a habit added through KOS.routines.addHabit('Stretch'), the select had zero options; saving stores params.habit undefined and the goal reads 'No habit linked'. For the user (migrated 26 Oct) the list shows only the habits frozen at migration, including ones since removed, while the measure resolves through KOS.routines (goals.js:641-646). habit-streak also duplicates routine-streak.

### GO-23 · P1 · bug — UR-22 verified through Goals: one 0% quiz per topic turns five topics Green and completes 'Move topics to Green' at once

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Empty account: a 'Move topics to Green' goal on five Maths leaves (baseline 0). Logging one quiz attempt at 0% on each leaf makes KOS.rag.effective return band 'g' for all five (auto() starts at 100 and the quiz penalty is capped at 25, so 0% -> 75 = Green), and the goal computes 5/5 'completed' with an activity-only receipt and an achievements touch. Exam goals 'Topics green or covered' (scopeCount) and Exams readiness coverage read the same band, so they are met by failing quizzes too.
- **Evidence:** eval fx8: bands ['g','g','g','g','g'] after study.quiz[k]={attempts:1,lastPct:0}; goal '5|5|completed'; completionLedger receipt {type:'topics-green',payout:'activity-only'}; js/modules/rag.js:29-90 (score from 100, quiz cap 25, Green >= 70); js/core/goals.js:534-546, 574-581; js/core/goals-exams.js:58-66
- **Root cause:** rag.js auto() subtracts capped penalties from 100 with no evidence floor
- **Proposed fix:** Fix RAG as UR-22 proposes (evidence-weighted score, minimum evidence before any band, Green only when recall and practice both clear their bar). In Goals, count a leaf only when its band rests on enough evidence (e.g. rag.auto(...).evidence >= threshold) and judge topics-green on the deadline (hold) rather than on first touch.
- **Flags:** effort M

### GO-25 · P1 · bug — Editing a title goal silently relinks it to another title; only the first 60 in-progress titles can ever be linked

- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The Linked title select of 'Complete a specific title' / 'Finish a series' lists only titles with status inProgress, alphabetically, capped at 60. Editing a goal whose title is now completed (or planned, on hold, or past the 60th) leaves its own title out of the list, so the browser selects the first option and Save rewrites linkedEntryId. Reproduced: goal 'Finish Zzz' linked to entry 2 (completed); Edit then Save without touching anything -> linkedEntryId 1 ('Aaa Watching'). It also means a planned title can't be a goal ('finish X before December') and a user with more than 60 titles in progress can't pick most of them.
- **Evidence:** eval: options ['1:Aaa Watching'], selected '1', goal.linkedEntryId 2 -> 1 after Save; js/modules/goals.js:864-871, 955
- **Root cause:** select filled from a filtered, capped query without the current value
- **Proposed fix:** Always include the goal's current title as the selected option; replace the capped select with a search picker over the whole vault (any status), as the Collection's own pickers do.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-03 · P2 · bug — Repeating goals count activity from before the goal started in their first period (week and month)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** A weekly Study-hours goal (target 2 h, week Mon-Sun) started Wed 14 Oct: its first outcome is the week of Mon 12 Oct and it was judged MET from 2 h logged on Tue 13 Oct, the day before it existed. A monthly goal started 20 Oct judged October as 15 h, counting 10 h from 5 Oct and 2 h from 13 Oct. closePeriods begins at periodOf(g, g.startDate) and measures the whole period, and the live period's measure does the same. Same UR-20 class: things done before the start count.
- **Evidence:** eval fx2: weekly outcomes {'2026-10-12':{met:true,value:2}} with startDate 2026-10-14 and the only Oct 12-18 session dated 2026-10-13; monthly outcomes {'2026-10':{met:true,value:15}} with startDate 2026-10-20; js/core/goals.js:379-397 (closePeriods), 418-419 (from = per.from)
- **Root cause:** period ranges ignore startDate
- **Proposed fix:** Clamp each period's from to max(per.from, g.startDate) when measuring (and prorate or mark the first partial period 'partial' so a 3-day first week is not judged against a 7-day target), or start the first period at the next boundary.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-04 · P2 · bug — Changing a repeating goal's 'week runs' or its repeat keeps the old periods: history fills with overlapping weeks and months

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Editing a weekly goal from Monday-weeks to 'From the day it starts' (Wednesday) kept the three Monday-keyed outcomes and added three Wednesday-keyed ones, so 'Every week so far' shows six periods for three weeks (2026-10-12, -14, -19, -21, -26, -28) and the run is computed across both. Switching the same goal from Every week to Every month kept all six week keys and added '2026-10'. update() only merges outcomes when repeat is unchanged, but normalise keeps raw.outcomes whatever the repeat, and weekFrom changes are not considered at all.
- **Evidence:** eval fx2 wStart.outcomes (6 keys); eval fx3 after repeat:'month' -> keys ['2026-10-12','2026-10-14','2026-10-19','2026-10-21','2026-10-26','2026-10-28','2026-10'], run 2; js/core/goals.js:162-168 (normalise keeps outcomes), 266 (merge on same repeat)
- **Root cause:** outcomes keyed by period start are carried across a change of period grid
- **Proposed fix:** When repeat or weekFrom changes, drop (or archive under a separate key) outcomes whose keys do not match the new period grid, and re-judge from startDate; say so in the editor ('the history restarts').
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-05 · P2 · bug — A met goal stays 'Met' after its target is raised or a manual count is lowered (10% shown as Met)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** A manual goal nudged to 3/3 completes; nudging to 1 keeps 'completed'; editing the target to 10 keeps 'completed' with _pct 10, so Done lists it as Met at 1 of 10. derive() returns 'completed' whenever g.status==='completed' && completedAt, and update() never clears it when the target, type link or dates change. The same holds for an auto goal edited after completion (e.g. a UR-20 goal whose target the user raises to fix it stays Met). There is also no -1 or undo for a manual goal's +1 (only '+1' in actionFor) and no Reopen in the UI (G.reopen is unused), so a mis-tap cannot be corrected except by Restart, which wipes the start date.
- **Evidence:** eval fx2: man {st:'completed'} -> after nudge -2 {st:'completed',cur:1} -> after target 10 {st:'completed',cur:1,tgt:10,pct:10}; js/core/goals.js:305 (sticky completed), 259-272 (update), js/modules/goals.js:243 (+1 only); grep: reopen not referenced in js/modules/goals.js; tick(): notice 'goal:3:done | Goal reached — Finish Zzz | 0 of 1 title' after the goal's link changed
- **Root cause:** completion is sticky by design for evidence types but edits are not treated as a new judgement
- **Proposed fix:** In update(), if target/type/links/startDate/deadline change on a completed goal, re-derive (clear completedAt; keep the ledger receipt so nothing is paid twice). Give manual goals a stepper (-1/+1 or a 'Set count' field in Edit) and an Undo toast after +1.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-08 · P2 · bug — Stay-under goals on live state (No overdue assignment, Carry-overs cleared, Subscriptions below) flip between Missed and active and are judged only at the moment they are looked at

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Fixture: a 'No overdue assignment' goal for 1-30 Nov with 3 overdue assignments is 'failed' the moment it is made (before its deadline), then goes back to 'active' (failedAt cleared) once overdue reads 0, then, with the deadline moved to yesterday while overdue was 0 for one compute, becomes 'completed' and stays completed (sticky) after overdue returns to 3. So a month with overdue work every day except the last look is Met, and a breach early in the month is forgotten. The measure reads KOS.assignments.counts() / pacing.dueThisWeek() / subscriptions() NOW, not over [start, deadline]; derive() treats current<=target at the first compute after the deadline as success. add() also gives every such goal a deadline of month end silently.
- **Evidence:** eval fx5: a '3|failed|failed|1' -> b (overdue 0) '0|active|active|0|under' -> c (deadline 2026-11-04) '0|completed' -> d (overdue 3 again) '3|completed'; js/core/goals.js:656-674 (live measures), 307-311 (under-direction derive), 251 (month-end default)
- **Root cause:** state types are judged like range counts
- **Proposed fix:** For live stay-under types, record a breach (first day current>target inside the range) into params and judge from it: failed once breached (or 'held N of M days'), completed only if never breached by the deadline. Alternatively derive from history: assignments' due/submitted dates give overdue days in the range.
- **Flags:** effort M

### GO-11 · P2 · bug — 'Review flashcards' and 'Keep recall' offer Japanese, Mind and Code but never count their reviews

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The subject select of cards-reviewed and recall-rate lists every subject (All, CS, Maths, IT, Code, Japanese, Mind, Creatives), but the measure reads only ledger entries of type 'flashcards' or 'due-review'. Japanese reviews are logged as type 'ja' and Mind's review blocks as type 'mind' (with metrics.cards), Code's retrievals as type 'code', so a 'Review 200 Japanese cards this week' goal stays at 0 forever, and 'All subjects' silently leaves those reviews out.

- **Root cause:** measure hard-codes two session types while the editor lists KOS.subjects.ids()
- **Proposed fix:** Count review sessions by kind across owners (flashcards, due-review, ja reviews, mind reviews, Code retrievals) or restrict the select to subjects whose reviews the measure reads; the same review-log rows (KOS.reviewLog, src per owner) could be the single source.

### GO-12 · P2 · ui — iPhone: 'Aim at something new' template rows are 180px tall for one line of text

- **Detail / repro:** On the dense Goals page at 402px each of the three template rows in the 'Aim at something new' tile is 322x180 with a single 12.5px line, so the tile is ~650px of mostly empty boxes. ### GO-13 · P2 · ux — iPhone: goal cards hide the deadline, the pace chip and the action button

- **Devices:** iphone
- **Detail / repro:** Under 700px the card's band top (pace chip: Behind / Too early / Display only) and footer ('3 days left · by Sun 8 Nov', and the action: Start focus, Review, Today's Daily 20, +1 for a manual goal) are display:none. On the phone list a goal therefore shows neither when it ends nor whether it is behind, and a manual goal's +1 is only reachable by opening it. Only the hero keeps them.
- **Evidence:** shots/goals/dense-all-iphone.png; eval (iphone): hidden ['k-gl-bandtop','k-gl-cardfoot'], card text 'Focus blocks by Sunday 5 of 30 blocks 25 to go.'; css/views/goals.css:229,233
- **Root cause:** phone rule hides parts instead of recomposing them
- **Proposed fix:** Keep a compact one-line foot on phone (pace chip + 'n days left') and the action as an icon button, instead of hiding both.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-24 · P2 · bug — Editing a 'Move topics to Green' goal's subject or topics keeps the old baseline, so it can be met instantly

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** topics-green records params.baseline (green topics at creation) in onCreate, and update() only re-runs onCreate when the TYPE changes. A goal made for IT (baseline 0) and edited to Maths, where 5 leaves are already green, reads 5 new green topics and completes 5/3 on the spot; the reverse edit leaves it unreachable. Same for exam_recall/exam_topics_green baselines when relinked to another exam (linkExam does not re-baseline).
- **Evidence:** eval fx8: g2 baseline 0 (IT) -> update links {subject:'maths'} -> '5|3|completed|5 green now|0'; js/core/goals.js:268 (onCreate only on type change), 574-576; js/core/goals.js:849-855 (linkExam)
- **Proposed fix:** Re-run def.onCreate (re-baseline) in update()/linkExam whenever links, refs, subject or params that the measure reads change, before computing; tell the user 'counting from now'.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-27 · P2 · ux — Projected-recall goal with too little data shows '–' and a meaningless 'The line says 4.3%', without saying why

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** A template-made 'CS Paper 1 mock recall ≥ 95%' goal on an account with no rated cards: recallNow() is thin, so onCreate stores baseline 0 and the page shows SO FAR '–' beside THE LINE SAYS '4.3 % by today' (a straight line from 0% to 95% across the weeks), which no recall figure can follow. The reason the measure is empty ('Appears after 20 rated cards in scope…', the measure's meta) appears nowhere on the goal page, and the page has no action (the list card's 'Review' button is not repeated here).
- **Evidence:** shots/goals/detail-exam-mac.png; eval: page text has no 'Appears after'/'20 rated cards' and no 'Review'; js/core/goals-exams.js:111-121 (baseline 0 when thin), js/core/goals.js:474 (_expected drawn whenever reach + not noPace); js/modules/goals.js:548-560
- **Proposed fix:** When the baseline is unknown (thin), store null and draw no line until the first measured figure becomes the baseline; print _meta under '–' on the goal page and add the type's action (examAction/actionFor) to the page header.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-01 · P3 · ui — First-goal template grid leaves an empty sixth column at 1470 (auto-fill)

- **Devices:** mac
- **Detail / repro:** On an empty account, #/goals at mac width shows the five templates in a grid of six 186px tracks, so a sixth empty track (~196px) sits at the right of the card: dead width the user standing rule forbids.
- **Evidence:** shots/goals/empty-all-mac.png; eval: .k-gl-tpls gridTemplateColumns = 186px x6 with 5 children; css/views/goals.css:138 repeat(auto-fill, minmax(var(--gl-tpl-min),1fr))
- **Root cause:** auto-fill keeps empty tracks; auto-fit collapses them
- **Proposed fix:** Use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...,1fr)) so the five tiles stretch across the card (or cap columns at the template count).
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-09 · P3 · data — Reports drop repeating-goal periods that straddle a report boundary (weeks from a weekday, payday months)

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** goalFacts counts an outcome in the report whose range holds the period's START key. A weekly goal whose week runs from its start day (e.g. Wed-Tue) has key Wed 4 Nov; the week report for 2-8 Nov is built on Mon 9 Nov, before that period ends (Tue 10), so it has no outcome yet, and the 9-15 Nov report skips the key because 4 Nov is outside it: that period is never reported. A Money goal's month follows Money's month start (periodOf uses KOS.money.periodRange), so a payday month starting the 25th has the same gap in month reports. Read from code; not reproduced in a saved report.
- **Evidence:** js/core/report.js:698-711 (day = period key, kept only if p.start<=day<=p.end); js/core/goals.js:63-81 (weekFrom 'start' keys, money periods)
- **Root cause:** outcome keyed by start, report built when the period may still be open
- **Proposed fix:** Attribute an outcome to the report whose range holds the period's END (or the judgement date at), so every period lands exactly once after it has been judged.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-10 · P3 · bug — A stay-under goal breached early never sends its 'Goal missed' notice

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** tick() only pushes ':missed' while now - failedAt < 2 days (NEWS_MS). A stay-under goal (spend below, no overdue) is marked failed the day it goes over, but notices() only emits ':missed' once the deadline has passed; by then failedAt is usually more than two days old, so the notice is dropped and the month-end miss is silent. Similarly, a goal restarted after completion reuses the id 'goal:<id>:done', so its second completion is deduped by the ledger within 45 days.
- **Evidence:** js/core/goals.js:818-820 (missed only after deadline), 864-873 (at = failedAt, dropped when older than NEWS_MS); fx5 shows failedAt set on creation day for no-overdue
- **Root cause:** news window measured from the status change, not from the event the notice reports
- **Proposed fix:** Use the deadline (or max(failedAt, deadline)) as the news time for ':missed'; key ':done' by completedAt day or the restart's startDate.
- **Flags:** effort S

### GO-18 · P3 · data — Spend-below goals are judged Met for months with no Money records at all

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** A monthly 'Spend below £60' goal started 1 Sep on an account with no transactions shows two met periods (✓✓) and 'Under'. The measure returns 0 spent whenever the range has no rows, so months before Money was used, or when nothing was imported, count as kept; the 'Under budget' badge logic and Reports' periods met read the same outcomes. Invariant 76 asks for no claim without evidence. money-no-spend has the same flaw: every day without a recorded 'out' transaction counts as a no-spend day, so a user who does not log daily meets 'No-spend days' automatically (js/core/goals.js:700-710).

- **Proposed fix:** Treat a period with no transactions (or before the first one) as 'no evidence' (current null) so it is not judged; say 'No spending recorded' instead.

## EX — Exams hub, Files, ink/Pencil surfaces (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** The Exams & Deadlines hub, Files and the ink engine are functionally sound at their cores. Scope exclusions, linking and unlinking result attempts, redo items, file dedupe by hash, skip reports, PDF text search, scan-to-PDF and pen strokes with undo and redo all behaved correctly under fixtures. Most problems are in presentation on the touch devices: the timed paper's question navigator is crushed to 7px slivers (flex items with no flex-shrink:0), the iPhone ink palette is 500px wide on a 402px screen, the iPhone Exam Room checklist overlaps, and in Side by side the docked ink bar hides Undo. Judgement and wording problems: start-by rounds every run-up up to whole weeks plus a buffer, so short-notice tests are created already 'passed'; Thin bands still name a 'limiting' signal; the Calendar's sample mock is migrated into a real assessment on a fresh account; hard-coded or raw values reach the screen ('Start the rapid drill · 15' with 0 items, '40 of null.'). Structural causes: one global ink tool pref that strips don't clamp, three separate file-size formatters, fixed-width grid columns sized for a letter or a short number, and dialogs that are not closed on navigation.

**Coverage.** Seeded and empty accounts. A DOM measurement script ran over 25 hub/Files/Pen routes at mac (1470x832), ipad (820x1180) and iphone (402x874) on the seeded account, and over 17 routes on the empty account at iPad. Screenshots were taken and examined for: assessment page (Dawn), Season (Mac), Results (iPad, Mac), Library, Scope, Load, Full Companion (iPad), Guide (Mac, empty iPad), timed mode (iPad landscape, iPhone), the tally dialog, post-mortem, assessment editor, Files (iPad, iPhone, menu, chips), Scan pages (empty and with a photo), Storage, Pen and ink (Dawn), Handwritten docked/drawn/ruler/Side by side (iPad landscape), answer pad Type/Write (iPad), iPhone palette re-check, timetable in Dawn and azure-butterfly. Behaviour was exercised by fixture through real UI or KOS APIs, as listed in the matrix. The full item → presentation → behaviour → result matrix and the explicit NOT-checked list are in /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/findings/exams-files-ink.inventory.md. Findings 1-27 in the jsonl come from the earlier interrupted auditor, whose evidence paths point at an earlier scratchpad; this pass re-verified its iPhone palette P1 (palette 500x62 at x=20 on a 402px viewport). NOT checked: the Trend page and Playbook visuals, the recognition drill, pack/set papers, print, the import and goal-template dialogs, PDF viewer layers/pins/clip/Ask, the Share Target, the camera, cloud sync of files and ink, lasso/shape/text/image/eraser modes, export, gestures needing real touch, and AI marking. A duplicate of the app-wide 16px-input finding (already filed by the a11y-hci audit) was not filed again.
