### DI-08 · P2 · data — A 404 on an update deletes the local event or reminder (e.g. after reconnecting a different Google account)

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** When a PATCH to Google Calendar or Google Tasks answers 404/410, the cycle deletes the LOCAL record inside inbound(): extgcal.js:421 KOS.calendar.deleteEvent(ev.id), exttasks.js:417 KOS.reminders.remove(it.id). disconnect() (ext.js:241-250) clears only the kv (sync tokens, mirrors) and leaves every record's ext link in place, so connecting a different Google account (or the event being moved to another calendar) turns the next local edit of any linked event or reminder into a silent local deletion, with no undo and no notice. This contradicts the 'never inferred from absence' intent of invariant 158 and is the opposite of Todoist's behaviour (an update to a missing item there is just retried forever, exttasks.js:330-333).
- **Evidence:** Re-read 7 Nov: unchanged since 56b1a8c except ext.js:364 (background redraw); Google Tasks path now at exttasks.js:419 (r.status === 404 → KOS.reminders.remove). Original: js/core/extgcal.js:419-421, js/core/exttasks.js:416-417, js/core/ext.js:241-250
- **Root cause:** A failed write is treated as proof of a remote deletion.
- **Proposed fix:** On 404 for an update, unlink the record (ext = null, keep it local, count it as 'unlinked' in the status) instead of deleting it; delete locally only from a pull that reports the item cancelled/deleted. Clear (or archive) ext links on disconnect and on connecting a different account (compare the account id).
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-09 · P2 · data — The full backup leaves out saved Reports and snapshots, and builds one giant string that can fail on the iPad

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** ipad, iphone
- **Detail / repro:** store.snapshotFull collects state, media, attachments (kurenai-os-files, every binary as base64), money, reviews, mind, ink and creatives, but not kurenai-os-reports (saved weeks/months/terms/years, their Kurenai words and the boundary snapshots that status moves need — 'never recomputed', invariant 101/102). Signed out, a restore on a new device loses every saved report and snapshot for good. The backup is serialised with JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) into a single Blob: with a few hundred MB of files (the app asks for persistent storage at 200 MB) the base64 plus indentation is a string of several hundred MB, which risks an out-of-memory reload on iPad Safari, and that failure is silent (no error reaches done()). A failing sub-export (e.g. creatives) aborts the whole backup instead of reporting the missing part.
- **Evidence:** Re-run 7 Nov in browser (slot 19, seeded): 11 saved reports + 1 snapshot on the device; snapshotFull keys have no 'reports'; size 3,078,746 chars with no attachments; restore report lists 7 sections and never mentions Reports. Original: js/core/store.js:513-583 (no reportStore step; JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) at 588), js/core/reportstore.js (no exportAll), js/modules/attachments.js:454-480 (base64 for every blob)
- **Root cause:** Backup coverage list maintained by hand; whole-document serialisation.
- **Proposed fix:** Add KOS.reportStore.exportAll/importAll to the snapshot; stream the backup (build the Blob from parts: a JSON head plus one part per file, no indentation) or offer 'backup without files' when files exceed ~100 MB; report per-section failures like importFull does instead of failing the whole export.
- **Flags:** effort M

### DI-10 · P2 · data — The whole state lives in one localStorage key with no fallback: when it outgrows the quota every later change is lost on reload

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all, iPhone/iPad Safari first
- **Detail / repro:** Measured on the seeded account: the state document is 372,924 characters in one key (kurenai-os-v1); srs is 110 KB for 675 rated cards (164 B a card), sessions 84 KB for 600 (140 B each, capped at 2,000), pacing 85 KB. The curriculum alone has 5,436 flashcards, so a fully reviewed deck is ~0.9 MB before Code, Japanese facets and Mind cards, and every new domain adds to the same document. Chrome refused the write at ~5.2 M characters total; WebKit's limit is of the same order. When setItem throws, save() shows one toast ('Save failed — storage may be full. Export your data.') and keeps running on the in-memory copy; every later change, and the pagehide flush (which only logs, store.js:417-425), is lost on the next reload or when iOS evicts the page. Reproduced by filling localStorage on the slot: the save failed with QuotaExceededError and the change was not stored. There is no size readout in Archive › Storage for the state document, and no migration of the big parts (srs, sessions, facets) to IndexedDB.
- **Evidence:** Re-measured 7 Nov: seeded 372,887 chars (srs 110,391; pacing 84,696; sessions 84,052), empty 96,139; tight quota fill → console 'save failed QuotaExceededError … kurenai-os-v1 exceeded the quota', the reminder not stored until space was freed and flush() ran. Original: kos.mjs eval 17 → state 372,924 chars; srs 110,391; sessions 84,052; pacing 84,696; 5,436 curriculum cards; quota experiment → errs ['Kurenai OS: save failed QuotaExceededError…'], stored:false, toast 'Save failed — storage may be full. Export your data.'; js/core/store.js:395-425
- **Root cause:** Single-key localStorage persistence for an unbounded document.
- **Proposed fix:** Move the large, append-heavy parts (srs/cards, the session ledger, Japanese facets, Mind cards) into IndexedDB records like the review log, or store the document in IndexedDB with localStorage as a small boot cache; show the state size in Archive › Storage with a warning at 60% of quota; on a failed save keep a persistent banner (not a toast) and retry into IndexedDB.
- **Flags:** effort L

### DI-11 · P2 · data — Every replicated store pulls with a strict updated_at > cursor on now() stamps, so a row committed late is skipped forever

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** multi-device
- **Detail / repro:** Media, files, money, reviews, mind, ink, reports and push all pull 'updated_at > cursor' and then advance the cursor to the largest updated_at seen. The touch trigger stamps updated_at := now(), which in Postgres is the TRANSACTION START time. If device A's upsert (a 500-row media chunk, a money batch) starts at t1 and commits after device B's quicker write stamped t2 > t1, a third device that pulls between the two commits sets its cursor to t2 and never fetches A's rows (t1 < t2). Nothing ever re-reads them: the pulling device silently lacks those transactions/reviews/ink strokes until a restore. With three devices syncing on focus this is a real, if rare, divergence with no symptom.
- **Evidence:** Re-read 7 Nov: q.gt('updated_at', …) at cloudsync.js:358/376, money.js:1126, reviewlog.js:133, mindjournal.js:191, inksync.js:97, reportstore.js:324 and push.js:90; kos_touch_updated_at still sets now() (migration 20260716000001:26-35). Original: supabase/migrations/20260716000001_kos_sync_init.sql:26-35 (now()); q.gt('updated_at', …) at js/core/money.js:1126, reviewlog.js:133, mindjournal.js:191, inksync.js:97, reportstore.js:324, cloudsync.js:358/376; cursor = max seen (money.js:1189, 1207)
- **Root cause:** Timestamp cursor over transaction-start timestamps.
- **Proposed fix:** Stamp with clock_timestamp() in the trigger and pull with an overlap window (gt cursor − 2 minutes) — every store already skips its own echo by stamp or uid, so re-reading a few rows is harmless; or use a monotonic bigserial 'version' column per table as the cursor.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-16 · P2 · integration — Todoist: moving a task to another linked project in Todoist is undone by the next sync

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Two Reminders lists are linked to two Todoist projects (School→P1, Home→P2). Move a synced task from School to Home in Todoist. The next cycle does not move the reminder (its listId stays School; only ext.list becomes P2), and tdPush then sees ext.list (P2) differ from the local list's project (P1) and sends item_move back to P1. The user's move in Todoist is silently reverted and the reminder never changes list here.
- **Evidence:** audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/exp/td2.js moveRemote → 'after remote move local: [{list:1 (School), ext:{id:T1,list:P1}}] cmds [[item_move:{id:T1,project_id:P1}]] remote project P1'; js/core/exttasks.js:191-196 (reconcile writes ext.list only, never listId), 270 (moved = lk.id !== it.ext.list), 287 (item_move to the local list's project)
- **Root cause:** The list is not a three-way-merged field: the pull records the remote project in ext.list, and the push reads any difference between ext.list and the local list as a LOCAL move.
- **Proposed fix:** In reconcile, when remote.list differs from base list and maps to another linked Reminders list, move the reminder there (listId = linked[remote.list]) inside inbound; only treat a local listId change (lk.id !== base list) as a local move. Keep a base list in ext.base so the three-way rule applies to the list as to every other field.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-17 · P2 · integration — A linked reminder moved to a list linked to the other provider is copied there and orphaned in the first

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Reminders lists can link to Todoist or Google Tasks. Move a Todoist-linked reminder to a list linked to Google Tasks (or the reverse): gtPush sees ext.p !== 'gtasks' and creates a Google task, overwriting ext with the Google link; the Todoist task is neither deleted nor unlinked. The Todoist mirror still holds it, so the next time it changes in Todoist (or on a full sync) byLink('todoist') finds no reminder and imports it again as a NEW reminder: one item becomes two, in two services. Moving a linked reminder to an UNLINKED list keeps it linked and both-way syncing (verified: a title edit is still pushed, a Todoist rename still lands on the reminder in the unlinked list), which contradicts 'a list links to ONE project' (invariant 160).
- **Evidence:** audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/exp/td2.js moveLocal → 'moved to unlinked: cmds []', 'edit while unlinked: cmds [[item_update:{id:T1,content:Local move edited}]]', 'remote rename reaches unlinked list item: Remote rename list 3'; js/core/exttasks.js:412 (!linkedHere → gtCreate, ext replaced at 437-440), 254-258 (Todoist add only when not linked; nothing queues a delete when the list link changes), 270 (moved only when the new list is a todoist link)
- **Root cause:** Each provider's push only considers its own links; a reminder's list move is never translated into an unlink of the old provider.
- **Proposed fix:** Treat a list change as a change of link: when a reminder's list link provider/project differs from ext.p/ext.list, queue a delete (or item_move for same provider) for the old link in state.ext.deletes and clear ext before the other provider creates. For an unlinked target list, either queue the remote delete or unlink (ask once).
- **Flags:** effort M

### DI-18 · P2 · data — Creatives' file store is shared by the real account and the Empty and Sample review namespaces

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Every other IndexedDB is suffixed by KOS.dataMode ("-empty"/"-sample") so a review namespace never touches the real data. kurenai-os-creatives is not. In the Empty or Sample namespace, every work, sketch and Writing Desk draft saved goes into the REAL account's store (and so into its next full backup as orphan rows), and a Restore done while in a review namespace runs creatives.files.importAll, which CLEARS the real store (os.clear()) and replaces it with the backup's creatives.
- **Evidence:** js/core/creatives.js:438 (DB_NAME = "kurenai-os-creatives", no suffix) vs js/core/money.js:39, mediadb.js:97, ink.js:293, reviewlog.js:23, mindjournal.js:20, reportstore.js:28, attachments.js:17, exampapers.js:28, files.js:343 (all + KOS.dataMode.suffix); importAll clear at js/core/creatives.js:465; store.js:708 (restoreCreatives runs in any mode)
- **Root cause:** The suffix convention is repeated by hand in each store; the newest store missed it and nothing checks it.
- **Proposed fix:** DB_NAME = "kurenai-os-creatives" + ((KOS.dataMode && KOS.dataMode.suffix) || ""); add a smoke assertion that every indexedDB.open name carries the suffix.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-19 · P2 · integration — The Todoist/Google sync lease does not exclude a second tab on the same device, and is never renewed during a long cycle

- **Devices:** iPad (app + Safari), Mac (two windows)
- **Detail / repro:** The lease holder is state.ui.extDevice, one id per browser profile, and kos_ext_lease grants the lease to the holder that already has it. Two open tabs or windows (or the Home Screen app plus a Safari tab on the iPad) therefore both 'win' and run their cycles at the same time against the same media-kv mirror and sync token. Each tab holds its own in-memory reminders (the two-tab clobber finding), so tab B's pull meets the task tab A just created and linked as an unknown remote item and imports it as a new reminder, while B's own unlinked copy is item_add'ed with the same uuid and linked to the same Todoist id: two reminders, one task — the same end state as the two-device duplicate, reachable on ONE device. Separately, the lease is 120 s and is never extended; a cycle that runs longer (several 90-command chunks, a slow network, Google Tasks paging) lets another device in mid-cycle.
- **Evidence:** js/core/ext.js:73-77 (device() = state.ui.extDevice, shared by every tab of the profile), 268-270 (lease once per cycle, LEASE_S 120 at :40), 306-319 (no renewal); supabase/migrations/20261030000001_kos_ext.sql:44 (lease_holder = p_holder re-grants); in-tab guard only: js/core/ext.js:326 (var running); duplicate end state reproduced by audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/exp/td.js twodev → local 'Made on A': [[3,'T3'],[4,'T3']]
- **Root cause:** Exclusion is designed per device, but the app's real unit of concurrency is the tab.
- **Proposed fix:** Make the holder per tab (device id + a random per-page suffix kept in memory) or coordinate tabs with a Web Lock (navigator.locks.request('kos-ext-'+p)) / BroadcastChannel; renew the lease between chunks and lists, and abort the cycle when renewal fails. Also de-duplicate on pull: before importing an unknown remote id, look for a local reminder already linked to it.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-20 · P2 · data — Money, the review log, Mind's Journal and saved Reports replicate with no error surfaced anywhere

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Each side store's syncCloud(cb) is only ever called WITHOUT a callback (debounced after a change, at boot and on a 30-minute interval), so an RLS refusal, a missing table, a network error or a failed chunk is dropped: nothing is logged, nothing is shown, and Archive › Cloud sync's 'Last synced' describes the state document only. A user who adds transactions on the iPhone can see 'Last synced 10:42' on both devices while kos_money has rejected every upsert. Only handwriting has a visible status (Pen and ink). The local put/delete callbacks in the pull ignore their error argument too, and the cursor is still advanced (money.js:1205-1206), so a row that failed to write locally is skipped for good.
- **Evidence:** callers without cb: js/core/money.js:1220, 1226-1227; js/core/reviewlog.js:212; js/core/mindjournal.js:260, 267-268; js/core/reportstore.js:417, 423; contrast js/modules/inkset.js:92 (ink shows its result); js/core/money.js:1193-1206 (deleteRaw/putRaw callbacks take no err, meta.cursor = maxTs); js/modules/cloudui.js:86, 190 ('Last synced' from cloudsync status only)
- **Root cause:** Each replicator copied Money's pattern, which treats replication as fire-and-forget; there is no shared status contract for secondary stores.
- **Proposed fix:** Give every replicator a status record (last ok, last error, pending count) in a shared registry (e.g. KOS.cloudsync.sideStatus(name, …)) and render it in Archive › Cloud sync as one line per store; only advance a cursor after the local write succeeded.
- **Flags:** effort M

### DI-21 · P2 · data — 'Reset everything' only resets the state document: the media vault, files, money, ink, Mind, reviews, Creatives and reports all stay

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The confirm dialog promises 'This removes study progress, notes, flashcard schedules, the Governor, the media vault, the planner and every attachment from this device'. The handler calls KOS.store.reset(), which only replaces the localStorage document with DEFAULTS. Every IndexedDB store survives: the 1,880-entry media vault, attachments, Money transactions, handwriting, Mind's Journal, the review log, Creatives' works and saved Reports. After the reset the app shows those leftovers (Money, Files, the vault) against a fresh state, and a signed-in device then replicates the leftovers back up. Reproduced on slot 19: a transaction, an ink page and a reminder added, Reset everything confirmed → reminders 0, but money ['Reset test'] and the ink notebook remain.
- **Evidence:** kos.mjs eval 19 → {btn:true, rem:0, moneyTx:['Reset test'], ink:true}; js/modules/hub.js:3436-3474 (dialog text, store.reset() at 3471), js/core/store.js:747-751 (reset replaces state only)
- **Root cause:** Reset predates the IndexedDB stores; each new store was added to backup but not to reset.
- **Proposed fix:** Add KOS.store.resetFull(): clear every IndexedDB store of the current namespace through each owner's importAll(empty)/clear (media incl. kv except credentials, files, filetext, money, reviews, ink, mind, creatives, reports, papers), then reset state and reload; or reword the dialog to what it does.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-22 · P2 · ux — Import backup replaces everything the moment a file is picked, with no confirmation and no safety copy

- **Devices:** all, worst on iPad/iPhone (no tooltip)
- **Detail / repro:** Backup & Restore's 'Import backup…' opens the file picker and importFull runs on change: the state is replaced (KOS.store.replaceState) and media, money, reviews, Mind and Creatives stores are cleared and rewritten before anything is shown. That it is 'a complete restore, not a merge' is only in the button's title tooltip, which touch devices (iPad, iPhone) never show. Picking an old file by mistake overwrites today's work with no undo; nothing snapshots the current data first, and on a signed-in device noteRestore then makes the cloud follow the restored data. The success message lists sections restored but never says what was lost (and saved Reports are silently not part of it).
- **Evidence:** js/modules/hub.js:3356-3376 (onchange → store.importFull directly; title-only warning at 3375), js/core/store.js:620-621 (replaceState before any check of the other sections), 735-737 (noteRestore)
- **Root cause:** The restore was built as a direct action on file selection.
- **Proposed fix:** After the file is read and validated, show a danger dialog ('Replace this device's data with the backup from <exportedAt>? N sessions, M media entries… This can't be undone') with Cancel focused; before restoring, take a snapshotFull into a kept 'before restore' copy (or offer to export one).
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-12 · P3 · integration — Todoist: a command the server rejects is resent on every cycle forever, with no status shown

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** tdPush applies a record's bookkeeping only when every command in its group returns 'ok'. A rejected command (item_update or item_delete for a task deleted or moved out of reach in Todoist, an invalid label, a due string Todoist cannot parse) leaves base and the delete queue unchanged, so the same command is sent every cycle (every few minutes and on every focus) and the Connections status still says the cycle succeeded, because sync_status errors are never turned into counts or an error. A partly-applied group (item_update ok, item_close rejected) also re-sends the parts that did apply.
- **Evidence:** Re-read 7 Nov: exttasks.js:329-334 unchanged (only all-ok entries call a.ok; non-ok sync_status ignored). Original: js/core/exttasks.js:329-334 (only the all-ok case is handled; errors in r.sync_status are dropped), js/core/exttasks.js:256 (delete queue entry kept on error)
- **Root cause:** Error results of batched commands are ignored.
- **Proposed fix:** Read sync_status errors: for 'not found' (error_code 22) drop the queue entry or unlink the record; for other errors record them in counts and setStatus so Connections shows 'n changes refused' with the reason; apply per-command bookkeeping rather than per group.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-13 · P3 · data — An unreadable stored state is replaced by a fresh one and overwritten on the next save

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** At boot, if JSON.parse or deepMerge of kurenai-os-v1 throws, the app logs a warning and starts from DEFAULTS; the next save() (any render that creates a progress record, the boot seeders) writes the empty state over the unreadable original, so whatever was recoverable from it is gone and the user is not told. With cloud sync the empty-local guard then adopts the cloud copy, but a signed-out user loses everything silently.
- **Evidence:** Re-read 7 Nov: store.js:382-390 unchanged (catch → DEFAULTS with console.warn; next save overwrites). Original: js/core/store.js:382-390 (catch → DEFAULTS, console.warn only), 393 and 395-410 (save overwrites KEY)
- **Root cause:** No quarantine of the original before the first overwrite.
- **Proposed fix:** On a parse failure copy the raw string to a side key (kurenai-os-v1.corrupt-<ts>) or into IndexedDB before anything saves, and show a blocking notice offering Restore from backup / cloud.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-14 · P3 · content — Backup & Restore's 'What a backup covers' list is out of date: half of what the file holds, and everything it leaves out, is unlisted

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The list names study, productivity, Governor, the media vault, the purchase planner and attachments. The file also carries Money transactions, the review log, handwriting, Mind's Journal and Creatives work, none of which is listed; and it does NOT carry saved Reports and snapshots, the Paper library's own PDFs (unless kept in the cloud), Japanese saved lines, or the Google/Todoist sign-ins (records stay linked but need reconnecting) — the reader is not told. The closing line points only to 'Sync & Import' for reconnecting, not Connections.
- **Evidence:** Re-shot 7 Nov: shots/data-integrity/data-mac.png and data-ipad-1107.png still list six rows (study, productivity, Governor, media, planner, attachments); Money, handwriting, review log, Mind, Creatives, Code/Japanese/Exams are not named and Reports' absence is not stated. Original: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/data-integrity/data-mac.png; list text read via eval; js/core/store.js:513-583 (what snapshotFull includes)
- **Root cause:** Hand-written copy that did not follow the backup's growth.
- **Proposed fix:** Generate the rows from the same table snapshotFull uses (one row per store with its live count), and add a short 'Not in the file' line naming Reports, the Paper library and connections.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-15 · P3 · ui — Archive › Storage accounts for none of the app's real data and prints rows of 0 KB

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** On the seeded account (1,880 media entries, 373 KB state document, money, reviews) 'On this device' says 48.4 MB used while 'By kind of data' lists only Files, Past papers, Your ink and Text index, each '0 KB' — supporting zeros that invariant 77 says to suppress — and never shows the state document (the one store with a hard ~5 MB ceiling), the media vault, Money, the review log, Mind or Creatives. The numbers cannot explain the total. On the Mac the last card ('Not linked anywhere') sits alone in a row with two empty columns beside it.
- **Evidence:** Re-shot 7 Nov: shots/data-integrity/storage-mac.png → '47.4 MB used', By kind of data rows 0 KB / 0 KB / 1 KB / 0 KB; the media vault, money, reviews, Mind and reports are not listed. Original: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/data-integrity/storage-mac.png, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/data-integrity/storage-iphone.png
- **Root cause:** Storage page written for Files R4 only.
- **Proposed fix:** List every store (state document with its share of the localStorage quota, media vault, money, reviews, ink, mind, creatives, reports, files, papers, text index) with sizes from navigator.storage.estimate().usageDetails or a count × average, hide zero rows, and let the last card span the row.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-23 · P3 · integration — A reminder deleted here while its task was edited in Todoist comes back for one sync cycle

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Delete a synced reminder locally; before the next cycle, the task is edited in Todoist. The cycle PULLS first: the edited item is in the incremental result, byLink has no reminder for it, so reconcile imports it as a new reminder; THEN tdPush sends the queued item_delete. The reminder re-appears in Reminders (with a new id) until the following cycle (up to 15 minutes) removes it again. Any alert or tick made on it in between is lost.
- **Evidence:** audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/exp/td2.js both → 'delete vs remote edit: local [{id:5,ext:{id:T1}}] remote deleted true cmds [[item_delete:T1]]' then 'next cycle local []'; js/core/exttasks.js:212-213 (delete queue read), 225-235 (pull imports before the queue is applied), 180-187 (create path does not consult state.ext.deletes); CYCLE_MS 15 min at js/core/ext.js:40
- **Root cause:** The pull does not know about pending local deletions.
- **Proposed fix:** In reconcile's create path skip a remote id that is in the delete queue (q['todoist:task:'+id]); same for Google Tasks.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-24 · P3 · data — Restore is not authoritative for handwriting or files: ink pages and files not in the backup survive it

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Every other store's importAll clears before writing (media, money, reviews, Mind, Creatives). ink.importAll only puts, so notebooks and pages created after the backup (or from another account) stay, now attached to a restored state that may not reference them; and restoreFiles returns early when the backup has no attachments, leaving every current file in place, while a backup WITH attachments clears them. cloudsync.noteRestore then re-baselines as if the device held exactly the backup. Restore also clears the whole media kv (mediadb.importAll ks.clear()), so the cloud merge base, the Todoist/Google mirrors and sync tokens and the GitHub outbox are reset to the backup's (tokens themselves are excluded by design), which forces full re-syncs; the report shown to the user mentions none of this.
- **Evidence:** js/core/ink.js:531-540 (no clear), js/modules/attachments.js:488-493 vs js/core/store.js:651-652 (if (!items.length) return next()), js/core/mediadb.js:1373-1374 (es.clear(); ks.clear()), js/core/store.js:735-740 (noteRestore)
- **Root cause:** Each store's import semantics were written independently; there is no single contract for 'restore replaces'.
- **Proposed fix:** Clear docs/pages in ink.importAll; call attach.importAll with [] too (or document merge semantics for both); keep per-device sync kv (ext.*, cloudsync.base, code.github.outbox) out of the clear, or list what was reset in the restore report.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-25 · P3 · arch — Japanese mined lines are kept in the synced state document, against 'personal media never leaves the device'

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.ja.mine() stores each saved line's text, reading, translation and its source object in state.japanese.mined, which is part of the state document: it is uploaded to kos_state by cloud sync (DEVICE_PATHS does not exclude it) and written into every backup. Invariant 115 and docs/japanese-plan.md say personal media lines live in IndexedDB only and never sync. Nothing calls mine() yet (the reader and media pages are not built), so no user data is affected today; it will be the moment the reader ships.
- **Evidence:** js/core/ja.js:278-289 (st.mined[id] = {text, reading, en, src, at}; store.save()), js/core/cloudsync.js:165-172 (DEVICE_PATHS: no japanese.mined), docs/japanese-plan.md:1070 (115: personal media never leaves the device); grep '.mine(' → no caller
- **Root cause:** The backend was written before the storage decision for personal media was applied to it.
- **Proposed fix:** Before the reader lands, move mined lines to an IndexedDB store (namespaced by KOS.dataMode.suffix) keyed by the hash id, keep only the facet key in state.japanese.facets, and add a smoke assertion that syncableState() carries no mined text.
- **Flags:** effort S

### DI-26 · P3 · arch — Mind's Journal replication has no test and no injectable cloud, unlike every other replicated store

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Money (smoke86, _setCloudApi), the review log (smoke96), ink (smoke105), reports (smoke72) and files (smoke17/106) each run their push/pull against a fake table. kos_mind's syncCloud (push-then-pull, echo skip, remote deletion without a tombstone) is exercised by no suite and exposes no way to inject a fake API, so a regression in the Journal's replication (a private, local-first store per invariant 139) would ship unnoticed.
- **Evidence:** grep 'kos_mind|mindJournal.syncCloud' tools/smoke*.test.js → no match; js/core/mindjournal.js:180-197 (cloud() = cloudApi || realCloud(), but KOS.mindJournal at :271-275 exports no _setCloudApi); smoke86/96/105/72/106 pass on this build
- **Root cause:** Copy of Money's replicator without its test seam.
- **Proposed fix:** Export _setCloudApi and add a smoke covering push, echo skip, pull, remote delete and a two-device edit, modelled on smoke86.
- **Flags:** effort S

**QoL ideas from this auditor:**
- Show the state document's size and its share of the ~5 MB localStorage quota in Archive › Storage.
- Connections: show the last cycle's refused commands and duplicate links, with a 'Fold duplicates' action.
- After a restore or first link, toast what was merged or replaced, naming the counts per domain.
- Add a 'Download a copy of this device first' button to the first-link dialog.
- Archive › Cloud sync: one status line per replicated store (Money, reviews, Journal, ink, reports, files) with its last success.
- Restore report: say which sections the file did not carry (saved Reports) and which per-device sync records were reset.

**Backlog ideas from this auditor:**
- Move the state document (or its big parts: srs, sessions, facets) from localStorage to IndexedDB with per-record writes and cross-tab coordination (BroadcastChannel or Web Locks).
- Replace per-device counter ids for assignments, reminders and events with random string ids, as Money, Routines and Exams already use, retiring rekeyCollisions.
- Make provider sync state-consistent: pull and push the cloud state around each leased cycle, and keep pending provider adds in synced state so any device recognises them.
- Use a monotonic version column (bigserial) as the replication cursor for every kos_* table.
- Audit every view for sub-objects of KOS.store.state captured at render and written later (stale after replaceState); with redraws held on task pages a stale page lives longer.
- A single store registry (name, namespace suffix, backup, restore semantics, reset, replication, status) that store.js, reset, Storage and the backup page all read, with a smoke asserting every indexedDB.open is registered.

## AP — Architecture, maintainability, performance, docs drift (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** Top-up on the production build (e30b837, sw kos-redraw-1). All twelve earlier findings still hold and most got worse with the Achievements/art/shop release: boot now loads 346 synchronous scripts (16.9 MB JS, 9.95 MB of it curriculum data) and spends long seconds compiling content before main.js; derived reads are still un-memoised, and the new badge engine re-measures all 254 badges on every Seat/Wall render and tab switch, so first renders of the Governor, shop and Wall cost seconds on the dense account and an owner tick produces ~0.6-0.9 s long tasks. Every boot also runs the exam cap pass over all 5,442 cards with linear leaf scans (0.7-1 s, moving nothing) and readiness about 15 times. There is still no view lifecycle: KOS.rerender drops focus to body, detached pages leak through lazily removed listeners, and a wrong staleness check now lets the Wall's async callback pop a set dialog over whatever page you navigated to; the redraw stopgap's hand-kept TASK_VIEWS list leaves the two new draft pages (Edit your seat, the Wall's Showcase) unprotected. Maintainability: hub.js and aitools.js stay ~3.8-3.9k lines and governor-ui.js has grown to 1,730; the four study spaces still copy the lesson machinery; dead CSS grew (16 governor classes left by the Stage rebuild). Docs drift is the most user-facing structural problem: README/PROGRESS/HANDOFF name releases a week or more old, AGENTS.md's gate command skips smoke108 and smoke113, in-app Help covers none of the last six features, and CLAUDE.md is a 186 KB file whose 271-line baseline is a release diary with stale entries.

### AP-01 · P1 · perf — Boot loads ~16.6 MB of JavaScript in 340 synchronous script tags, most of it curriculum content no first view needs

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** changed: now 346 scripts (4 defer/async), 16.9 MB JS of which js/data 9.95 MB, 26 stylesheets 1.31 MB (was 340 / 16.6 MB / 1.2 MB). Dense boot on slot 20 at machine load 6-10: domInteractive 53-127 s, 78-106 long tasks totalling 52-125 s; evaluating scripts before main.js took ~18 s, and the first KOS.show after main.js 13.7 s when the restored route was the Wall. Absolute times are inflated by the shared machine, the shape holds.
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** all; worst on iPhone 17 and iPad (cold launch of the Home Screen app)
- **Detail / repro:** index.html lists 340 <script src> tags; only KaTeX, supabase.js and env.local.js are deferred. Summed on disk: 16.64 MB JS (js/data/content 8.28 MB in 126 files, js/modules 3.33 MB, js/core 2.50 MB, js/data 1.67 MB, js/labs 0.60 MB) plus 1.21 MB CSS in 24 sheets. Every topic's notes for every subject (CS, Maths, IT, Code units 1-12, tracks, Japanese, Mind, Creatives), the 567 KB past-paper index, and the 383 KB Rider project scaffolds (code-projects-files.js, needed only when exporting a Rider zip) are parsed and executed before Home renders. In the harness a cold reload of the EMPTY account took 15.0 s to domInteractive with 61 long tasks totalling 15.4 s (max 2.75 s); the CPU profile shows 11 s of (program) (parse/compile) and the top self-time scripts are content files executing their builders (cs-p2-46b.js 746 ms, code.js lesson() 316 ms, cs-p2-411.js 545 ms, cs-p2-410a.js 497 ms, maths-stats-s4 325 ms...). The machine was shared with other audit slots so absolute times are inflated, but the shape is unambiguous: the content payload dominates boot, and on an iPad/iPhone (slower JS, tighter memory, Safari evicting a backgrounded Home Screen app) every cold launch pays it. Heap after boot on the empty account: 68 MB.
- **Evidence:** arch20/boot.mjs runs on slot 20 (6 Nov): {jsN:346, jsMB:16.9, domInteractive:53357, longTasks:78, longMs:51726} and {domInteractive:70719, longTasks:87} on Home; python count of index.html <script src> = 346; arch20/trace-boot-dense.txt (script evaluation, achcatalogue.js 943 ms) | earlier: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/prof-boot-empty.txt; index.html lines 48-55 (only defer tags) and the 340-script list; sizes via stat: exam-index.js 566,954 B, code-projects-files.js 382,808 B, it-f204.js 299,469 B, hub.js 232,148 B, aitools.js 208,176 B; Performance API: domInteractive 14,993 ms, longtasks 61 / 15,441 ms; dense account warm reload (SW controlling, V8 code cache): data-shell=ready at 21,064 ms, 35 long tasks totalling 19,166 ms, heap 58 MB (machine shared with other audit slots, load avg ~5)
- **Root cause:** Classic script-tag design (chosen so file:// works) with no lazy-loading layer; every new study space appended its whole content to index.html.
- **Proposed fix:** Keep the script-tag architecture but split content into lazily loaded bundles: KOS.content.get(key) already funnels every read, so make content files register a loader per subject/unit (a tiny manifest listing keys -> file) and inject the script on first open of a topic, a desk or search (search can use a prebuilt title/keyword index). Load exam-index.js only on #/exams, code-projects-files.js only on export, ja/mind/creatives content only when their desk opens. Target: boot payload under ~4 MB. Also add performance.mark('kos-boot-start'/'kos-interactive') in main.js so the cost is tracked by a smoke test budget.
- **Flags:** effort L

### AP-03 · P2 · perf — Cold-path cost after boot: the first render of each heavy view takes 0.5-2.8 s on the dense account (Exams, Code map, Due, Pacing, Calendar), then 20-200 ms

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds: first/warm render on slot 20 (load 7-10, so ~2-3x inflated): home 6560/4640 ms, calendar 10362/3683, exams 5393/4926, code 6452/2738, pacing 5929/2574, due 2302/857, a CS topic page 6735 then 3884; new heavy views: governor 3090-6101, governor/shop 7341/3436, governor/edit 7167/829, the Wall 1.9-7.9 s until its badges draw.
- **Devices:** all; most felt on iPhone 17 and iPad cold launches
- **Detail / repro:** Rendering each view three times in a row (via a cheap view in between) on the seeded account gave: exams 2750/589/179 ms, code map 1622/504/355, due 1623/263/22, pacing 1405/51/120, calendar 1015/168/189, japanese 825/59/311, routines 705/11/16, mind 670/171/126, home 205/175/63 (first ever Home after boot was 2.0-3.3 s). Steady state is acceptable; the first visit after a cold launch is not, and on an iPad/iPhone Home Screen app every relaunch after Safari evicts it is a cold launch. Two causes: (1) V8 lazily compiles functions from the 16.6 MB of eagerly loaded script on first use, and (2) the derived reads have no per-render snapshot, so first calls are expensive and repeated: KOS.exams.readiness over 17 assessments measured 3,247 ms then 696/78/55 ms on later runs; KOS.code.unitState (js/core/code.js:888) rescans every lesson and calls stats() (code.js:856) per call, and the Code map (js/modules/code.js:417-490) calls it per unit, per track need (needMet) and per track section (trackState); evidence() re-splits shipped notes with KOS.content.splitPages on every call (code.js:168, 66 ms/call measured). The Calendar month calls dayItems -> derivedOn (37 ms/call warm, calendar.js:563) for each of 35-42 cells, re-reading every Money rule, goal and exam start-by per cell.
- **Evidence:** arch20/views.js -> arch20/views-out.txt; eval topic1 6735 ms / topic2 3884 ms | earlier: eval timings above (slot 18, seeded); audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/prof-boot-dense.txt (readiness js/core/exams.js:635 1314 ms self in the boot profile, exams.js:945 predictPass 893 ms), arch/prof-code.txt, arch/prof-calendar.txt; js/core/code.js:166-190, 856-895; js/modules/code.js:417-490; js/modules/calendar.js:546-570, 1762-1800; js/core/exams.js:635-720, 943-960
- **Root cause:** Pure derive-on-read design (a good contract) without any memoisation layer, so composite pages multiply the cost; plus eager loading of all code.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a cheap per-tick memo: a KOS.store revision counter bumped by save(), and memoise the heavy pure reads (exams.readiness/leaves, code stats/unitState/pageCount, calendar derivedOn for a month range, srs.allCards) on (args, revision, day). Shipped content is immutable at runtime (invariant 86), so pageCount/listingsOf can be cached forever. For the calendar, compute derived items for the visible range once and bucket by date. Pair with lazy content loading (boot finding) to cut compile cost.
- **Flags:** effort M

### AP-08 · P2 · perf — Detached pages leak: global listeners are removed only when their event next fires, so every visited topic/Files/lesson page stays in memory

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds: still 15 isConnected-lazy removeEventListener sites (inkui, inksync, codetopic, mindtopic, jatopic, files, attachments, hub, inktab, crtopic); on this build 30 CS topic pages left 23,414 nodes / 2,237 listeners on the Files page vs 7,413 / 749 before, released only when a kos-ink event fired (9,487).
- **Devices:** iPad (long-lived Home Screen app) and iPhone most; all
- **Detail / repro:** 15 places add a window/document listener on each render and remove it lazily inside the handler ('if (!node.isConnected) { removeEventListener(...); return; }'): hub.js:2719 and 3169 (kos-ink on every topic page), files.js:283 (paste) and 292 (kos-files-index), attachments.js:736 (paste), inkui.js:1422 (keydown), inktab.js:518, codetopic.js:214/228, jatopic.js:321/334, mindtopic.js:380/395, crtopic.js:246, inksync.js:339. Rare events (kos-ink fires only when ink is written; paste only on a paste) never come, so each closure keeps its whole detached page alive. Measured with forced GC (CDP HeapProfiler.collectGarbage + Memory.getDOMCounters) on the seeded account: on Files, 9,003 DOM nodes / 886 listeners; after opening 30 CS topic pages and returning to Files, 24,954 nodes / 2,369 listeners (about 16,000 detached nodes retained); dispatching one kos-ink event dropped it to 11,027 / 1,096. Three rounds over 23 views grew nodes from 1,786 to 14,110 and listeners from 157 to 1,795. Opening Files 5 times adds 5 document paste listeners. On an iPad Home Screen app kept open for days this is unbounded growth until Safari kills the page (which then pays the full cold boot).
- **Evidence:** arch20/mem2.txt and arch20/mem.txt (this build); grep -rEn isConnected[^;]*removeEventListener js | wc -l = 15 | earlier: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/arch/mem.txt, arch/mem2.txt; eval: 5 paste listeners after 5 Files visits; grep 'isConnected[^;]*removeEventListener' = 15 sites listed
- **Root cause:** No view lifecycle: KOS.show replaces #main with innerHTML='' and has no unmount step, so each module invented a lazy self-removal.
- **Proposed fix:** Give KOS.show a teardown hook: views register cleanups via a KOS.ui.onLeave(fn) (or an AbortController per render, passing {signal} to addEventListener) that KOS.show calls before clearing #main; replace the 15 lazy removals with it. Add a smoke check that navigating 20 views leaves the listener count flat (jsdom can count via a wrapped addEventListener).
- **Flags:** effort M

### AP-10 · P2 · a11y — KOS.rerender() drops keyboard focus to <body> on every redraw, including background ones (cloud pull, habit auto-tick)

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds on kos-redraw-1: the stopgap keeps the scroller position but not focus. Focus a control, KOS.rerender(): home, calendar, money, achievements (Showcase tab button), governor (Avatar) and routines all leave document.activeElement = BODY.
- **Devices:** Mac (keyboard), iPad with keyboard, VoiceOver on all
- **Detail / repro:** Invariant 65 says a redraw changes no focus. KOS.rerender (js/core/ui.js:344-357) re-runs KOS.show(..., {_nav:true}), which empties #main (ui.js, main.innerHTML = '') and rebuilds it; it restores main.scrollTop but not the focused control. Measured on the seeded account: focusing a control and calling KOS.rerender() left document.activeElement = BODY on Home (was home.review-line), Calendar (cal.mode), Routines (ui.tab), Reminders (rem.side-item) and Money (ui.tab). Background callers make this hit keyboard and VoiceOver users without any action of theirs: cloudsync.js:731 rerenderCurrent after a pull, routines.js:699 after autoSync ticks a habit, plus 142 KOS.rerender() call sites in total (most after the user's own action, where the control they used vanishes). A redraw also costs a full view build (225 ms Home, 326 ms Calendar warm).
- **Evidence:** eval on slot 20 (6 Nov): {home:{before:"Revise for: AQA 7517 Paper 2",after:"BODY"}, calendar:{before:"Show",after:"BODY"}, money, achievements, governor, routines all BODY}; js/core/ui.js:355-372 | earlier: eval on slot 18: {home:{ms:225,focusedBefore:'home.review-line',after:'BODY'}, calendar:{ms:326,after:'BODY'}, routines, reminders, money all BODY}; js/core/ui.js:344-357; js/core/cloudsync.js:723-731; js/core/routines.js:699
- **Root cause:** Redraw is implemented as navigation (rebuild #main) with only scroll restoration.
- **Proposed fix:** In KOS.rerender, before the redraw record the focused element's identity inside #main (closest [data-ui] plus data-key/data-id/aria-label and its index among matches) and after it focus the equivalent node with {preventScroll:true}, falling back to #main without announcing; skip background redraws while focus is inside #main and the user is typing (or defer them until blur).
- **Flags:** effort S

### AP-15 · P2 · perf — Badge measuring runs synchronously on the main thread: the Governor's Seat measures all 254 badges twice per render, and every topic tick re-measures 44 study badges

- **Devices:** all (worse on iPad/iPhone CPUs)
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.achievements.list() builds a fresh context (makeCtx, js/core/achievements.js:239) and runs every badge's measure (measureOne, :296) each time it is called; nothing is memoised across calls or renders. The Governor's Seat status page calls it twice per render (js/modules/governor-ui.js:358 the arc of medals and :527 the area cards) and Edit your seat once more (:732); the Wall calls it on each tab (js/modules/achievements.js:126, 613, 747). Many measures are themselves the expensive derived reads the earlier audit found un-memoised — KOS.exams.readiness for every upcoming exam (achcatalogue.js:251-256, the 'Ready' badge), Code/Creatives/Mind evidence over every lesson, topic bands over every leaf for the ~30 unit badges (reg.unit, achcatalogue.js ~246). Owner events re-measure by domain (touch, 400 ms debounce), and the 'study' domain holds 44 badges, so every store.setCheck/setStatus (js/core/store.js:452/466 → onProgress) costs one main-thread long task some 400 ms after the tick. Measured on the dense account (machine shared, load 5-9, so absolute figures are inflated): a single onProgress('cs') produced one 541 ms long task; evaluate(['study']) took 1.3-13.5 s across runs; KOS.achievements.list() 2.4-3.9 s cold, 138 ms warm; KOS.show('governor') 0.7-22 s (3.1 s typical first render), with measureOne, reg.unit, readiness, code/creatives/mind evidence, code.stats and srs.dueCards at the top of its CPU profile. Top-up 2 (load 7-10): KOS.achievements.touch([study]) produced long tasks of 920 and 631 ms; a reload that restores onto #/achievements made its first KOS.show take 13.7 s in the boot wrapper; the Wall shows Reading your records for 1.9-7.9 s on first open and re-measures on every tab switch and every rerender (4.4 s). A no-op full sweep writes nothing (0 store.save calls), which is correct. Measure exceptions are swallowed to null with no console line (achievements.js:307), so a schema change in an owner would silently stop a badge.
- **Evidence:** arch20/prof-governor.txt (CPU profile of KOS.show('governor')); eval on slot 20: {listCallsPerGovernorRender:2, list first 3929 ms / second 138 ms, evalStudy 13555 then 3112 then 1324 ms}, longtask observer after KOS.achievements.onProgress('cs') = [541]; js/core/achievements.js:239-262, 296-341, 446-466; js/modules/governor-ui.js:358, 527, 732; arch20/bootsteps.mjs [show 13708 ms on the Wall]; arch20/views-out.txt; eval longtasks after touch [920,631]; savesPerNoopSweep 0
- **Root cause:** list() and evaluate() both measure from scratch with a per-call context; measures reuse un-memoised derived reads; all of it runs synchronously.
- **Proposed fix:** Keep the last evaluate's per-badge values (in memory, keyed by a store revision or the ledgerKey already computed at achievements.js:134) and let list() read them instead of re-measuring; measure only when the owning domain's revision moved. Run the domain re-measure in idle slices (requestIdleCallback, a few badges per slice) so a tick never blocks input. The memo layer for readiness/code evidence recommended in the backlog would cut the rest.
- **Flags:** effort M

### AP-17 · P2 · bug — Opening a Wall set by link and leaving before the badges are measured pops the set dialog over whatever page you are on

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.views.achievements draws the Wall in the async KOS.achievements.list() callback (js/modules/achievements.js:126-135) and opens the set dialog there for #/achievements/set/<id>. The guard meant to stop a stale callback, `if (!body.isConnected && body.parentNode == null) return;` (:127), can never fire: body is a child of root, so body.parentNode is root even after KOS.show has emptied #main. So the callback draws into a detached tree and then calls openSetDialog on the new page. list() measures all 254 badges and takes 0.3-8 s on the dense account, so it is easy to leave in time (a set link from the bell, search or the Governor, then Back). Repro on slot 20 (seeded): KOS.show(achievements, set/study); 50 ms later KOS.show(home) -> 0.9 s later the Into the green set dialog is open over Home (URL #/home); after the earlier render-timing pass three such dialogs were stacked (role=dialog count 3).
- **Evidence:** shots/architecture-perf/ach-set-dialog-over-home.png; eval on slot 20: {view:home, hash:#/home, dialog:CS, Maths and IT Study ... Into the green, after:911}; js/modules/achievements.js:126-135
- **Root cause:** A wrong staleness check (parentNode of an inner node is never null) on an async render callback; no shared per-view cancellation token.
- **Proposed fix:** Make the guard `if (!body.isConnected) return;` (or compare a render token / KOS.currentNav() with the one at call time), and the same in governor-ui.js:358/527/732, whose callbacks have no guard at all. Long term: the view lifecycle (AbortController per view) recommended in the backlog.
- **Flags:** effort S

### AP-18 · P2 · perf — Every boot runs the exam cap pass over all cards (0.7-1 s) and readiness about fifteen times before the first page settles

- **Devices:** all (worse on iPad/iPhone CPUs)
- **Detail / repro:** main.js:138 calls KOS.srs.examPass() synchronously on every boot. It walks every scheduled card and, for each, examFor() searches every capped exam with e.leaves.indexOf(sid:ref) — a linear scan of an array of leaf keys (js/core/srs.js:182-191, 201-222), so the cost is cards x exams x leaves, and recordMemory/weights() is recomputed per card. On the dense account (5,442 cards, 11 upcoming assessments) one pass takes 0.7-1.0 s and moves nothing (returns 0) — it is only useful the first boot after an exam is added. In the same boot KOS.exams.readiness ran 15 times (1.8 s, 0.7 s and a dozen of 50-100 ms; Home focus plan, notices, the badge sweep and predictedAtExam each re-derive it), and today.build 2.8 s. Measured with a boot wrapper (arch20/bootsteps.mjs; machine at load 6-7, so absolute figures are inflated about 2-3x, the ratios hold).
- **Evidence:** node arch20/bootsteps.mjs 20 → [show 13708 ms (the restored Wall), today.build 2830, srs.examPass 2772, exams.readiness 1826, 658, 97, 86 ... x15, exams.freezePass 203]; eval: examPass 1010 ms then 712 ms, returns 0; readiness over 11 upcoming exams 1300 ms; js/main.js:138; js/core/srs.js:182-222
- **Root cause:** Pure derive-on-read functions with linear lookups, called from several boot paths without a memo or a changed-inputs check.
- **Proposed fix:** Build a Set of leaf keys per exam once in examIndex (or a leaf->exam map) so examFor is O(1); hoist weights(); run examPass only when its inputs changed (a hash of the cap list and the exam-day target kept in state.srsCfg) or in an idle callback after first paint. Memoise readiness per assessment on a store revision (the memo layer in the backlog).
- **Flags:** effort S

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** changed: now 113 suites, 39,291 lines of tests, 1,227 CPU-seconds (was 849 s); smoke56 242 s and smoke75 236 s are 39%; still no npm script (package.json has only dependencies) and no .github/workflows.

The documented way to run it is a shell for-loop in CLAUDE.md; package.json has no scripts (not even 'test'), jsdom/fake-indexeddb are the only deps, there is no .github/workflows, so the gate runs only when an agent remembers to run it, sequentially (~14 min). The suites total 38,936 lines; 78 of 112 read source files with readFileSync (source-text assertions, e.g. smoke55's CSS vocabulary), which is useful for invariants but brittle to refactors such as the hub.js split.

### AP-13 · P3 · arch — Date and formatting helpers are re-implemented per file (pad x18, addDays x14, iso/isoOf x16, hm x11, rid x8)

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** changed: pad now in 19 files, addDays 15, iso 11 + isoOf 7, hm 11, rid 8 (the new achievements/art code added more copies).
- **Devices:** n/a
- **Detail / repro:** Counting 'function <name>(' across js/core, js/modules, js/labs and js/engines: pad 18 files, addDays 14, iso 10 + isoOf 6, hm 11, rid 8, clamp 5. The copies are textually different (pad()+getMonth, ('0'+x).slice(-2), String().padStart, one Date.UTC variant), several just forward to KOS.srs.addDays, and the 'today' helpers differ (iso(new Date()), KOS.srs.todayISO(), G.todayISO()). They agree today, but this is where a routine-day vs calendar-day (invariant 148) or a local vs UTC slip would hide, and each new module copies one more.
- **Evidence:** grep -l per helper over js/{core,modules,labs,engines}/*.js (6 Nov) | earlier: grep -l 'function pad(' etc. over js/{core,modules,labs,engines}/*.js; grep -h -A3 'function iso(|function isoOf(' shows 5 distinct implementations
- **Root cause:** IIFE-per-file modules with no shared utility module for dates; copying a helper was the path of least resistance.
- **Proposed fix:** Add KOS.date (iso, parse, addDays, daysBetween, weekStart, hm, pad) in js/core next to srs, make KOS.srs's date functions delegate to it, and replace local copies opportunistically when a file is touched; a smoke rule can refuse new local 'function addDays(' definitions.
- **Flags:** effort S

### AP-16 · P3 · arch — The smoke gate is not reliable under load: five suites fail when run three at a time and pass alone

- **Devices:** n/a
- **Detail / repro:** Running all 113 suites with three in parallel on the shared test machine (load ~10) failed smoke2, smoke4 (vault cards not rendered in jsdom), smoke16 (wishlist cover), smoke17 (applyCosmetics not called after a pull) and smoke45 (toast announcements). Each passed when re-run alone (2-16 s). The failures are timing assumptions (fixed waits in the tests) rather than product bugs, but they make a parallel runner — the obvious answer to the gate's 20-minute CPU cost — unusable, and they would read as regressions on a slow CI machine. The gate itself is now 1,227 CPU-seconds (450 s wall with three workers); smoke56 (242 s) and smoke75 (236 s) are 39% of it.
- **Evidence:** arch20/gate-summary.txt (exit code, ms, suite; sorted by time); scratchpad logs: smoke4 'STEP anime vault renders + lazy fallback…: Error: no cards rendered' tools/smoke4.test.js:390; smoke17 'applyCosmetics was not called after a remote state applied'; smoke16 TypeError tools/smoke16.test.js:550; serial re-runs all exit 0
- **Root cause:** Tests wait fixed times for async work (IndexedDB, timers) inside jsdom.
- **Proposed fix:** Replace fixed sleeps in those five suites with waits on a condition (poll for the cards, the announcement, the applyCosmetics call); then add a parallel runner (npm test) with a per-suite timeout.
- **Flags:** effort M

## AX — Cross-cutting accessibility and HCI sweep (complete)

**Auditor's summary.** Top-up on kos-redraw-1. All 21 findings from the stale f4fa493 run were re-measured: 19 hold and 2 changed (the Dawn gold Buy now passes, leaving the danger button at 3.14:1; Goals' blank first paint is now about 0.3-0.6 s). None went away. The release's new surfaces (Badge Wall, the Seat as the Stage, Gold Shop, painted art slots, the Assistant redesign) add 25 new findings: 13 from the interrupted first top-up pass and 12 from this one. The main root causes are the same as before. Shared primitives undo the touch and 16px floors (base-layer rules lose to component rules). Status colours are tuned for the dark ground: Dawn and now the light shop themes inherit --red-soft and dark-ground scrims, so overdue dots reach 1.3:1 and text over the painted art 3:1. Dialogs are never tied to the route, so every drawer, sheet and set dialog stays open over the next page. There is still no document title, no haptics, no sound setting, and an inaccessible toast Undo. The new code is mostly careful (decorative art aria-hidden, reduced motion on the unlock overlay, named set panels, 100% visible focus on the Wall and Shop). Its slips are local: an unnamed compact showcase picker, dead Rotate thumbnails, a locked mode that rewrites the rule, double announcements, and a desktop preview shrunk to 28% on the iPhone.

**Coverage.** Inventory and matrix are in audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/findings/a11y-hci.inventory.md. Measured with a11y-scan.js and a11y2-geo.js (names, touch size, ovals, contrast, 16px inputs, overflow, clipping, centring, tiny glyphs) over 24 routes at 1470x832, 820x1180 touch and 402x874 touch on the seeded account (a11y21-*.jsonl), plus the Wall/Seat/Shop/Avatar/Edit/Home routes on an empty account at mac and iphone (a11y21-empty-*.jsonl). The focus-visible sweep (a11y-focus.js) covered Wall, Showcase, Seat, Shop, Avatar and Edit. Screenshots were taken and inspected: Home (Graphite/Dawn/Washi Morning, mac and iphone), the drawer (Rotate and locked Your own), Calendar, Money (Dawn), the CS desk (Dawn), the Exams hero (Graphite/Dawn), Focus (iphone Dawn), the Badge set dialog, the Shop on iphone, the empty Wall and Edit seat on iphone, and the Assistant at ipadl. Contrast over painted art was sampled from pixels. Behaviour was exercised: every drawer mode with the config read back, Hide/Show/Voice focus, Wall routes, set dialog focus and arrows, Calendar Cancel margins, Goals load timing, Help marks, the Assistant chip sizes, and a dialog surviving 7 hash navigations. All 21 carried findings were re-measured or re-read (see recheck). NOT checked: the full tools/responsive_audit.mjs matrix (started; at ~400 cells it needed ~2 h on the shared slot tab, so it was stopped and replaced by the targeted scans); the unlock overlay triggered live (verified in code only); share-card finishes, notebook papers, pen sets and story covers (left for the Reports and ink areas); real VoiceOver and real iOS devices (headless Chrome only; the iOS zoom is inferred from computed font sizes).

> **Build audited:** First run on f4fa493 (sw kos-creatives-1, 23 commits before production). RE-CHECKED on main 6 Nov 2026 (sw kos-redraw-1): every carried-over finding has a 'Re-checked on kos-redraw-1' verdict; the Badge Wall, Seat and shop pages were swept.

### AX-01 · P1 · bug — iPhone: most text fields and selects are under 16px, so iOS Safari zooms the page on every focus

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Independent check:** confirmed; corroboration only, reviewed by Claude 8 Nov
- **Devices:** iPhone
- **Detail / repro:** Invariant 40 promises 16px inputs on the phone, and base.css sets input, select, textarea { font-size: max(16px, 1em) } under max-width 700px. That rule lives in @layer base, which the declared order (tokens, base, layout, components, views, themes) puts BELOW every component and view rule, so any class that sets a font size wins. Measured at 402x874: Assistant composer 14.5px, Reminders quick-add 14px, Focus topic/objective inputs 13.5px, Help search 13px, Files search 13.5px, Backup & Restore e-mail/password 13.5px, Routines settings times 13.5px, Media Sync inputs 13.5px, Assignments subtask input 13px, every .k-pill-select sort/filter (Assignments, Exams & Papers, Shrine, Wishlist, topic page reader select, Card stats retention) 12.5px, Pacing lesson-day selects 12px, vault score corners 14px. On the user's iPhone each of these zooms the viewport when tapped and leaves it zoomed (the layout then scrolls sideways until pinched back). Only the phone search sheet was special-cased (layout.css:457).
- **Evidence:** css/base.css:156-160 (rule inside @layer base); css/tokens.css:35 (@layer tokens, base, layout, components, views, themes); overriding rules e.g. css/components.css:406 .k-input, :417 .k-pill-select font-size var(--fs-12-5), css/views/assistant.css:216 .k-asst-input font-size var(--fs-14-5); measurement audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-iphone.jsonl (font16 lists per view, script a11y-scan.js) | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Re-measured at 402x874 on kos-redraw-1 (a11y21-iphone.jsonl): Assistant composer 14.5px, Focus topic/objective inputs 13.5px, Files search 13.5px, Shrine/Wishlist status selects 12.5px, Seasonal year select 12.5px; the new picture drawer's condition selects are .k-input--sm too (js/modules/artslot.js:69). css/base.css:156-160 still sits in @layer base.
- **Root cause:** Cascade-layer order: a base-layer guard cannot override component-layer declarations.
- **Proposed fix:** Move the phone 16px rule to the last layer (themes, or an unlayered rule at the end of components.css) so it wins: @media (max-width:700px){ input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]):not([type=range]), select, textarea, [contenteditable] { font-size: max(16px, 1em) !important } } — or set --fs-input tokens that components read. Add a smoke check that no visible field computes under 16px at 402px.
- **Flags:** effort S

### AX-02 · P2 · a11y — Undo in toasts cannot be reached by keyboard or screen reader

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** The one Undo route for Daily Review triage (Tomorrow, Done, Study block) and Reminders' 'ticked in your plan' is a button inside #toast. #toast is aria-hidden="true" and the button is created with tabindex=-1, so it is out of the tab order and hidden from assistive tech; the announced sentence ('<title> · moved to tomorrow') never mentions Undo. The toast disappears after 8 s with no pause on hover/focus (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.2.1 Timing). A keyboard or VoiceOver user has no undo for these actions.
- **Evidence:** js/core/ui.js:72-87 (tabindex '-1' at :76, 8000 ms timer :81, announce(msg) without the action); index.html:140 (#toast aria-hidden=true); callers js/modules/dayreview.js:534,615,621,622, js/modules/reminders.js:344 | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Re-read js/core/ui.js:72-87 (tabindex -1, 8000 ms, announce(msg) only) and index.html:141 (#toast aria-hidden=true).
- **Root cause:** #toast was made purely visual in Phase F; the later action variant reused it without restoring access.
- **Proposed fix:** Give action toasts a focusable, named Undo: drop tabindex=-1 and aria-hidden on the action toast (or render action toasts in a non-hidden region), announce 'msg. Undo available (Ctrl/Cmd+Z)', pause the timer on hover/focus, and add a global Cmd/Ctrl+Z that runs the latest toast action.
- **Flags:** effort S

### AX-03 · P2 · ux — Focus chime is silent on iPhone/iPad and has no on/off or volume setting

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** iPhone, iPad (silent); all (no control)
- **Detail / repro:** The only sound in the app (Pomodoro cycle end, break end, stopwatch break nudge) is a Web Audio oscillator whose AudioContext is created lazily inside the timer tick, never from a user gesture and never resume()d. WebKit starts such a context 'suspended', so on the user's iPhone and iPad the chime never plays; the cue is then only a 2.6 s toast that a user away from the screen will miss. There is also no setting anywhere to turn the chime off, choose a sound or set its volume (grep finds no Sound/Chime control). Japanese voice lines and the Assistant's speech are the only other audio.
- **Evidence:** js/modules/focus.js:788-801 (chime(): new AC() on first call from tick, no ctx.resume()); call sites :496, :508, :522 inside the interval tick; grep -rniE '"(Sound|Chime)' js/modules js/core → none | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): js/modules/focus.js:788-800 unchanged: AudioContext created lazily at chime time with no unlock on a gesture and no setting.
- **Root cause:** Audio unlock rules of iOS WebKit not handled; no audio preference model.
- **Proposed fix:** Create/resume the AudioContext in Start's click handler (unlock it), call ctx.resume() before each chime, and add a Focus setting 'Sound at cycle end' (on/off + volume, per device in state.ui). Also send a device notification for cycle end when the page is hidden.
- **Flags:** effort S

### AX-04 · P2 · a11y — Status chips fail AA contrast app-wide (3.5–4.3:1 at 11.5px), worst in Atelier Dawn

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** Every .k-chip paints its text in the role colour on an 18% wash of the same colour. The wash darkens/lightens the ground towards the text, so the role colours that pass on the page (4.5–5.8:1, computed from the tokens) drop below 4.5:1 on their own chip. Measured on the seeded account (Mac, real theme via KOS.governor.setTheme): Dawn — Assignments 'Overdue' 3.68, vault 'In progress' 3.52–3.62, Wishlist '◆ Priority purchase' 3.36, '#urgent' 4.02, 'Medium' 4.04, '23 behind' 4.04, Governor '● All systems open' 3.96; Graphite — 'Overdue' 3.93, 'Coursework / NEA' 4.28, 'Not enough evidence' 3.94, 'recall 94%' 3.94, 'Too early to call' 3.94. These are the app's most decision-relevant labels (overdue, at risk) and are 11.5px, regular weight.
- **Evidence:** css/components.css:191-199 (.k-chip: color var(--chip-c); background color-mix(var(--chip-c) 18%, transparent)); scan output audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-mac-dawn2.jsonl and a11y-mac.jsonl (script audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-scan.js); token ratios computed: Dawn --red on --s1 5.78, on its own wash 3.68 | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Graphite, seeded, this build: k-chip 'Free' (Gold Shop) 3.94, '○ Not enough evidence' 3.94, goal.pace '◌ Too early to call' 3.94, 'In progress' 4.35, 'Gemini · auto' 4.28, '◆ Priority purchase' 4.23 (all 11.5px); Dawn Home day dot '5' 3.42 @14px.
- **Root cause:** Chip ink is the same role token as its wash; tokens were tuned for page ground, not for the tinted chip.
- **Proposed fix:** Give chips an ink variant per role: text = oklch(from var(--chip-c) calc(l - 0.12) c h) in Dawn (calc(l + 0.08) in dark themes), or keep the role colour for a dot and set the label in --text-2. Add a smoke check that every [data-tone] chip ≥ 4.5:1 in Graphite and Dawn.
- **Flags:** effort S

### AX-05 · P2 · a11y — Touch-size floor is undone by shared primitives: pill selects 30px, switches 34x20, checkboxes 18x18 on iPad and iPhone

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** iPad, iPhone
- **Detail / repro:** base.css gives every button/select/text input a 44px min-height under (pointer: coarse), but with zero specificity, and several SHARED primitives cancel or bypass it, so the same defect shows up on every page (other areas reported page instances; this is the common root cause). Measured on iPad (820x1180, touch) and iPhone: .k-pill-select 30px tall everywhere it is used (Assignments filters, Exams & Papers, Shrine/Wishlist/vault sort, topic reader select, Card stats); .k-switch 34x20 (Notifications ×5, Pen and ink ×4, Storage, Routines settings ×10, Focus 'Penalise tab-switches', Media Sync auto, Exams season/quiet); native checkboxes 18x18 (Pacing lesson ticks, Wishlist plan.check, tracker k-box, Files ink filter, Home habit tick input); the rail collapse toggle 24x24; scroller arrows 32x32; Reports Share/Export 32px; Card stats retention inputs 30px.
- **Evidence:** css/base.css:115-121 (:where(...) floor; no input[type=checkbox], no .k-switch); css/components.css:417 (.k-pill-select { min-block-size: 0 } cancels it); css/components.css:207 (.k-switch fixed --fx-switch-w/h, not in the coarse block at :669-677); css/layout.css:233-235 (.k-rail-toggle at --hit-dense); measurements audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/a11y-ipad.jsonl, a11y-iphone.jsonl | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): Under touch at 820x1180 and 402x874: switches still 34x20 on the new Avatar & profile page (gov.theme-follow, gov.art-on, gov.art-reduced), the Wall's List view, Focus penalty, Pen and ink, Exams; Seasonal year select 96x31; the Assistant's Pin/Hide/Voice chips 21px tall (see the Assistant finding).
- **Root cause:** The floor is a zero-specificity base rule; primitives set their own sizes after it.
- **Proposed fix:** In the components coarse block add: .k-pill-select { min-block-size: var(--hit-coarse) }; .k-switch { scale or an inset ::before hit area to 44x44 } (keep the visual 34x20 but pad the label/row); input[type=checkbox]:not(.k-switch) { inline-size/block-size 24px plus a 44px label hit area }; remove min-block-size:0 from .k-pill-select. A smoke check over every view at pointer:coarse for interactive boxes < 44px would stop the regressions.
- **Flags:** effort M

### AX-07 · P2 · bug — Backspace on any focused button navigates Back, even inside an open dialog, leaving the dialog over a different page

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** Mac, iPad with keyboard
- **Detail / repro:** main.js treats a bare Backspace outside text fields as 'Back'. Keyboard users routinely have focus on a button (after clicking Cancel/Done/a rating, or tabbing), so a stray Backspace — e.g. meant to correct a field they thought was focused — leaves the page. The handler does not check for an open dialog: reproduced on the Calendar's New event modal with focus on Cancel; Backspace changed the route #/calendar → #/home and the modal stayed open, kicker 'Calendar', floating over Home. Browsers removed Backspace-as-Back for exactly this data-loss reason; Help & Guide does not list it (it lists Alt ← / →).
- **Evidence:** js/main.js:20-29 (keydown: !typing && key === 'Backspace' → KOS.back(), no dialog/overlay check); repro via eval: before '#/calendar', after '#/home', dialogStill true; shots/a11y-hci/backspace-under-dialog-mac.png; js/modules/help.js:299 shortcut list | Re-check 6 Nov 2026 (kos-redraw-1): js/main.js:24 unchanged (Backspace outside inputs = Back, no dialog check). The general case (any navigation leaves a dialog open) is now its own finding.
- **Root cause:** Global shortcut written before dialogs were overlays rendered outside the router's control.
- **Proposed fix:** Drop the bare Backspace binding (keep Alt+←/→ and the buttons), or at least ignore it when a [role=dialog][aria-modal=true], the Focus overlay, a review sheet or the Exam Room is open and when focus is inside #main controls.
- **Flags:** effort S

### AX-08 · P2 · a11y — The document title never changes: every page is 'Kurenai OS — Study Atelier'

- **Re-checked on kos-redraw-1:** holds
- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** No view sets document.title; only Focus writes it (the countdown, then back to the default). So the browser tab, the history list (long-press Back, Mac History menu), Mac window/tab switcher, bookmarks, and screen-reader page announcements all read the same name on Home, a topic, Money or a vault (WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled). The router already knows the view and its label (KOS.currentNav), and the phone title bar computes the page title.

- **Proposed fix:** In router.js after each KOS.show, set document.title = '<page h1 or nav label> · <section> — KurenaiOS' (topic: '<ref> <title> · CS'); Focus keeps prefixing the remaining time.

### AX-22 · P2 · ux — Edit your seat throws away unsaved changes on any navigation, with no prompt

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** On #/governor/edit, picking showcase badges, a background, a title or a sigil marks Save as lit (dirty()), but leaving by the rail, Back, Backspace, the bell or search discards the draft silently. There is no leave guard anywhere in the router (no beforeLeave / canLeave hook), so the only protection is remembering to press Save. CLAUDE.md lists the 'leave-with-changes prompt' as not built; this records the user-visible effect.

- **Root cause:** No navigation-guard primitive exists; the editor keeps its draft in a closure.
- **Proposed fix:** Add a small router hook (KOS.router.guard(fn)) that a view can set while dirty; on navigation ask 'Leave without saving? Keep editing / Discard' (Cancel-first, invariant 49), and clear it on Save/Discard.

### AX-23 · P2 · ux — Buy in the Gold Shop spends gold on one tap with no confirm and no undo

### AX-24 · P2 · bug — The Wall's tabs and set links have no URL: #/achievements/recent, /titles, /showcase and /set/<id> all open Sets

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** CLAUDE.md documents #/achievements[/sets|recent|showcase|titles|set/<id>], and the view parses its arg (achievements.js:110-113), but js/core/router.js has no ENCODE/DECODE entry for 'achievements'. So KOS.show('achievements','titles') writes '#/achievements', a reload or a shared link to #/achievements/titles or #/achievements/set/streaks opens Sets with no dialog, and Back from a set dialog opened by 'View on the Wall' does not return to the tab you were on. Every tab switch is also not a history entry the way the Governor's tabs are.

- **Root cause:** The view was added with an argument but not registered in the router's route table.

### AX-25 · P2 · perf — The Wall, the Seat's showcase and Edit your seat wait 7-12 s on a dense account because every open re-measures all 254 badges

- **Devices:** all, worst on iPhone
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.achievements.list() measures every badge afresh on each call (no cache between the boot/30-minute sweep and the pages). On the seeded account (1,880 media rows) one call took 6.9-7.9 s, the Collection set alone 5.1 s; the Wall body shows 'Reading your records…' for 12.5 s after navigation, the Seat's arc stays six empty rings with no label for ~12.9 s and Edit your seat says 'Reading your badges…'. Measured on a loaded machine (load average ~7.3 from parallel audit slots), so absolute times on the M4 will be lower, but the work is the same on every visit and on every phone tab switch.
- **Evidence:** eval timings: list() 7867/920/7452 ms; per set: collection 5127, exams 1473, mind 1158, study 983, ALL 6954 ms; Wall body ready 12512 ms; Seat note after 12867 ms; js/core/achievements.js:329-341 (list → measureOne per DEF each call); shots/a11y-hci/t-wall-iphone.png ('Reading your records…'), t-seat-ipad.png (empty arc)
- **Root cause:** list() and evaluate() share measureOne with no memo; Collection badges scan the vault.
- **Proposed fix:** Cache the last sweep's views (value, p, tier) keyed by domain and invalidate on touch(domains); list() returns the cache at once and refreshes in the background. Make the Collection measures read counts from the media index instead of scanning rows.
- **Flags:** effort M

### AX-26 · P2 · ui — iPhone: the Seat's empty showcase draws six squashed ovals until (or unless) its note arrives

- **Devices:** iPhone
- **Detail / repro:** At 402px the arc becomes a nowrap flex row of six 44px slots plus the note div (flex-basis 100%). While the note is empty — the ~8-12 s before list() answers, and permanently when no badge is earned or near (a new account) — the note takes the row and the six empty slots shrink to ~26x50 ovals. Only once the note has text does :has(.k-gv-arc-note:not(:empty)) turn on wrapping and the rings become 44x44 circles.
- **Evidence:** shots/a11y-hci/t-seat-iphone.png (six ovals under the XP bar); eval after the note loaded: slots 44x44, .k-gv-arc display flex height 92; css/views/governor.css:518-523 (flex, no wrap until :has(note:not(:empty)), slot without flex: none)
- **Root cause:** Flex items shrink by default; wrap depends on the async note.

### AX-27 · P2 · bug — A badge set dialog opens over whatever page you moved to, seconds after leaving the Wall

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.show('achievements', 'set/<id>/<badge>') — what the unlock overlay's 'View on the Wall' and a ping click do — renders the Wall and opens the set dialog only when list() answers (8-12 s on a dense account). If you leave in the meantime, the stale callback still runs: its guard `if (!body.isConnected && body.parentNode == null) return;` passes because the detached body still has its root as parent, so the Wall is drawn into a detached node and openSetDialog() appends a modal over the new page (Money in the repro), stealing focus.
- **Evidence:** eval: KOS.show('achievements','set/focus'); after 1 s KOS.show('money') → .k-ach-dlg 'Focus' appeared over #/money 8022 ms later; shots/a11y-hci/t-setdlg-over-money-mac.png; js/modules/achievements.js:126-135 (guard and openSetDialog in the async callback), :647 and :715 (callers)
- **Root cause:** Wrong staleness test in the async list() callback.
- **Proposed fix:** Guard on body.isConnected alone (or a render token compared with KOS.current) before drawing and before openSetDialog.
- **Flags:** effort S

### AX-38 · P2 · bug — No dialog closes on navigation: the router leaves every open dialog, drawer and sheet over the next page

- **Devices:** all
- **Detail / repro:** KOS.ui.openDialog keeps a dialog stack but neither router.js nor KOS.show ever closes it, so any navigation while a dialog is open (browser Back/Forward, the iPad edge-swipe, a hash link, Backspace, a notification click, KOS.show from a timer) draws the new page under the old dialog, with the scroll lock still set. Reproduced: opened the picture drawer on Home (KOS.artSlot.open), then changed location.hash through #/files, #/reminders, #/calendar, #/goals, #/help and #/assistant: the Home hero drawer was still open over the Assistant (one .k-dialog-overlay, data-scroll-lock set). Several areas report the per-surface symptom (Creatives work dialog, Mind sheets, Money phone sheet, Badge set dialog, Backspace under a dialog); this is the shared root cause.
- **Evidence:** shots/a11y-hci/n-asst-ipadl.png (Home's hero drawer over the Assistant at 1180x820); eval: .k-dialog-overlay count 1, data-scroll-lock present after 7 hash changes; js/core/ui.js:155-240 (openDialog/dialogStack, no navigation hook); js/core/router.js (no dialog handling)
- **Root cause:** Dialog lifetime is not tied to the route; each surface assumed the user leaves only via its own buttons.
- **Proposed fix:** In the router's navigation path (before rendering a different view, not on KOS.rerender), close every dialog on the stack via its own close path (teardown runs onClose), or let a dialog opt in to staying ({keepOnNav}).
- **Flags:** effort S
